title: Honour OS-level prefers-reduced-motion when choosing beacon motion
description:
Oculist honours its own motionSensitivity setting (visionSettings.motionSensitivity: full | reduced | off) but never checks the OS-level prefers-reduced-motion media query. A user who has asked their operating system to reduce motion still gets full beacon animations unless they separately find and change the extension setting.

Original scope also covered capping flash opacity on the Impact Burst / Speed Lines effects; those effects were reverted in 2554612 and 1b9f7de, so that half no longer applies (see closed oculist-kd7).

Remaining work: treat window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') as a downgrade-only signal on the motion mode read in content.js — drawActiveOverlays() (~1567) and animate() (~1607) both compute the same value. When the OS asks for reduced motion, 'full' becomes 'reduced'; an explicit 'reduced' or 'off' is left alone, so the setting can only ever reduce motion further, never override the OS upward. Must react to the media query changing at runtime, not just at load.
close_reason: Implemented in 0f89a22 on branch v1.6.0. Shared effectiveMotion() in extension/content.js downgrades 'full' to 'reduced' when matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') matches; explicit 'reduced'/'off' untouched. Regression test test/prefers_reduced_motion.test.js flips the emulated preference at runtime and asserts the beacon part count drops and restores; verified it fails without the fix. Full suite: 22/22 pass.

title: Add 4 impact-frame candidates (Round 4) to effects-playground.html
description:
CORRECTION to original brief: artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html already exists (predates this epic) as a living gallery of 22 candidate beacon effects across 'Round 1/2/3', built specifically for this kind of side-by-side prototyping. Do NOT create a new file or a new grid/card layout — extend this existing file with a new 'Round 4' of 4 additional candidates, following its established conventions exactly.

Existing conventions to match (read the file first, don't guess):
- Effects are `function fxName(r) { ... }`, where `r` is the single shared `#match` element's rect (one real article, one real `<mark id="match">`, not per-candidate cards).
- Elements you create get `className` including `'fx'` (see existing fx* functions for the exact pattern) and are mounted via the existing `mount(el)` helper (appends to document.documentElement).
- Only one effect is 'live' at a time: `window.runEffect(key)` calls `clearFx()` first (removes all `.fx` nodes and drains any registered restorers), then `eff.run(rect())`. Don't fight this — build your 4 effects to be self-cleaning within their own duration like the existing ones (most use a `setTimeout` to remove their own elements), the `clearFx()` safety net is for rapid re-trigger, not your primary cleanup path.
- If an effect temporarily mutates page state outside its own new elements (e.g. body transform, mark text color), capture prior state and register a restorer via `addRestorer(fn)`, following the `captureStyleAttr`/`restoreStyleAttr` pattern already in the file (search for `addRestorer` usage in an existing effect, e.g. fxGravity or fxZoompunch, for a concrete example). Prefer NOT mutating page-wide state at all if your effect doesn't need to — simpler is fine here.
- Naming convention: function `fxCapitalizedsquashedname` (e.g. `fxZoompunch`, `fxDepthdive`, `fxMatchstrike` — capitalize only the first letter, rest of the compound name is lowercase, no inner camelCase), registry key is the same name lowercased with no prefix (e.g. `zoompunch`, `depthdive`).
- Registration: add 4 new entries to the `effectsRegistry` object (around line 1514) AFTER the existing 22, in the same `{ label: '...', run: fxWhatever }` shape.
- Sidebar grouping: `buildSidebar()` currently slices `window.EFFECTS` into round1 (first 10, no divider), round2 (next 5, 'Round 2' divider), round3 (remainder, 'Round 3' divider). Add a 'Round 4' divider for your 4 new entries — extend the slicing logic (e.g. `window.EFFECTS.slice(15, 19)` for round3 and `.slice(19)` for a new round4, or whatever indices are correct given the final registry order) and call `addDivider('Round 4', round4)` after the existing `addDivider('Round 3', round3)` call. Do not change how rounds 1-3 are computed/labeled.
- Use the `Z` constant (2147483645) for any z-index, matching every existing effect.
- No autoplay on load — effects only fire via sidebar button click or the 'Replay last' button, exactly like the existing 22. Do not add a load-time autoplay for your 4.

Design intent (why these 4, and why they should look distinct from a generic 'glowing highlight'): these are 'impact frame' candidates, inspired by anime/manga impact-frame conventions — hard, SHORT, high-contrast hits rather than smooth glowing animations. Aim for roughly 150-350ms total runtime per effect (a handful of anime frames), near-instant snaps rather than long eased curves, and flat/hard-edged shapes (solid fills, bold outlines) rather than soft blurred gradients. This is a deliberate contrast with most of the existing 22 effects, which tend to be smoother/longer — that contrast is the point of this round.

Build these 4:
1. **Impact Burst** (`fxImpactburst` / key `impactburst`) — hard white flash (~60-80ms) + a flat-color jagged star/burst shape centered on the match that snaps to full size almost instantly and cuts off abruptly (no long fade).
2. **Speed Lines** (`fxSpeedlines` / key `speedlines`) — flat-color (not gradient) straight lines radiating from the match at evenly-spaced angles, snapping to full length fast, hard cutoff.
3. **Shatter Crack** (`fxShattercrack` / key `shattercrack`) — 8-14 jagged 2-segment 'crack' lines at randomized angles/lengths radiating from the match (mimicking a glass-crack impact), plus a quick flash. Each 'crack' = two short connected line segments at a slight angle offset, not a single straight line (that's what makes it read as a crack rather than a ray).
4. **Hard Freeze Flash** (`fxHardfreeze` / key `hardfreeze`) — the most literal 'impact frame': a near-full-opacity flash across the viewport for ~2-3 frames (~80-120ms), plus a bold angular outline that snaps around the match at the same instant. Prefer `steps()` or a very short easing over long cubic-bezier curves.

Verification (no test suite exists for this file — it's a prototype):
- Open the file in a browser (this repo's playwright devDependency works fine for a scripted check) and click each of the 4 new sidebar buttons; confirm zero console errors, each effect visibly fires near the match, and `.fx` node count returns to its pre-fire baseline within ~1s of each firing (no leaks).
- Confirm the existing 22 effects and their Round 1/2/3 grouping are untouched and still work (spot-check a couple, e.g. click 'Sonar Ping' and 'Ink Bloom').
- No changes to any file outside artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html.
acceptance_criteria: 4 new effects (impactburst, speedlines, shattercrack, hardfreeze) registered in effectsRegistry and grouped under a new 'Round 4' sidebar divider; each fires via its sidebar button with zero console errors and self-cleans its .fx nodes within ~1s; existing 22 effects and Round 1/2/3 grouping unaffected; no changes outside effects-playground.html
close_reason: Round 4 (Impact Burst, Speed Lines, Shatter Crack, Hard Freeze Flash) added to effects-playground.html; reviewer-verified after 2 rounds of fixes (options-level steps() misuse, burst-point clamping, keyframe fade-back artifact). No changes outside the playground file.

title: Add 'Speed Lines' effect (manga radiating focus lines + hitstop)
description:
Add a new beacon effect to repo/extension/content.js mimicking manga/anime 'speed lines' (a.k.a. focus lines): straight lines radiating from the impact point across a wide radius, evoking the classic manga panel technique used at a moment of impact, combined with a brief hitstop flash.

Steps:
1. In the `i18n` object (content.js:118-178), add `effectSpeedLines: 'Speed Lines'` near the other `effect*` keys.
2. Write `function animateSpeedLines(rect) { ... }`, placed near the other `animate*` effect functions. Guard clause first: `if (!rect || rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;`.
3. Visual composition, `position:fixed` (viewport-anchored, same convention as `animateIris` at content.js:466):
   a. A brief hitstop flash: full-viewport white overlay, opacity spikes 0 -> ~0.5 -> 0 fast (~100-150ms), lower peak opacity than a full flash effect since the lines carry most of the visual weight here.
   b. 12-20 thin straight lines radiating outward from the match center at evenly distributed angles (`360 / count` degrees apart), each a rotated absolutely-positioned div (`width: 1-3px scaled by getBeaconScale()`, long length e.g. 40-60% of viewport diagonal, `transform-origin` at the near end so it grows outward from the match like a manga speed line). Animate each line's length via `transform: scaleX(0) -> scaleX(1) -> scaleX(0.3)` (grows fast, recedes) with a fast easing, staggered fade-out.
   c. Color: use `getEffectiveColors().beacon` for the lines (see note below on accessibility), optionally blended with white near the origin for a 'hot core' look, consistent with how `animateAnimeLaser` mixes accent color + white (content.js:380-400).
4. Every created element must have `className = 'oc-beacon'`.
5. Color must come from `getEffectiveColors().beacon` as the primary driver, not hardcoded black/white-only — this project's Vision Accessibility Suite depends on every effect reflecting the user's active beacon color for color-blind palette support, so don't design a monochrome-only variant even though real manga speed lines are typically black ink on white.
6. Scale line length/width/count by `getBeaconScale()`; reduce line count under `settings.performanceMode` (Lite Mode), same pattern as `animateAnimeLaser`'s `sparkCount` (content.js:428).
7. Append all elements to `document.documentElement` once at the end, not incrementally.
8. Clean up: `setTimeout` to `.remove()` every element, timed via `getBeaconDuration(totalMs + 100)`.
9. Register in `effectsRegistry` (content.js:215-223): add `speedlines: { label: i18n.effectSpeedLines, run: animateSpeedLines },`. Do not reorder or touch other entries.
10. Do not modify any other effect function, i18n locale files, or build.js.

Edge cases:
- Zero-size rect must no-op.
- Keep this visually distinct from the sibling 'Impact Burst' task (star-shaped burst) — this effect is straight uniform radiating lines, not a star polygon. If both tasks land, they should not look like near-duplicates.
- No new npm dependencies.

Acceptance criteria (done-criteria for review):
- `npm test` passes unchanged, including test/settings_panel.test.js's alphabetical-order and effect-existence assertions.
- 'Speed Lines' appears as a selectable radio option in the Settings panel's Highlight Effect list.
- Triggering the effect creates only `.oc-beacon`-classed nodes, all removed from the DOM within ~2s of firing.
- No files changed outside repo/extension/content.js.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes; 'Speed Lines' selectable in settings panel; effect fires without throwing on a zero-size rect (no-op) and a real rect (creates+removes only .oc-beacon nodes); visually distinct from the Impact Burst star shape; no files changed outside repo/extension/content.js
close_reason: Implemented and reviewer-verified: Speed Lines effect added to effectsRegistry, all tests pass, no DOM leaks, visually distinct from Impact Burst.

title: Add 'Impact Burst' effect (comic star-burst impact frame)
description:
Add a new beacon effect to repo/extension/content.js that mimics an anime/manga 'impact frame': a hard white flash + a jagged comic-style star burst snapping onto the active match, evoking a punch/hit moment (reference: anime impact frames — hard cut to white/flash, sharp radiating burst shape, brief hitstop, then release).

Steps:
1. In the `i18n` object (content.js:118-178), add `effectImpactBurst: 'Impact Burst'` alongside the other `effect*` keys (near line 177).
2. Write `function animateImpactBurst(rect) { ... }` placed near the other `animate*` effect functions (e.g. after `animateAnimeLaser` at content.js:324 or `animateIris` at content.js:466 — follow whichever sibling function's structure is closest). Guard clause first: `if (!rect || rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;` (copy this exact pattern from animateAnimeLaser).
3. Visual composition (three layered elements, all `position:fixed` since the effect is viewport-anchored on the match, same convention as `animateIris`):
   a. A brief full-viewport white flash overlay (inset 0) that spikes opacity 0 -> ~0.85 -> 0 very fast (~100-150ms total) to simulate a 'hitstop' flash-cut. Use `getBeaconDuration(...)` for all durations, never a raw literal.
   b. A jagged star-burst shape centered on `rect` (use `clip-path: polygon(...)` with 8-12 alternating long/short points to fake a comic impact star), filled with `getEffectiveColors().beacon`, sized relative to `rect` and `getBeaconScale()`. Animate transform scale with an overshoot easing (e.g. `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)`) so it 'snaps' in rather than eases smoothly — 0.2 -> 1.3 -> 1, then fades.
   c. 6-10 short radiating spike lines around the match (thin rotated divs, angle evenly distributed like a starburst), colored with `getEffectiveColors().beacon`, scaling outward and fading — reuse the randomized-placement-loop pattern from the spark generation in `animateAnimeLaser` (content.js:428-456) for consistency, but evenly spaced angles instead of random (bursts read as more 'impact', sparks read as more 'explosion').
4. Every created element must have `className = 'oc-beacon'` (required for the extension's cleanup/resize/DOM-scan logic — grep `.oc-beacon` usage in content.js to confirm all touchpoints before finishing).
5. Color: primary visual color must come from `getEffectiveColors().beacon`, not a hardcoded black/white-only palette — this project has a Vision Accessibility Suite with color-blind palettes that depend on every effect surfacing the user's active beacon color, so don't design an effect that reads correctly only in one color scheme. White is fine for flash/highlight accents (other effects mix white + accent color), just not as the *only* color.
6. Scale all counts/sizes by `getBeaconScale()`, and downscale element/spike counts under `settings.performanceMode` (Lite Mode), same as `animateAnimeLaser`'s `sparkCount` logic (content.js:428).
7. Append all elements to `document.documentElement` once at the end (not incrementally) to avoid layout thrashing, per the existing comment convention in `animateAnimeLaser`.
8. Clean up: `setTimeout` to `.remove()` every element created by this effect, timed via `getBeaconDuration(totalMs + 100)`, mirroring `animateIris`'s multi-element cleanup (content.js:521-524).
9. Register in `effectsRegistry` (content.js:215-223): add `burst: { label: i18n.effectImpactBurst, run: animateImpactBurst },`. Do not reorder or touch the other 7 entries.
10. Do not modify any other effect function, the settings-panel sort logic, i18n locale files, or build.js.

Edge cases:
- Zero-size rect must no-op (return early), same as all sibling effects.
- Must not throw if called back-to-back rapidly (user pressing next-match fast) — rely on the same fire-and-forget DOM node pattern the other effects use; do not add any global mutable state beyond what's local to the function call.
- No new npm dependencies.

Acceptance criteria (done-criteria for review):
- `npm test` (repo/package.json → `node --test test/*.test.js`) passes unchanged, including test/settings_panel.test.js's alphabetical-label-order assertion and existing effect-existence assertions.
- 'Impact Burst' appears as a selectable radio option in the Settings panel's Highlight Effect list (auto-sorted alphabetically by the existing code — no manual sort-order edit needed).
- Manually triggering the effect (e.g. via the extension's find bar on a page, or a quick jsdom/script smoke check) creates only `.oc-beacon`-classed nodes, all of which are removed from the DOM within ~2s of firing (no leaked nodes).
- No changes outside `repo/extension/content.js`.
acceptance_criteria: npm test passes; 'Impact Burst' selectable in settings panel; effect fires without throwing on a zero-size rect (no-op) and on a real rect (creates+removes only .oc-beacon nodes); no files changed outside repo/extension/content.js
close_reason: Implemented and reviewer-verified: Impact Burst effect added to effectsRegistry, all tests pass, no DOM leaks.

title: fxEdgeticks has a real edge-clamp occlusion the 96-grid could never see
description:
Found by the oculist-1ta.26 reviewer, 2026-09-12, while measuring that bead's blast radius across all 47 keys.

THE FINDING. fxEdgeticks is 96/96 clean in the existing grid, yet DIRTY 8 of 8 in the new EDGE-PLACEMENT block at maxPixels=14. That is a genuine edge-clamp occlusion, previously unrecorded, and exactly the class oculist-1ta.26 was built to expose.

Reproduce: node occlusion-sweep.js edgeticks in artifacts/prototypes/. The edge block runs after the grid and forced blocks.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY. It does not change the gate. edgeticks is already red from its FORCED-LANDING block (0/4 clean, maxPixels=334 at HEAD), so the run already exits 1. But that pre-existing red is a different defect, and fixing the forced-block one would leave this edge defect as the sole remaining reason the key is red. Someone fixing the forced defect and expecting green would otherwise be surprised.

14px is small. Judge whether it is worth fixing before fixing it: check whether any of it is glyph ink, the way the oculist-1ta.6 review did for wandcast, where 35px included 1px of ink. A handful of pixels on the match's own background may be acceptable; ink on the glyphs is not.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The 14px is characterised: which element paints it, at what edge and viewport, and whether any is glyph ink.
- Either it is fixed and edgeticks goes 8/8 clean in the edge block, or the reason for accepting it is recorded in the source next to the clamp.
- The forced-landing defect is NOT in scope here; do not fix both under this bead without saying so.

title: arrowshot-fallback-check's grid cannot kill a regression of the playground's own newlyBackward guard: add a seeded random mode
description:
Found by the oculist-201u reviewer, 2026-09-12, while verifying that bead's new metric.

THE FINDING. The reviewer mutated the PLAYGROUND's own production guard, dropping the newlyBackward term from takeCandidate at effects-playground.html:4728, so the guard that stops the chooser accepting a candidate which reverses a flight is gone:

  takeCandidate = flightClearCand >= flightClearBase && !newlyBackward
  becomes
  takeCandidate = flightClearCand >= flightClearBase

arrowshot-fallback-check.js's output against that mutant is BIT-IDENTICAL to unmutated: still PASS, same instrument counts. The mutant survives. A control mutant (takeCandidate = false) does shift the counts, bareSign 2088 to 727, which proves the candidate branch is exercised and the survival is not a harness plumbing problem. The grid simply never reaches a geometry where accepting the candidate would BOTH improve flight clearance AND reverse the flight.

WHY IT MATTERS. oculist-201u made newlyBackward the check's authoritative reversal metric, and it is correct by construction: verified against the pre-change source, against two independent mutants that move only the launch point, and shown to have a load-bearing forward-before gate. This is not a defect in that metric. It is that the checked-in script's 9034-geometry deterministic grid is too coarse to exercise the one production guard the metric mirrors, so the durable guard cannot currently fail if that guard is removed.

The bead oculist-201u cites 1.83M grid and 400k random geometries, but those came from the original reviewer's separate scratch tooling. This script has no random mode at all: grep confirms no random generator in the file.

STEPS

1. Add a seeded random mode to artifacts/prototypes/arrowshot-fallback-check.js, something like --random N --seed S. Seeded so a failure is reproducible; a random check nobody can re-run is worse than no check.
2. Confirm it holds all four safety counts at 0 on the current playground, at a sample size large enough to be meaningful.
3. The acceptance test is the mutant above, not the sample size: with the newlyBackward term dropped from takeCandidate at effects-playground.html:4728, the check must FAIL and exit 1. If it still passes, the sampling is not reaching the geometry class and N is not the answer.
4. Keep the deterministic grid as the default. Random mode is an addition, not a replacement, so the fast path stays fast and reproducible.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Seeded random mode exists and is documented in the file header.
- Current playground: 0 violations under both grid and random.
- The dropped-guard mutant fails the check and exits 1.
- Default invocation behaviour and runtime are unchanged.
close_reason: H-select-reversal pinned as a named deterministic case, so the dropped-guard mutant now fails at the DEFAULT invocation (9035 fallback, newlyBackward=1, exit 1); clean playground passes at 9035, runtime unchanged ~32s. Seeded random mode added as an exploratory sampler but explicitly NOT the guard: a first attempt made it the guard and failed review (3/8 seeds caught it, default seed 1 missed even at N=200000 after 415s). Reviewer PASS after one retry, with attribution proof: HEAD's pre-change script against the same mutant still passes, so the kill comes from this diff. Also corrected two errors in the reachability documentation. Commit 29ad961 on goal/p3-cleanup in the workspace repo. Noted non-blocking: one cosmetic imprecision remains in the 'left' aside (when launchX < leftEndX < launchX + STRIKE_GAP the floor is leftEndX), but the invariant it concludes holds in both arms.

title: prefire-scroll-abort-check success-path fires don't clear .fx before checking, letting a leftover node from a preceding sub-case mask a real regression
description: runNormalFireOnce, runFalsePositiveSubcase, and runPaddingMarginNormalCase in artifacts/prototypes/prefire-scroll-abort-check.js assert only document.querySelectorAll('.fx').length > 0, with no clearFx-equivalent step before firing (unlike runAbortSubcase, which explicitly removes leftover .fx first). Observed via the oculist-1raa poll-based rewrite: several rows report an anomalously fast settle+mount time (17-40ms, vs. the real ~530-630ms observed elsewhere), consistent with the check picking up a still-mounted .fx from the immediately preceding sub-case rather than the current fire's own effect. This predates oculist-1raa (the old fixed 700/900ms sleep-then-single-read had the same gap, just silently) and was not fixed under that timing-only bead. If a genuine regression stopped a real fire from drawing at exactly the moment a preceding case's effect was still mounted, the assertion would falsely pass. Fix direction: clear .fx (or otherwise isolate state) before each success-path fire, same as the abort path already does.
close_reason: Folded into oculist-1raa and fixed there. clearFx(page) helper now called before every fire in runNormalFireOnce and runFalsePositiveSubcase; runAbortSubcase's inline clear refactored to the same helper with its original ordering preserved. Reviewer confirmed clear ordering correct at all three sites. Commit 60740fc. Note runMatchstrikeFullLifecycle still has no clear, but asserts peak >= 10 which stale nodes cannot fake; left as pre-existing and out of scope.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Folded into oculist-1raa rather than worked separately. The oculist-1raa reviewer established this is not adjacent to 1raa but load-bearing for it: 1raa's new bounded wait exits on '.fx count > 0', so the missing clear on the success paths lets a previous case's surviving nodes satisfy the wait immediately. Measured: 14 of 20 B.3 iterations returned in under 100ms with staleAtExit=3, freshAtExit=0. Fixing the clear is what makes 1raa's exit predicate sound, so it is being done inside 1raa. Close this against that work.

title: fxArrowShot's crown HI wedge is a 0-pure-pixel construction at archerH 78: keep it, resize it, or drop it
description:
Discovered while closing oculist-uxa0, which corrected the comment but was explicitly scoped to comment-only and left the geometry alone.

THE FINDING. The crown's left (HI) highlight wedge, the polygon at 24,7 15,20 20,20 in artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html, yields ZERO pure HAT_HI pixels at archerH 78 on chromium measured in the full sprite. Every one of the 21 HAT_HI px the old comment attributed to it actually comes from brimFrontD. Confirmed by three independent methods across two agents: hide-one-element mutation, point-in-polygon attribution, and the toggle-visibility crop.

This is the same failure class the 1ta epic keeps hitting: oculist-1ta.18 (clipped ellipses squeezing the base to 12), oculist-1ta.22 (forearms invisible at natural size). A tone wedge that does not survive at the floor size.

IT DOES STILL READ, which is why this is P3. The wedge shows as a lighter sliver along the crown's left edge via near-exact antialiased blend, nearby pixels landing within 1-4 RGB units of pure HAT_HI. 'Survives only as antialiasing' is a different claim from 'achieves 21 pure pixels', and the wedge was presumably built expecting the latter.

ENGINE CAVEAT worth knowing before anyone touches the geometry: the zero is chromium-in-context specific. The oculist-uxa0 reviewer measured the same page on WebKit at crown-only 21/3/21, and chromium rendering the three crown elements in isolation also gives 3 pure HI px. So the wedge is not geometrically incapable of producing pure pixels; it is losing them to compositing in the full sprite on chromium. House standard is chromium-only (250 chromium refs, 0 webkit across repo/test and artifacts/prototypes), so chromium is the condition that counts, but the divergence points at the mechanism.

THE DECISION. Three ways to go, and this needs a judgement rather than an obvious fix:
1. Keep as-is. It reads via antialiasing, the comment is now accurate, nothing is broken.
2. Widen or resteepen the wedge so it clears a pure-pixel threshold at archerH 78, accepting it will look different at larger sizes where it already worked.
3. Drop the wedge and accept a two-tone crown at every size, simplifying the construction.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A choice among the three is made and recorded in the source comment next to the wedge.
- If geometry changes: re-measure crown-only and whole-hat tone counts at archerH 78, chromium, in the full sprite, and confirm occlusion-sweep.js stays 96/96 clean for arrowshot.
- If keeping as-is: no code change, the reasoning goes in the comment.
close_reason: Option 3 chosen and implemented: the crown HI wedge is removed. Evidence overturned the other two options: the wedge yields 0 pure HI px up to archerH ~87 and never more than 5 of an ~83px budget at the 112 ceiling, so it works at no size in the range; and it is imperceptible at native size on both chromium and webkit, reading only under magnification. Shadow wedge kept, confirmed sole source of all 10 HAT_SHADOW px. Post-removal crown-only 13/0/10, whole-hat 14/21/10. Sweep 96/96 clean, maxPixels=0. Reviewer PASS, reproduced every number independently and endorsed the ruling. Engine caveat recorded in the comment: on webkit the wedge did produce pure pixels at every size, so this is a real if imperceptible loss off-chromium. Commit c7036d5 on goal/p3-cleanup in the workspace repo.

title: Decide whether the q4nl archer clamp may push the archer fully off-screen
description:
The q4nl archer clamp puts the archer fully off-screen on about 15% of fallback geometries where main kept it on-screen. Nobody has ruled on whether that is acceptable.

Measured by the final oculist-q4nl reviewer, 2026-09-11. In a 40k random sample, 2877 of 19171 fallback geometries end with the archer entirely outside the viewport where main kept it visible: 1901 below and 976 above. The grid's below-only counter gives 4213, and 400k random gives 18578.

NOT A DEFECT BY THE SAFETY BAR. Every one of those geometries is already painted-dirty on main, none is worse by painted clearance, and the four safety counts are 0. The effect still draws its target rings and its arrow; only the archer is gone, so it reads as an arrow fired by nobody.

THE DECISION FOR CHRIS. oculist-aouc's own text calls an off-screen degrade an accepted last resort, but that was about the arrow's endpoint, not about losing the figure. The lever is how far the clamp is allowed to move the archer before it gives up and keeps main's result: today it takes any strictly-better archer clearance, however far off-screen that lands.

OPTIONS
1. Accept it, and record that in the fallback's comment.
2. Require the clamped archer to keep some minimum on-screen fraction, else keep main's result. The bead's measurements say that would hand roughly 15% of these geometries back to main's overlap.
3. Prefer the clamp direction that keeps more of the archer on screen, even when the other direction clears by more.

DONE-CRITERIA (once chosen)
- The chosen rule is implemented, or the decision is recorded in the fallback's comment with no code change.
- The four safety counts stay 0 against main on the grid and 400k random.
- occlusion-sweep.js's centered-500x180 and 500x220 rows stay clean.

title: arrowshot-fallback-check.js: 536 pre-existing archer overlaps left unfixed by the NEVER WORSE safety property
description:
UPDATE (oculist-q4nl review, run 2): the fix now computes a real HEAD/main
baseline inside fxArrowShot (computeHeadBaseline-equivalent, byte-for-byte
reproduction of oculist-aouc RUN 7's own feather/hat archerYAdjust and capped
push) and only swaps in q4nl's own whole-body archer clamp when it is a
PROVABLE improvement: baseline's own archer clearance <= 0 (still
overlapping), candidate's archer clearance is strictly better, candidate's
flight clearance is not worse, and no forward flight turns backward. Full
selection logic and proof of the "0 worse" / "0 clean-baseline-but-changed"
guarantees are in effects-playground.html's fxArrowShot, the SELECT block's
own comment.

TRUE SPLIT after this fix, measured by arrowshot-fallback-check.js's own
ARCHER STILL OVERLAPS report-only assertion (now report-only, not a
violation -- see its own comment) plus a changed-vs-kept-baseline
classification:

  523 of 9034 fallback geometries still leave the archer overlapping
  #match, EVERY ONE of them with the chooser's own result byte-for-byte
  identical to the baseline (HEAD/main) computation inside the same
  function -- confirmed by tagging each violation with whether the SELECT
  block's own takeCandidate flag fired: 0/523 do. All 523 are PRE-EXISTING
  on HEAD; 0 are introduced by q4nl's own clamp.

This is fewer prior candidates fixed than run 1's more aggressive (and,
per review, regression-causing) single-candidate replacement reached (which
touched everything with an archer overlap, not just cases strictly provable
as safe) -- the safety-first baseline/candidate design trades some
additional fixed cases for the guarantee that nothing regresses against
main. The underlying cause is unchanged from the original description: for
these 523, the archer CAN be moved to a position with positive painted
clearance, but doing so reshapes the flight's own launch point enough to
make the flight's painted clearance worse than leaving the archer alone,
and the flight is the harder, pre-existing safety bar (oculist-aouc RUN 7).

A fix would need to search across BOTH archer candidates (not just the
nearer on-screen one) combined with the flight's own push loop, picking
whichever joint combination gives the best overall result while still
holding all of RUN 7's and q4nl's own safety properties -- out of scope for
q4nl itself.

Run `node arrowshot-fallback-check.js` in artifacts/prototypes/ to
reproduce; count is currently 523 (report-only; worse=0, guardedDiff=0,
cleanButDiffers=0, reversed=0 -- exit 0).

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Final count after the N=480/Q=96 precision alignment across all three
tools (fxArrowShot's SELECT block, this check's own flightClear oracle, and
paint.js): 536, not 523 -- the 480-resolution SELECT judgment is slightly
more conservative than the 240-resolution one was, since it can see a few
more marginal flight conflicts the coarser sampling missed. Same
conclusion: 0/536 changed from baseline (fxArrowShot's own takeCandidate
flag never fires on any of them), so all 536 remain pre-existing on
main/HEAD, 0 introduced.

title: arrowshot-fallback-check: count forward flights turned backward, each measured against its own launch
description:
arrowshot-fallback-check.js does not count a forward flight turned backward, each measured against its own launch point.

Found by the final oculist-aouc reviewer, 2026-09-11. The check's reversal rule, taken from the implementer's scan2.js, measures main's endpoint against the NEW launch point. On its own that loosens the check: a reversal caused by archerYAdjust moving the launch point would be hidden. It is harmless today, because the reviewer's original newlyBackward metric (main forward, new backward, each against its own launch) is 0 on 1.83M grid and 400k random geometries. But the committed check is meant to be the durable guard, and it lacks that metric.

The original sign-change rule is also wrong in the other direction: it counted 22,255 grid geometries as reversals when all of them were main-backward flights that the fix turned forward. So use newlyBackward, not a bare sign change.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The check counts newlyBackward (main forward against main's launch, new backward against the new launch) and fails on any occurrence.
- It still exits 0 on the current playground and 1 on 221379b's.
- A scratch mutant in which archerYAdjust reverses a flight is caught.
close_reason: newlyBackward implemented on forwardSignFor (each flight judged against its own launch), folded into violations, old rule removed so there is one authoritative metric. Reviewer PASS: confirmed the old rule's blind spot from the pre-change source (both sides reduced to the same expression with no endpoint push) and empirically (old rule 0 vs newlyBackward 1212 on its own mutant); confirmed the forward-before gate is load-bearing (ungated would give 2088 false violations). Exits 0 on current playground, 1 on 221379b's (newlyBackward=785). Commit 17584f2 on goal/p3-cleanup in the workspace repo.

title: occlusion-sweep: assert foottap's forced-left landing on its figure element, not the .fx union
description:
The sweep exercises foottap's left landing but never asserts it, because foottap's .fx union reads 'overlap' in every scenario.

Found by the oculist-g1d2 reviewer, 2026-09-10. classifyLanding uses the union of all .fx rects. foottap's motion-line container is a fixed 40px box, wider than its 12px GAP, so the union crosses match.left by about 5.6px and reads overlap on 99 of 99 scenarios. So the forced-left rows' expect for foottap checks nothing. If a later change stopped foottap reaching left, its figure would land right, off-screen, and the rows would still print clean.

MEASURED ALTERNATIVE (the reviewer's probe): classify on the first .fx element, figWrap, which mount() appends first. That is never overlap: right on 96 of 96 grid scenarios and left on all 3 forced-left rows.

STEPS
1. Let a key choose which element classifyLanding reads, e.g. a per-key selector or "first .fx element" option. Use it for foottap only. Every other key keeps the union.
2. Set expect foottap 'left' on forced-left-1, -2 and -3.
3. The 96-grid lines stay byte-identical for all keys, and the forced output for batflight, arrowshot and reanimate is unchanged.

DONE-CRITERIA
- foottap's forced-left rows report landing=left and assert it.
- A scratch mutant that keeps foottap's figure on the right in those rows produces LANDING MISMATCH and exit 1.
- The grid output is unchanged for every key.
close_reason: Opt-in per-key landing source added: foottap classifies on the first mounted .fx element (figWrap), every other key keeps the union byte-for-byte. Forced-left rows now report landing=left and assert it. Reviewer PASS, with the decisive control: HEAD's harness against a mutant that stops foottap reaching left reports CLEAN exit 0, while the fixed harness reports 3 LANDING MISMATCH and exit 1. 96-grid byte-identical for all four keys. Reviewer also established classifyLanding has exactly one call site, so the grid never classified landing and no blind spot remains there. Commit 0abc76f on goal/p3-cleanup in the workspace repo.

title: prefire-scroll-abort-check row B.3 flaked once with ~120ms of wait headroom
description:
prefire-scroll-abort-check.js row B.3 flaked once, 19 of 20, with only about 120ms of headroom in its wait.

Seen by the oculist-ag8w reviewer, 2026-09-10, on HEAD run 2 of the plain fixture: index 8 did not draw. HEAD and the ag8w fix compute the same target there, so it is not that change. It did not reproduce: 40 probe fires settled in 536-580ms (median 555), all drew, and the working copy went 20 of 20 twice.

The harness waits 700ms for the smooth scroll to settle and the effect to mount. With a 580ms worst-case settle, that is ~120ms of headroom, which a loaded machine can eat.

FIX DIRECTION. Poll for the settle or the mount with a bounded timeout, rather than a fixed 700ms sleep. There may be a helper to copy in the other prototype harnesses.

DONE-CRITERIA
- B.3 waits on an observable condition, not a fixed sleep.
- 5 consecutive runs of prefire-scroll-abort-check.js exit 0.
- The abort rows still fail against a mutant that draws unconditionally.
close_reason: Fixed sleep replaced with a bounded poll keyed on a fresh mount: .fx cleared before every fire, so nonzero count at exit can only be the current fire's mount; position stability demoted to a gate that can delay but never cause an exit. Reviewer PASS after one retry (first attempt exited on stale DOM in 14 of 20 B.3 iterations). Verified: 35/35 waits exit entryFx=0 staleAtExit=0, min 551ms; 5 consecutive runs exit 0; unconditional-draw mutant still fails A.1/A.2/C.6. Commit 60740fc on goal/p3-cleanup in the workspace repo.

title: Playground effects keep playing against a stale rect after a mid-animation resize
description:
No effect in the playground reacts to a viewport resize mid-animation, so a resize leaves every effect playing against a stale match rect.

Found at the second review of oculist-1ta.6. oculist-1ta.12 fixed mid-animation SCROLL with a central scroll-dissolve hooked in rect() and mount(). A real wheel at t=950 took wandcast from 8 nodes and 28 animations to 0 and 0 within 460ms. A resize fires no scroll event, and there is no resize handler anywhere in effects-playground.html. The effect keeps playing at the old coordinates. For flanking figures that is cosmetic. For fxWandCast it is worse: its static clip-path hole stays at the old rect, so a resize that shifts the match slightly would let back-arc sparkles paint onto the glyphs.

DECISION NEEDED BEFORE BUILDING: is this worth handling in the prototype at all, or only at promotion into extension/content.js? Check first whether content.js already handles resize for shipped effects. If it does, the likely answer is to mirror its mechanism in the playground's central hook, the same way 1ta.12 did for scroll: dissolve on resize and give no effect its own handler.

Accept (if built): with a resize at mid-effect for wandcast and batflight, all .fx nodes and animations reach 0 within the same window the scroll dissolve uses, and #match is unmutated.
close_reason: Resize joins scroll on the existing central dissolve funnel, three functional lines, no per-effect wiring. Acceptance met on chromium and webkit: wandcast 8 nodes/25 anims to 0 in 195ms, batflight in 189ms against a 240ms window, #match byte-identical. Reviewer PASS, with mutation-proven probes (removing the listener gives 1107/1224ms; deleting the teardown removal leaks 12 listeners over 12 fires). No leak over 60 natural completions, no cross-run contamination, dragged-edge stream invokes the handler exactly once, scroll path and pre-fire suppression unchanged. Decision record: content.js DOES handle resize but abruptly, and ships none of these effects (registry is 12 unrelated ones), so there was nothing to mirror and this is new prototype design; abrupt-vs-dissolve stays open at promotion. Both recorded at the listener. CORRECTION: the implementer reported clip-path bleed eliminated; the reviewer could not reproduce that. It is reduced, 59 to 45 px-squared, not eliminated, because sparkles keep painting through the 180ms fade. Outside this bead's Accept clause, filed as its own bead. Commit 5b40011 on goal/p3-cleanup in the workspace repo.

title: Occlusion sweep never places the match near a viewport edge
description:
occlusion-sweep.js never places the match near a viewport edge, so edge-clamp occlusions pass it clean.

Found at the second review of oculist-1ta.6. fxWandCast came back 96/96 clean with maxPixels 0, yet with the match moved 10px from the right edge at 320x900 it paints 35 px inside the match rect, 1 of them glyph ink. The cause is a clamp that only engages within about 25px of an edge. The playground's paragraph text never puts #match there, so no SCENARIO exercises any effect's edge-clamp branch. Several effects have one: the right-else-left-else-clamp side logic, and the rx clamp in fxWandCast.

STEPS
1. In /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/prototypes/occlusion-sweep.js, add edge-placement scenarios. At a few viewports (at least 320x900 and 1280x900) and fonts (natural and 48px), put the match about 10px from the left edge and about 10px from the right edge. The reviewer did this by hiding the sidebar and moving #match with CSS position:relative plus left/right offsets. Choose a method that does not mutate #match in a way the harness's own cleanupAndAssert would flag, or teach cleanupAndAssert about it. Say which.
2. Keep the existing 96-scenario grid unchanged, so historical numbers stay comparable. Report the edge scenarios as an additional block.
3. Accept: batflight, arrowshot and foottap stay clean in the edge block (the reviewer measured 0 for all three). fxWandCast at its oculist-1ta.6 commit shows DIRTY in the edge block, so the new scenarios catch the known defect.

Do not change any effect in this bead.
close_reason: EDGE-PLACEMENT block added: 2 viewports x 2 fonts x 2 sides, sidebar hidden and #match nudged with position:relative to land 10px from the requested edge, reported separately and gating the exit code. 96-grid untouched, verified byte-identical by running old and new harness and diffing. title: fxHorseman loses the rear and throw beats at 360px and 320px viewports
description:
Found by the oculist-1ta.7 reviewer, 2026-09-09, while checking that prototype's criterion 1. A real gap, not a taste question, and separable from the aesthetic verdict Chris still owes on the effect itself.

WHAT HAPPENS. At 360x900 and 320x900, the two narrowest viewports in the sweep grid, the rear, throw and pumpkin launch all happen off-screen. Only about 15px of sprite is on screen at the moment of the throw.

WHY. rearX clamps to startX + 0.6 * SPRITE_W, which evaluates to -60, i.e. below zero. It clamps against the sprite's own width rather than against the viewport, so on a narrow viewport the stop-and-throw position lands off the left edge.

WHY IT MATTERS. Criterion 1 of oculist-1ta.7 is that gallop, rear, throw, arc, burst and exit are all visible and in that order. Two of those six are invisible at these sizes, so the criterion is met at 1280x900 and not met across the whole grid. The pumpkin's arc, the burst and the exit are unaffected, so the effect still resolves; it just loses the beat that motivates the throw.

FIX DIRECTION: clamp rearX against the viewport (and the match's own left edge) rather than against the sprite width, so the stop position is always on screen with the throwing hand visible. Check the GAP_CLEAR flanking still holds afterwards, since the rear is deliberately placed to the match's left with real clearance and moving it right could eat that gap.

DONE-CRITERIA

- All six beats are visible at 320x900 and 360x900, not just at 1280x900.
- The rear still sits clear of the match with its GAP_CLEAR gap intact at every grid viewport.
- The pumpkin still launches from the throwing hand's actual rotated position.
- Nothing regresses at 1280x900, where the beat timings are already correct.

title: Crown's own HAT_HI wedge is 0 pure pixels at archerH 78, not 21 as the source comment claims
description:
While measuring oculist-1ta.20 (hat base tone visibility), pixel-exact scans of the archer hat crown at archerH 78 found:

- Crown-only region (crownD path + both wedge polygons): HAT_BASE=15, HAT_HI=0, HAT_SHADOW=10.
- Whole-hat region (adds brimBackD + brimFrontD): HAT_BASE=15, HAT_HI=21, HAT_SHADOW=10.

The source comment above the wedge polygons (effects-playground.html, near the crownD/wedge block, ~line 4399-4401) reads: "measured 15 pure HAT_BASE px (up from the original dome's 12), 21 HAT_HI, 10 HAT_SHADOW, all three tones present" -- written directly under a discussion of the crown's own left (HI) wedge construction ("left (HI) wedge narrow at 5 units (steep edge, survives narrow)").

That reads as a claim about the crown's own tri-tone split. It is not accurate for the crown alone: the crown's own HI wedge (points '24,7 15,20 20,20') produces zero exact-color pixels at archerH 78 -- confirmed by direct pixel dump of an isolated screenshot crop of just that polygon. The 21 HAT_HI figure is real, but it comes entirely from the separate brimFrontD path (the beak), which happens to share the same HAT_HI fill color and sits well below/right of the crown. "All three tones present" is true of the hat as a whole but not true of the crown's own tri-wedge split, which is only 2 tones (BASE + SHADOW) at this size.

Not a visual defect on its own -- the crown's HI wedge still reads visually as a lighter highlight via antialiasing blend even without a bit-exact pixel (verified: nearby pixels land within 1-4 RGB units of pure HAT_HI). This bead is filed because the source comment's attribution is misleading for anyone reasoning about the crown's own tone split in the future, and because it means the crown's own three-tone claim is currently unverified/false at the pixel-exact level, not just thin like HAT_BASE was.

Suggested fix: correct the comment to attribute the 21 HAT_HI pixels to brimFrontD, not the crown wedge, and note the crown's own HI wedge measures 0 pure pixels at archerH 78.

Measurement method: ad-hoc playwright script (not part of the permanent suite), see /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html crownD/wedge block for the geometry referenced.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN ey2e ALONE. That bead framed it as a batflight problem. It is not: three effects now have landing branches the grid structurally cannot reach, and reanimate is the extreme case at 0 of 96. That technique is the basis of a fix, but it lived in a scratch script.

FIX DIRECTION. Add scenarios that force the non-preferred landings rather than relying on viewport size alone: push the match toward the edge the effect prefers so the fallback has to run. Fold it into SCENARIOS or add a second pass, and keep the existing 96 unchanged so the reference numbers still hold.

title: ensureVisible's intended-target formula ignores scroll-padding and scroll-margin, which would suppress every effect on a real page
description:
Found by the oculist-1ta.13 reviewer, 2026-09-09, while probing that bead's tolerance boundary. HARMLESS IN THE PLAYGROUND, potentially total in the extension. This should be settled BEFORE the logic reaches extension/content.js.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. oculist-1ta.13 made ensureVisible skip the effect when the settled match position is more than 4px from where scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) intended to put it. The intended target is computed as (window.innerHeight - elHeight) / 2.

WHY THAT IS INCOMPLETE. scrollIntoView honours scroll-padding on the scrolling container and scroll-margin on the target element. The formula ignores both. On any page that sets scroll-padding-top to clear a sticky header, which is extremely common, the browser will settle the element BELOW the computed centre by the padding amount. That is a correct scroll, but the formula reads it as a failed one.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT SUBTLE. Past 4px the effect is skipped entirely. A site with, say, a 64px sticky header would suppress EVERY beacon, silently, with no error. That is the exact failure mode oculist-1ta.13 was careful to avoid for wheel events, reintroduced by geometry instead of by input.

HOW IT WAS FOUND. The reviewer forced resting offsets with scroll-margin-top to test the tolerance boundary, which is precisely this mechanism used deliberately: offset = margin/2, deltas 0-4 drew and 5+ skipped.

FIX DIRECTIONS. Either read the computed scroll-padding and scroll-margin into the target calculation, or stop computing an expected position at all and instead capture the position the browser settles at for an UNINTERRUPTED scroll and compare against that. The second sidesteps the whole class, since it never has to model what scrollIntoView will do.

DONE-CRITERIA

- A page with scroll-padding-top set still draws its effects.
- A page with scroll-margin-top on the match still draws its effects.
- Genuine aborts (keyboard End, scrollTo) are still suppressed on such a page.
- The oculist-1ta.13 result still holds on the plain fixture: coverage rows draw nothing, false-positive rows draw normally.
close_reason: ensureVisible centres the scroll-margin-expanded box in the scroll-padded scrollport. Reviewer verified: C.1-C.4 fail at HEAD and pass after, genuine aborts are still suppressed under padding and margin, plain-fixture 1ta.13 rows unchanged, and a mutant is still caught.

title: occlusion-sweep never exercises batflight's above/below landings, and batflight gates the exit code
description:
Found during oculist-1ta.8, self-reported by the implementer and independently confirmed by the reviewer, 2026-09-09.

MEASURED. A landing-classification probe across all 96 sweep scenarios (8 viewports x 12 font sizes) for batflight: 61 RIGHT, 35 LEFT, 0 ABOVE, 0 BELOW.

WHY. occlusion-sweep.js positions the match with scrollIntoView({block:'center'}), which keeps it vertically centred in every scenario. A side landing therefore always fits, and the above/below fallbacks are never reached.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. batflight is one of only two clearance-contract keys the sweep's exit code actually depends on, and it is half of the '96/96 clean' claim on record. Two of its four landings have never been swept. oculist-1ta.8 was exactly a defect in one of those unswept landings: the mist's fade grew 19-30px upward against a GAP of 10 and tinted the match. The sweep reported 96/96 clean throughout, before and after, because it never produced that landing.

So the sweep's clean result is narrower than it reads: it covers the landings that ordinary centred geometry produces, not the fallbacks that degenerate geometry produces. The fallbacks are precisely where clearance is tightest and where a bug is most likely.

RELATED, same shape of gap: oculist-e2w (deferred artwork is dropped, so exempt keys' counts are lower bounds) and oculist-wc19 (a comment names 320x900 as a mirrored-landing case, and no grid viewport produces one for fxFootTap either). Three separate effects now have landings or artwork the sweep structurally cannot see.

FIX DIRECTIONS. Add scenarios that force the fallbacks, e.g. a viewport short enough that neither side fits, or a match pinned near the top or bottom edge. oculist-1ta.8's verification did this with a synthetic-geometry script; that approach could be folded into the sweep as extra scenarios rather than kept in a throwaway.

DONE-CRITERIA

- The sweep produces at least one above landing and at least one below landing for batflight, and reports them.
- Reverting oculist-1ta.8's fade anchor makes the sweep fail rather than stay clean.
- The existing 96 scenarios and their numbers are unchanged, so the reference figures still hold.

title: Now that the sweep's timer neutralization works, the six exempt effects' pixel counts are lower bounds, not measurements
description:
Raised by the oculist-1ta.21 reviewer, 2026-09-09. This is a measurement limitation, not a code defect, and it only became true when oculist-hgt revived the neutralization.

THE SHAPE OF IT. occlusion-sweep.js drops every setTimeout an effect schedules during runEffect, which is what makes the sweep deterministic. But effects-playground.html names FOURTEEN fx* functions that mount top-level nodes from inside a later setTimeout, including fxMatchstrike, fxComet, fxStamp and fxInkbloom. That artwork is therefore never created during a sweep, so those effects' printed pixel counts are a LOWER BOUND on their real occlusion rather than a measurement of it.

CONCRETE EXAMPLE. fxMatchstrike's setTimeout(..., 400) body creates a glow div at left r.left-4, top r.top-4, width r.width+8, height r.height+8, i.e. artwork positioned exactly over the match, plus six embers across the match's width. None of it is measured.

WHY THE EXIT CODE IS STILL TRUSTWORTHY. fxBatFlight and fxArrowShot contain no setTimeout at all, and they are the clearance-contract keys the exit code depends on. All four affected effects named above are in NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT and report N/A. So nothing that gates CI is wrong; what is wrong is the confidence a reader places in the N/A rows' numbers.

THE TENSION, and it is a real design fork rather than a bug to squash. Determinism and completeness are in conflict here. Suppressing timers is what made the sweep reproducible (oculist-hgt), but it is also what hides this artwork. Options include sweeping twice, once neutralized for determinism and once not for coverage; driving deferred mounts synchronously via a seam rather than dropping them; or accepting the lower bound and labelling the rows so nobody reads them as complete.

DO NOT default to the third option silently. It is the cheapest and may be right, but it should be chosen.

DONE-CRITERIA

- Either the deferred artwork is measured, or every affected row says its number is a lower bound and why.
- batflight and arrowshot stay exit-code-trustworthy either way.
- Whichever way it goes, the reasoning is in the file rather than only in this bead.
close_reason: Labelling path taken: LOWERBOUND marker threaded through per-row lines, both SUMMARY lines and the FINAL recap, so the incomplete-count caveat reaches the last per-key line a reader sees. Fourteen deferred-mount keys re-derived from source by two independent methods (not taken from the playground's snapshot list); indirection closed structurally, no mount() call sites exist outside an fx function body. Exit-code semantics unchanged, byte-identical to HEAD modulo label strings for one clean and one red effect. batflight/arrowshot trustworthiness restated on the true reason (cleanup-only setTimeout), correcting this bead's own description, cited by function name and quoted fragment since the line-number citation went stale in three days. Reviewer PASS after one round of NEEDS-WORK (FINAL block was unlabelled, citations stale). Ten clearance-contract keys still drive pass/fail on lower-bound counts: flagged in-file and filed as oculist-xh9p. Commit e348015 on goal/p3-cleanup in the workspace repo.

src/inspector/injected-script.cc, ProtocolPromiseHandler's constructor calls
m_evaluationResult.SetWeak(...) UNCONDITIONALLY at construction time -- i.e.
every Runtime.evaluate/awaitPromise:true call holds the awaited promise via a
WEAK v8::Global from the moment the eval is accepted, for the entire time it
is pending. If nothing else in the page's live JS graph keeps the promise
strongly reachable, a GC that runs while it's pending can collect it, and
V8 Inspector reports exactly "Promise was collected"
(PromiseHandlerTracker::discard, DiscardReason::kPromiseCollected). This is a
genuine GC race, not a CDP message being dropped.

Note V8's `main` branch (not yet shipped) has since moved to a lazier design
-- the promise stays strongly held until an explicit session reset / context
destroy / object-group release calls makeWeakForSession/Context/ObjectGroup --
so this may already be fixed upstream by the time Chromium ships a later
version; worth re-checking before investing effort here.

For the test idiom specifically: `new Promise(resolve => chrome.storage.session
.get(key, r => resolve(...)))` is never assigned to a variable, so its only
strong retention path is the pending storage.get() callback closure ->
resolve()'s internal [[Promise]] slot. Under load that path is evidently not
always enough to save it from a GC race with V8 Inspector's weak handle.

IF this becomes worth fixing (e.g. CI starts running on contended hardware):
1. Consolidate the 36 duplicated `evalInContentScript` definitions into ONE
   helper in test/helpers/ (a wait.js companion, e.g. test/helpers/cdp.js) --
   test/helpers/wait.js already only takes evalInContentScript as a parameter
   (waitForContentScriptValue), it does not define it; no existing shared
   helper is being bypassed today, one needs to be created.
2. In that single helper, add a bounded retry SCOPED SPECIFICALLY to the
   "Promise was collected" error string (not a blanket retry on any CDP
   error) -- re-issuing the same expression is safe because the calls that
   hit this are the chrome.storage-wrapped ones, which are idempotent reads/
   removals.
3. Alternative worth comparing: give content.js's isolated world a
   long-lived, page-global handle to storage values (avoiding an ephemeral,
   unretained Promise entirely) and poll it with the *existing*
   waitForContentScriptValue synchronous-poll primitive instead of
   awaitPromise -- this sidesteps the weak-handle GC race altogether rather
   than retrying around it, at the cost of a content.js-side change.
4. Re-verify at load ~55+ before/after; a capped, monitored load generator on
   a shared machine could not safely reach that range in oculist-52u's
   investigation (11 concurrent users, 10 cores) -- confirmed clean at ~15
   only. Reproducing this reliably may require a dedicated/isolated box.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
CORRECTION from the oculist-52u reviewer, 2026-09-09, who verified the V8 source claim first-hand. The mechanism verdict stands; the retention paragraph in this bead's description is wrong in detail and should not be acted on as written.

WHAT THIS BEAD SAYS. That the promise's only strong retention path is the pending storage.get callback closure into resolve's [[Promise]] slot, and that under load that path is not always enough to keep it alive.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. In Chromium 149.0.7827.55, extensions/renderer/bindings/api_request_handler.{h,cc} holds an in-flight request's callback in a v8::Global<v8::Function> extension_callback_ inside AsyncResultHandler, owned by PendingRequest. That is a STRONG root. So while the storage.get is genuinely in flight, the promise is strongly reachable and cannot be collected.

THE REAL WINDOW is post-resolve, pre-microtask: after resolve() fires, the pending request is destroyed and the closure dropped, but before the inspector's thenCallback reaction microtask runs. A PromiseReaction holds the derived promise and the handler function, not the original promise. So 'GC'd while pending' is right; 'the starved page loses the closure's grip' is not the mechanism.

WHY IT DOES NOT CHANGE THE REMEDY. A retry scoped to the literal 'Promise was collected' string is still safe and still idempotent for these calls, and the poll-a-page-global alternative still sidesteps awaitPromise entirely. Only the explanation needs fixing, not the plan.

STRENGTHENED, from the same review. In ProtocolPromiseHandler::add, when value->IsPromise() the handler chains onto the ORIGINAL promise, so the weakly-held object is literally the test's new Promise(...), not a derived one. And the lazy-makeWeak redesign on V8 main is absent from 15.0-lkgr and 15.1-lkgr too, so the shipped-everywhere claim holds through Chromium 151, not just 149.

UNVERIFIED, and worth knowing before anyone relies on the window above: the exact ordering of Chromium's microtask checkpoint relative to AsyncResultHandler destruction. That is what would pin the collection window precisely.

comments.text:
DEFERRED BY DECISION, 2026-09-09. Passed into the sweep-truth-and-harness-debt /goal run, deliberately not worked, and Chris confirmed leaving it deferred rather than doing the consolidation now.

REASONING. This bead is conditional by construction: its title starts 'If CI/dev machines ever run this suite under sustained load ~55+' and its body is scoped 'IF this becomes worth fixing (e.g. CI starts running on contended hardware)'. STILL TRUE AND STILL WAITING. The 36 duplicated evalInContentScript definitions are real debt independent of the load condition, so someone may want step 1 on its own merits some day. comments.text:
RE-CHECK DONE 2026-09-10, the step this bead says to do first. Verdict: NOT SHIPPED for the Chromium this suite runs, so the bead does not close as obsolete, and it stays deferred under the 2026-09-09 decision.

THE V8 CHANGE.
