title: occlusion-sweep's window.setTimeout neutralization is dead at HEAD, so deferred-mount effects measure as noise
description:
Found by the oculist-aun reviewer, 2026-09-09, with a decisive experiment. This is a silent HARNESS REGRESSION introduced by oculist-eke (f3ad34c) and it invalidates any occlusion-sweep number taken at HEAD for a deferred-mount effect.

THE MECHANISM. occlusion-sweep.js neutralizes deferred work by patching window.setTimeout to a no-op around runEffect:

  const realSetTimeout = window.setTimeout;
  window.setTimeout = function () { return 0; };
  try { window.runEffect(key); } finally { window.setTimeout = realSetTimeout; }

effects-playground.html no longer calls window.setTimeout. oculist-eke shadowed setTimeout inside the IIFE over a nativeSetTimeout reference captured at page load, so the harness patches something the effects never touch. The neutralization is dead code.

CONSEQUENCE. Deferred mounts and the effects' own cleanup timers run on real wall clock DURING the sample loop, so they race it. Measured at HEAD: .fx count goes inkbloom 1 to 7 and matchstrike 2 to 10 over 1500ms, while comet 6 to 0 and stamp 1 to 0 as cleanup fires.

MEASURED NON-DETERMINISM AT HEAD. inkbloom run twice: dirty 54 then 53, maxPixels 2113 then 1996, 77 of 96 per-scenario lines differ. comet twice: maxPixels 3699 then 3426, 82 of 96 lines differ.

THE DECISIVE EXPERIMENT. The reviewer extracted effects-playground.html at 1d9faf5 (pre-eke, zero occurrences of nativeSetTimeout, the tree the oculist-ucs reviewer measured) and ran the sweep twice: inkbloom CLEAN, comet 1031/96, stamp 4137/96. Both runs identical, 0 of 288 per-scenario lines differing, reproducing the recorded ucs numbers EXACTLY.

WHICH NUMBERS ARE TRUSTWORTHY. The three effects that reproduced exactly at HEAD (matchstrike 9356, scanline 1560, emberignite 819) are the non-deferred ones. The three that did not (stamp, comet, inkbloom) are precisely the deferred-mount ones. The recorded ucs numbers are reliable; anything measured at HEAD for a deferred-mount effect is not.

CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: the stamp 4137 to 9246 and comet 1031 to 3820 discrepancies noticed during oculist-aun were attributed to oculist-9j4 and to nothing respectively. Both are this. The 9j4 guard is unreachable without a scroll or supersede and the sweep does neither.

FIX DIRECTION. Patch before the page's own script evaluates, e.g. an init script via addInitScript, or reset the page between scenarios. Whatever is chosen must be verified against the shadow rather than against window, since that is exactly the assumption that broke.

REPRODUCER: node occlusion-sweep.js inkbloom, twice, and diff the per-scenario lines.

DONE-CRITERIA

- The neutralization actually suppresses deferred work in the playground as it exists now, verified against the shadow and not against window.
- Two consecutive runs of inkbloom and comet produce identical per-scenario output.
- The pre-eke numbers are reproducible at HEAD: matchstrike 9356, stamp 4137, scanline 1560, comet 1031, emberignite 819.
- A runnable check fails if the neutralization silently dies again.
close_reason:
The neutralization is live again and now reaches the shadow. page.addInitScript installs the hook BEFORE page.goto, so the playground's load-time var nativeSetTimeout = window.setTimeout captures a controllable wrapper rather than the browser native; the wrapper reads a page-global flag at call time, so the harness still toggles per runEffect the way the old try/finally intended, and counts what it drops. Contract: for the span of one synchronous runEffect, any setTimeout an fx schedules is dropped entirely and never fires later; WAAPI animations created synchronously are untouched, which is what the sweep needs to observe.

Reviewer PASS with verification well past the brief. Determinism: inkbloom and comet each run 4 times including under 8 spinning CPU loads, all byte-identical. Pre-eke numbers all five exact (matchstrike 9356, stamp 4137, scanline 1560, comet 1031, emberignite 819), and stronger, running the fixed harness against the extracted pre-eke playground reproduces all 96 comet per-scenario lines identically, so this is full behavioural equivalence rather than matching summaries. Suppression proven directly: a neutralized matchstrike run leaves 2 .fx elements still after 2.5s, versus 2 growing to 10 within 700ms unneutralized, so timers are dropped rather than deferred.

Criterion 4 met and hardened. runNeutralizationControl fires matchstrike (verified to make 4 unconditional setTimeout calls, no branches or geometry conditions) on every invocation and asserts the drop counter moved. Reviewer reproduced both historical failure shapes (hook never installed; hook installed after goto, the eke-style disconnect) and both exit 1, then attacked canary rot by pointing the canary at a key that schedules no timers: it FAILS CLOSED rather than silently passing.

inkbloom reads maxPixels 0, which is restoration and not over-suppression: the pre-eke playground with the pre-eke harness also yields 0. That is the separate unsampled-endpoint gap on oculist-1ta.21, deliberately not chased here.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Cosmetic addendum from the oculist-aun re-review, 2026-09-09. occlusion-sweep.js's STABILITY WARNING cites 77/96 and 82/96 as the measured unstable per-scenario line counts. A later run of the same command produced stamp 96/96, comet 96/96, inkbloom 50/96. That divergence CONFIRMS the instability the warning documents rather than contradicting it, but a reader who tries to reproduce those two specific numbers will not. When this bead lands and the numbers become stable, replace the illustrative counts with reproducible ones or drop them.

title: The orphan-armed marker span arms the extension's own domObserver, a new coupling the test did not have before
description:
Found by the oculist-3wq reviewer, 2026-09-08. Dormant today, with roughly 9x headroom at its worst, but it is a coupling that did not exist before that bead and it is not obvious from reading the test.

WHAT WAS ADDED. oculist-3wq crosses the isolated-world boundary by appending an invisible span.oc-orphan-armed-marker to document.documentElement when the patched setTimeout intercepts the orphan timer being armed. armRedrawCounter()'s MutationObserver reads that and records __ocOrphanArmedAt in the main world.

THE HAZARD. The marker is not an oculist node, so the extension's OWN domObserver (content.js:4775) sees it as an ordinary page mutation and arms setTimeout(rescanAfterMutation, 350). If that ever fires, it draws an extra beacon and the clean path reports a spurious 2 !== 1, i.e. the test fails claiming the bug is present when it is not.

WHY IT DOES NOT FIRE TODAY. __ocDestroy disconnects the observer before the 350ms debounce elapses. Measured margin from marker append to the rebuild toggle: 3.0 to 39.4ms against 350ms, under concurrency 4. About 9x headroom at the worst observed value.

WHY IT IS WORTH TRACKING ANYWAY. The margin is a race against a debounce, not a guarantee, and it fails in the DANGEROUS direction: a spurious failure that looks exactly like the real regression this test exists to catch. Anyone debugging that would start by suspecting content.js.

FIX DIRECTIONS. Either give the marker a class the extension's domObserver already ignores (check how oculist's own nodes are excluded), or carry the arm time across the boundary without mutating the page at all.

DONE-CRITERIA

- Either the marker no longer arms domObserver, or a comment at the marker append states the margin and why it holds.
- The oculist-3wq mutation check still fails 2 !== 1 with clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer() removed.
- No change to the clean-path wall clock.
close_reason: RESOLVED BY oculist-4z3 (commit a087d6c), not worked separately. That bead's sibling-timer fix carries the orphan's arm time across the world boundary through an isolated-world global instead of a DOM node, so the span.oc-orphan-armed-marker and its MutationObserver handling were retired as dead code. The hazard is eliminated rather than mitigated: with no marker there is no non-oculist page mutation for the extension's domObserver to see, so the 350ms rescan is never armed and the 9x-headroom race against that debounce no longer exists. All three of jz0's own done-criteria verified independently by the 4z3 reviewer: the marker no longer arms domObserver (it does not exist; repo-wide grep for oc-orphan-armed-marker and __ocOrphanArmedAt finds zero hits outside bead prose), the mutation check still fails 2 !== 1 with clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer removed (2/2 runs, real AssertionError), and the clean-path wall clock did not increase (it dropped roughly 480ms). The only remaining boundary crossing is read-only: the main-world MutationObserver watches .oc-beacon nodes the extension itself inserts, which isOculistMutation filters at content.js:4777. Reopen if you disagree that a bead resolved by a sibling's diff should close without its own cycle.

title: Shared-CDP-session Runtime.evaluate+awaitPromise idiom can lose evaluations under load, across 36 test files
description:
Reproduced 2026-09-06 while triaging oculist-e7l, which anticipated exactly this ('if it recurs, it belongs with the test-infrastructure beads'). It recurred.

THE FAILURE. cdpSession.send: Protocol error (Runtime.evaluate): Promise was collected. Neither a timeout nor an assertion; the Playwright/CDP layer losing a pending evaluation.

THE IDIOM. 36 test files each define their own identical evalInContentScript helper, sending Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise true and a contextId over a single long-lived shared CDP client opened once per describe block. The calls that fail wrap a chrome.storage callback in a promise, e.g. new Promise(resolve => chrome.storage.session.get('oc-worklist', r => resolve(r['oc-worklist']))).

MEASURED. Originally seen once at chip_row.test.js:435 under load average around 58. Reproduced TWICE on 2026-09-06 at load averages 55 to 126, but at list_search.test.js:356, not in chip_row. That call was introduced by e97e029 on 2026-08-26 and is untouched by any recent work, so this is not something a specific fix introduced. chip_row.test.js:480 carries the byte-identical call. Reproducing it in a sibling file is STRONGER evidence for the idiom being the hazard than a chip_row reproduction would have been.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE AT ORDINARY LOAD. chip_row.test.js: 5 of 5 solo runs, 1 of 1 full suite, and 10 consecutive runs under 10 busy processes (load average about 8), all clean, zero CDP errors.

EXPOSURE NOTE. oculist-pzk's fix (7a760de) added one more instance of this idiom to chip_row.test.js's addTerm(), which is called 49 times per run of that file. Storage-wrapped evaluates in that file went from roughly 20 to roughly 69 per run, about a 3x increase in surface for this error. That does not make the fix wrong, it fixed a real cross-test resurrection race, but it concentrates exposure in the file the original sighting named.

FIRST STEP: establish whether 'Promise was collected' here means the evaluation was genuinely dropped by CDP or the page was starved long enough for the promise to be GC'd while pending. That determines whether the fix is a shared helper with a bounded retry, a different waiting primitive that does not rely on awaitPromise across a starved page, or simply an accepted limit of running this suite at load average 58.

DO NOT paper over it with a blanket retry-on-CDP-error before that question is answered.

DONE-CRITERIA

- The mechanism is characterised, not just observed.
- Whatever the remedy, it is applied in ONE place rather than copied into 36 files.
- A run at load average around 58 is either clean or the residual failure rate is recorded.
close_reason:
MECHANISM ESTABLISHED FROM PRIMARY SOURCE, and it is the GC side of the fork, not CDP dropping the evaluation. In V8 branch 14.9-lkgr, which is what Chromium 149 ships (installed browser reports 149.0.7827.55, chromiumdash maps mstone 149 to v8_branch 14.9), ProtocolPromiseHandler's constructor calls m_evaluationResult.SetWeak unconditionally, with no guard. So every Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise true holds the awaited promise through a weak v8::Global for its whole pending life; if nothing in the live JS graph roots it, a GC pass collects it and PromiseHandlerTracker::discard with DiscardReason::kPromiseCollected emits this exact string. That callback is the only producer of it in the file. In ProtocolPromiseHandler::add the handler chains onto the ORIGINAL promise when the value is a promise, so the weakly-held object is literally the test's new Promise(...). Upstream V8 main has since made makeWeak lazy, but that redesign is absent from 15.0-lkgr and 15.1-lkgr as well, so every Chromium through 151 has this shape. Reviewer verified all of the above independently by fetching the sources.

REMEDY: accepted limit, no code change now, which the bead names as one of its three permitted outcomes. This is an upstream weak-handle design that any awaitPromise caller hits, at loads this suite never runs at. Criterion 2 is satisfied by there being no change to copy anywhere; there is also no existing shared helper being bypassed, since test/helpers/wait.js takes evalInContentScript as a parameter and documents that each file defines its own. Criterion 3 is satisfied in its weaker recorded sense only: clean at load ~4 (321/321), ~8 (10/10 previously) and ~14.7 (22/22), while the 55-126 range that reproduces it was deliberately not attempted on a shared 10-core box with 11 users. No residual rate at ~58 exists and none was invented.

CORRECTION, from the reviewer, recorded on oculist-qpl: the retention story is not 'the starved page loses the closure's grip'. An in-flight chrome.storage callback is a strong root (v8::Global in AsyncResultHandler), so the promise cannot be collected while the request is genuinely pending. The unrooted window is post-resolve, pre-microtask. Does not change the remedy.

FOLLOW-UP: oculist-qpl carries the consolidation design, with any retry scoped to the literal string rather than blanket CDP errors. The bead's prohibition on a blanket retry was honoured; grep confirms no retry was added anywhere.

title: occlusion-sweep reports 5 of 6 deferred-mount effects dirty at HEAD, contradicting uc1's 96/96 clean claim
description:
Measured by the oculist-ucs reviewer, 2026-09-06, while confirming that bead's fix changed nothing here. Pre-existing at HEAD, unrelated to the ucs change, but it contradicts something already on the record.

MEASURED, identical before and after the ucs fix (which is how it was established as pre-existing):

- matchstrike: maxPixels=9356, dirty=96
- stamp: 4137, dirty=96
- scanline: 1560, dirty=96
- comet: 1031, dirty=96
- emberignite: 819, dirty=96
- inkbloom: CLEAN

The sweep's control passed in both runs, so the harness is not the problem.

WHY IT MATTERS. oculist-uc1 recorded a '96/96 clean, zero pixels' result. Five of these six are dirty at HEAD, so that claim must have covered a different effect set (probably the canonical/shipped effects rather than the playground's full 45). Someone should establish which set uc1 actually measured before the clean claim is relied on again.

FIRST STEP: read occlusion-sweep.js to find what dirty=96 counts and whether 96 is a constant denominator rather than a score. Then determine whether these five are a real occlusion defect or the sweep measuring something the playground effects were never expected to satisfy.

DONE-CRITERIA

- It is established whether the five dirty effects are a genuine defect or an inapplicable measurement.
- The uc1 clean claim is corrected on the record, with the effect set it actually covered named.
- If genuine, the defect is filed with a reproducer; if not, occlusion-sweep says so when run against playground effects.
close_reason: VERDICT: inapplicable measurement, not an occlusion defect. The five dirty effects render on or against the match by design; the sweep's match-clearance contract describes the batflight/arrowshot archetype, where the figure carries explicit GAP and REACH clearance math so it sits beside the match. occlusion-sweep.js now says so: a NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT set labels those keys N/A with per-effect evidence, and their dirty counts no longer set the exit code, while harness failures still fail. Graded rather than flattened: matchstrike, stamp, scanline, inkbloom STRONG, comet MEDIUM, emberignite kept but labelled a knowingly-tolerated halo overrun since its flame geometry never overlaps and all 819 pixels are box-shadow bleed. uc1's claim corrected on the record (see the comment on oculist-uc1): it covers batflight and arrowshot only, produced by oculist-1ta.16 and reused here, so it never contradicted the ucs numbers, it measured a disjoint set. Failed review once, passed on retry. TWO HARNESS DEFECTS FOUND ON THE WAY, both filed rather than fixed here: oculist-hgt, the window.setTimeout neutralization is dead at HEAD because the playground shadows setTimeout over a load-time native reference, so deferred-mount effects measure as wall-clock noise; and an escalation on oculist-1ta.21, where the sample loop never samples t=maxEnd, which is the sole cause of inkbloom's recorded CLEAN being a false negative. Correcting the earlier attribution: the stamp and comet number discrepancies are oculist-eke's shadow, not oculist-9j4.

title: A superseded run's deferred mounts attach to the NEW run's array, so they still land at a stale rect
description:
Measured by the oculist-ucs reviewer, 2026-09-06. NOT a regression: byte-identical before and after that fix. It is the one path left where a node lands at a stale position, and the mirror image of the case ucs guarded.

WHAT UCS FIXED. mount() early-returns when currentRunEls.dissolved is set, so a run cannot mount after its own scroll-dissolve. That holds only while the dissolved run is still the current one.

THE HOLE. mount() reads the module-level currentRunEls, not a per-run closure. An old run's pending setTimeout therefore calls the same global mount(), which by then sees the NEW run's array with dissolved === false, and attaches the stale nodes anyway.

MEASURED. Fire matchstrike, scroll at 120ms, fire scanline at 200ms. At 520ms the DOM holds scanline's 2 nodes at the correct rect PLUS matchstrike's 8 deferred nodes at the pre-scroll rect: 40x32@452,334, 64x30@458,335, and 6 embers.

FIX DIRECTION. The array flag is the wrong carrier. mount() needs real run identity: capture the run's own array (or a run token) at rect() time and have deferred mounts check the run they belong to, not whatever run is current when they fire.

ALSO. The comment at effects-playground.html:186-198 over-claims, describing the guard as per-run without the 'while that run is still current' qualifier. Correct it with the fix.

NIT, same area. effects-playground.html:181 sets currentRunEls.dissolved = false, which is dead: line 180 already assigns a fresh array. Left in place rather than shipped unreviewed; delete it here.

DONE-CRITERIA

- Firing a second effect after a mid-flight scroll leaves NO node from the first run at the pre-scroll rect.
- A new effect fired after a dissolve still mounts normally at the correct rect (the ucs reviewer confirmed this does not currently regress; keep it that way).
- The :186-198 comment matches what the guard actually promises.
- The dead assignment at :181 is gone.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on the second review. The last path where a node lands at a stale rect is closed. ROOT CAUSE: clearFx() does NOT cancel pending setTimeouts, so a superseded run's timers always survive and fire later, and mount() read the module-level currentRunEls rather than a per-run closure, so those late callbacks saw the NEW run's array with dissolved false and attached anyway. FIX, with no fx* function edited: the global setTimeout is shadowed inside the IIFE by a hoisted function declaration, so all 45 effects pick it up automatically. At schedule time it captures scheduledEls = mountRunEls || currentRunEls, which makes identity flow through nested timer chains rather than adopting whatever run is current when the outer callback fires; when the callback runs it restores mountRunEls for that callback's duration via try/finally. mount() then refuses when owner !== currentRunEls (new, a later run has replaced this one) or owner.dissolved (the existing ucs guard). rect() resets mountRunEls to null on a new run, which is load-bearing: without it an effect fired via the sidebar's ensureVisible() setTimeout(finish, 600) path would inherit a stale identity and refuse its own initial synchronous mounts. VERIFIED BY THE REVIEWER, not taken on trust. Bead scenario reproduced exactly: pre-fix 10 .fx nodes at t=520ms with 8 stale at the pre-scroll rect (40x32@450,334, 64x30@458,335, 6 embers); post-fix exactly 2, both at the post-scroll rect, 0 stale. The suppression risk, which would have been worse than the bug, was hunted and is clean: rapid re-fire 50ms apart counting only run 2's mounts gives matchstrike 10, comet 7, stamp 7, inkbloom 8, identical to each effect's clean single-fire baseline; re-fire after a dissolve puts all 10 nodes at the post-scroll rect and 0 at the pre-scroll one; the no-scroll path across all 45 effects with seeded Math.random shows 0 diffs and 0 page errors. A 45-effect supersede sweep found 14 effects whose stale deferred mounts are now refused and 0 effects mounting more than before. clearTimeout pairing verified empirically intact (the shadow returns the native id). FAILED THE FIRST REVIEW on two documentation-shaped defects, both fixed: the new harness asserted only that stale nodes were absent, so neutering mount() entirely still printed PASS, while its docstring claimed it checked scanline's nodes were present at the correct rect; and the comment enumerated the deferred-mount set as six effects including fxScanline and fxEmberignite, which mount synchronously and never had the defect. The harness now asserts exactly 2 scanline nodes at the post-scroll rect and was proven three ways by the reviewer: neutered mount FAILS with found 0, guard removed FAILS with 8 stale, unmutated PASSES. The enumeration is now the measured 14, independently re-derived by the reviewer with their own brace-matching scan and spot-checked by hand, and framed as a snapshot with the re-verification procedure named rather than as a contract. Full suite 321/321; the ucs and ak5 harnesses both still pass. Residual latent hazards filed as oculist-q9r: the shadow drops trailing args (0 of 82 call sites affected today), setInterval is unshadowed, and the harness docstring mislabels which guard clause its mutation falsifies.

title: instant_scroll stale-draw quiet window is anchored to m1's draw, not to the orphan timer's arm time
description:
Measured by the oculist-pzk reviewer, 2026-09-06, while passing that bead. Not a defect today; a detector that is weaker than it looks.

WHAT THE TEST DOES. instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw stretches the isolated world's setTimeout so mfar's 50ms orphaned draw timer fires at 4000ms instead, which makes __ocDestroy deterministically win the race the test is about. waitForRedrawCountToSettle() then uses a 4600ms quiet window, long enough that an un-cancelled orphan draw would land inside it and be observed. That is verified: with clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer() removed the test fails 2 !== 1, and the quiet window visibly restarts (clean 5.09s vs mutant 9.1-9.4s).

THE GAP. The quiet window is anchored to __ocRedrawAt, i.e. m1's own draw. The orphan fires at arm_time + 4000, and arm_time sits two CDP round trips AFTER m1's draw. So the 600ms of headroom between 4000 and 4600 is really a margin against CDP overhead, not a structural guarantee that the window still covers the orphan.

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT. It fails safe on the passing path: a slow box only makes the clean test wait longer. The risk is a weaker detector, not a flaky test. The margin held 7 of 7 runs including under full-suite load at concurrency 4.

FIX DIRECTION. Record the orphan's arm time inside the setTimeout patch (around instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw.test.js:250) and anchor the quiet window on that instead of on m1's draw. Then the coverage is structural and the 600ms guess disappears.

DONE-CRITERIA

- The quiet window's deadline is derived from the orphan timer's own arm time.
- The mutation check still fails: removing clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer() from __ocDestroy produces 2 !== 1.
- No increase in the clean-path wall clock beyond what the 4000ms stretch already costs.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. The deadline is now anchored on the orphan timer's own arm time, which is what the bead asked for, and the 600ms CDP-overhead margin is gone. Mechanism: the isolated content-script world shares only the DOM with the main world, so the fix follows the same route the existing __ocRedrawCount counter already uses. When the patched setTimeout intercepts the delay===50 call, it appends an invisible marker span; armRedrawCounter()'s MutationObserver sees it and records __ocOrphanArmedAt. The deadline becomes armedAt + 4000 + 500. Verified by instrumentation that the anchor really is the arm and not m1's draw: on the mutant the orphan draw was observed at armedAt + 4004.2, +4004.7 and +4003.2ms. THE DETECTOR CHANGED CHARACTER and the reviewer checked it on that basis. The old design was a quiet window that RESTARTED when the orphan landed, which is what proved it observed rather than outlasted; the new one waits to an absolute deadline, which is outlasting by construction. It is still sound, and the three links were verified: armedAt is recorded in an observer callback one microtask AFTER the append, so the deadline is conservative; the orphan's .oc-beacon append and the counter increment land in the same task checkpoint, measured 2.0 to 4.7ms of lag past the stretch; and waitForFunction resolves at the deadline while the count is read in a LATER round trip, so the count can only have grown. No window exists where the orphan fired but the count had not crossed the boundary before the read. FIRE_JITTER_MS of 500 was ruled legitimate rather than a re-smuggled sleep: the 600ms it replaced had to absorb four CDP round trips plus a waitForSelector and an inputValue read, all process-external and load-sensitive, while the 500ms absorbs one in-page timer dispatch and one observer hop, measured at under 1 percent of the budget. Filed as oculist-4z3 anyway, with the structural alternative the reviewer identified. Mutation verified independently both directions: removing clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer() gives a real AssertionError 2 !== 1 in 4 of 4 solo runs and 6 of 6 under concurrency 4, never a Playwright timeout and never the never-arms guard. The never-arms guard was proven to fire by making the patch intercept a delay that never occurs: a clear error, not a hang and not a silent pass. Assertions byte-identical to HEAD. Clean path did not regress, 5.72 to 6.06s against HEAD's 5.82 to 5.87s, slightly faster since 4500 from the arm lands earlier than 4600 from m1's draw. Reviewer's counts: 12 concurrency iterations at 5 files each, 60 executions, zero failures; full suite 321/321. One new latent coupling filed as oculist-jz0: the marker is not an oculist node, so the extension's own domObserver arms a 350ms rescan against it, currently disarmed in time with about 9x headroom.

title: Pack-notice cap safety rests on an undocumented, untested invariant
description:
Established by the oculist-2mx review, 2026-09-06, which closed that bead as not-a-bug. This is the fragility that made it not-a-bug, written down so it is not broken by accident.

WHY THE STALE MEASUREMENT IS SAFE TODAY. maybeShowPackDiscoveryNotice() has exactly one call site, the build branch (content.js:8067), where the count element is empty and sitting on its 58px min-width floor. Every other bar child is fixed-px and flex-shrink:0, and the bar is nowrap, so min-content equals max-content. The notice is therefore measured while the host is at its NARROWEST, which is the notice's TALLEST. The host width only grows from there, so the notice can only unwrap, so packNoticeChromePx is always an UPPER bound. The cap over-subtracts and never under-subtracts, and the panel cannot overflow.

WHAT BREAKS IT. Two changes flip that upper bound into an under-estimate and produce real overflow:
1. Localizing the i18n dict, particularly 'of' and 'noMatch'. The count is min-width 58px plus nowrap, so it is content-sized, not fixed. The reviewer measured the host growing 480 to 486.03px in plain English just by navigating to '999 of 999'. With a plausible German pair the notice height moved 46.594 to 31.188 after measurement, with no resize at all, purely from typing in the find box.
2. Moving the maybeShowPackDiscoveryNotice() call out of the build branch, so the notice can first appear while a search is already active and the bar is already wide.

CORRECTING TWO THINGS ON THE RECORD, both repeated in earlier beads and wrong:
- The bar is NOT a row of fixed-px controls. .oc-count is min-width plus nowrap, i.e. content-sized.
- The English notice does NOT fit on one line. At 12px/1.4 one line is 31.19px, two is 46.59px. The shipped 46.594px measurement IS two lines at the natural 480px host; it only unwraps above about 645px.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A comment at the packNoticeChromePx declaration (around content.js:1149-1157) states the invariant: measured at minimum bar width, therefore an upper bound, therefore safe.
- A test fails if the notice is ever measured while the bar is wider than its floor.
- No re-measurement machinery added. The invariant is the fix; the guard just keeps it true.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. No behaviour changed; oculist-2mx already adjudicated this not-a-bug, and the deliverable is the written-down invariant plus a guard. Comment at the packNoticeChromePx declaration (content.js:1159-1176) and one test in pack_discovery_notice.test.js. Invariant confirmed to still hold exactly as described: the single call site in window.__ocToggle()'s build branch fires before any search, with .oc-count on its 58px floor, so the bar is at its narrowest and the notice at its tallest, making packNoticeChromePx an upper bound. Guard mechanism: after the notice appears, assert .oc-count is still empty and its rendered width equals its computed min-width within 1px. Indirect by necessity, and the reviewer verified the two things that make it sound. First, the synchronicity argument is true: the build branch is a plain synchronous run with no await, rAF or microtask boundary between the getBoundingClientRect() and the notice becoming visible, and Playwright is out-of-process so waitForSelector cannot resolve mid-task; nothing in that window can shrink the count, so the only error direction is a spurious failure, never a spurious pass. Second, the isolated-world claim is correct, verified by probe: a page.addInitScript() patch of Element.prototype.getBoundingClientRect counted 0 calls, so a main-world hook genuinely cannot reach the content script. The reviewer noted a direct hook was still reachable another way, since createPackedFixtureExtension() already rewrites the fixture's content.js; worth knowing but not a gap. Both documented break scenarios were mutation-tested, which the implementer had only done for one. Scenario 2, the dangerous state it actually produces, is cleanly detected: 7 pass and the guard is the ONLY failure. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD, both found by the reviewer and both now fixed in the comment. (a) .oc-count IS flex-shrink:0 like every other bar child; what sets it apart is that it is content-sized (min-width plus nowrap), not its shrink behaviour. (b) The bead's own text is internally inconsistent about scenario 1: localizing 'of'/'noMatch' does NOT invert the bound. A longer count widens the bar, which unwraps the notice SHORTER (the bead's own 46.594 to 31.188 numbers), so the stale value remains an upper bound and merely becomes more conservative. Only moving the call site inverts it, by recording a short unwrapped notice that then wraps taller once the search is cleared and the bar returns to its floor. The comment now says this, and the guard covers exactly that case. Full suite 321/321.

title: Deferred-mount playground effects get only partial scroll-dissolve coverage
description:
Measured by the oculist-uc1 reviewer, 2026-09-06. A STRICT IMPROVEMENT on what came before, not a regression - these effects had zero coverage until uc1. Filed because 'every effect inherits the dissolve' is only partly true, and the gap should be written down rather than assumed away.

oculist-uc1 moved the arming into rect() so every effect inherits the scroll dissolve. armScrollDissolve's onScroll sets settled = true and removes its listener when it fires. Anything an effect mounts AFTER that point is therefore never dissolved, and lands at the stale rect the dissolve was meant to prevent.

MEASURED: scrolling 120ms into matchstrike dissolved the 2 nodes that were live, and the effect then mounted 8 more at the stale position. Same shape for comet.

AFFECTED, the effects that mount inside a later setTimeout: fxMatchstrike, fxComet, fxStamp, fxInkbloom, fxScanline, fxEmberignite.

NOT A LEAK: they self-clean at the effect's own timeout, so nothing accumulates. The symptom is purely visual, a few nodes appearing at the wrong place after a scroll.

FIX DIRECTION: rather than un-setting settled, the cheaper shape is probably for mount() to check whether the current run has already dissolved and refuse to mount, or mount hidden. That keeps one decision point instead of teaching six effects to check.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Scrolling mid-flight through any of the six named effects leaves no node at a stale position.
- The five effects verified in uc1 still dissolve and still leave no scroll listener behind.
- No effect mounts nodes after its own run has been dissolved.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. One decision point, as the bead steered: armScrollDissolve's onScroll sets dissolved on the run's OWN currentRunEls array object, and mount() early-returns when it sees that flag. No effect function was touched. Run identity works because rect() hands out a fresh array per run and runEffect() is synchronous (clearFx(); eff.run(rect())), so the flag self-resets and cannot leak between runs. Measured by the reviewer, max .fx count after a mid-flight scroll, pre to post: matchstrike 8 to 0, stamp 7 to 1, comet 6 plus a late burst to 0 late, inkbloom 6 to 1 to 0, scanline 2 to 2, emberignite 5 to 5. Every post-fix residual is at or below the mid-flight count, i.e. original nodes fading through the 240ms dissolve, never a new mount. Falsifiability confirmed independently in both directions on isolated copies: pre-fix FAIL with 8 nodes mounted after the dissolve, post-fix PASS with 0. The uc1 five (batflight, arrowshot, reanimate, vineswing, foottap) still dissolve to 0 with a scroll-listener delta of 0; still 1 ambient listener after all 11 effects complete and after 30 rapid matchstrike re-fires. No-scroll path is byte-identical in behaviour, peak and final .fx counts unchanged for all 11 effects; the guard is unreachable without a scroll. A 45-effect sweep with a mid-flight scroll produced zero page errors and zero residual nodes. Two corrections to the bead's own list: fxScanline AND fxEmberignite both mount everything synchronously and never had this defect, so the real deferred-mount set is matchstrike, comet, stamp, inkbloom only. The adversarial overlapping-run case was checked explicitly: the feared 'effects stop working after a scroll' regression does NOT exist, a new effect fired after a dissolve mounts normally at the correct rect. The mirror case does remain and is unchanged by this diff, filed as a follow-up. Occlusion dirtiness on five of the six is pre-existing, identical numbers at HEAD and after; filed separately. Full suite 320/320.

title: effects-playground: 6 effects mutate raw page state (body transform/mark color/article innerHTML) outside the mount()/rect() dissolve foundation
description:
Found while implementing oculist-uc1 (foundation-level scroll-dissolve for effects-playground.html, via rect()/mount()).

Every fx* function calls mount() at least once, so every effect gets at least partial scroll-dissolve coverage from the uc1 fix. But 6 of the 45 fx* functions ALSO mutate real page state outside any .fx-classed, mount()-tracked overlay element, via addRestorer()'s revert-on-cleanup mechanism -- that state is NOT tracked by currentRunEls and does not dissolve/revert early on scroll:

- fxZoompunch: document.body.animate() scale zoom, transformOrigin computed once at fire time (document-space Y already scroll-corrected via + window.scrollY, so this specific one is largely self-immune to vertical scroll already).
- fxDepthdive: document.body.animate() perspective rotateX/rotateY tilt, same transformOrigin pattern as fxZoompunch.
- fxStamp: a brief (130ms) document.body.animate() shake, self-clears almost immediately regardless of scroll.
- fxLetterwave: sets #match's own text color to transparent while its letter-span overlay plays; not position-dependent, so scroll doesn't make this specific mutation "stale" the way a position:fixed rect does.
- fxScramble: same #match color-hide pattern as fxLetterwave.
- fxShockwave: wraps words of the host <article> in place and animates them via transform (real in-flow content, not position:fixed) -- article.innerHTML is swapped back via addRestorer. Because the wrapped words are normal in-flow content, they scroll together with the match, so their relative geometry (and thus the shockwave's per-word direction/magnitude, computed once from cx/cy) is actually unaffected by a pure vertical scroll -- this one looks structurally scroll-resistant already, not just uncovered.

None of these looked like the same "pinned to a stale viewport rect" bug oculist-uc1 targets -- each either self-corrects within a short fixed timeout regardless of scroll, or (letterwave/scramble/shockwave) isn't position:fixed/viewport-anchored in the first place. Verified by inspection only, not by a dedicated scroll test for each of the 6.

Filed as a follow-up rather than fixed in oculist-uc1 because Chris's decision for that bead was scoped to "the shared baseStyle()/rect() foundation," and these 6 effects' extra page-mutation pieces sit outside that foundation by construction (they don't go through baseStyle()/mount() at all for this part).

Suggested next step: someone should make the call on whether any of these 6 actually need scroll-awareness (my read is probably not, given the self-correcting/scroll-resistant reasoning above), or whether it's just worth a comment in each function saying so explicitly so a future reader doesn't have to re-derive it.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. The call was made by measurement rather than inspection, which is what this bead asked for, and the answer is that NONE of the six needed a fix. The deliverable is six one-line comments naming why each is scroll-safe, plus raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js as the harness that establishes it. Measured 12/12 PASS, each effect on both a control and a scrolled-mid-flight arm on a fresh page.reload(), plus 3/3 REFUSED. The harness was proven falsifiable 3 of 3 on isolated copies, one mutation per family: deleting restore() from fxZoompunch's 900ms cleanup FAILS both arms with a stranded transform-origin; making fxLetterwave's colour restore conditional on dissolved FAILS ONLY the scrolled arm while the control passes, which is the strongest evidence that the scroll arm is live rather than vacuous; dropping article.innerHTML from fxShockwave's restorer FAILS both. The highest-value question, whether the just-landed oculist-ucs mount() refusal can orphan an addRestorer cleanup, is answered NO with a non-vacuous reproduction: refusal genuinely engages (control mounts 1/1/7 nodes for zoompunch/depthdive/stamp, 0 after a scroll at 60ms) and in that same refused run the body transform still reverts to none, with 0 .fx and 0 body animations. Mechanism confirmed in source: restorers are drained only by each effect's own unconditional setTimeout and by clearFx(); armScrollDissolve's onScroll sets dissolved and calls dissolveEffect, and never touches restorers. All six comments verified accurate against the code, each naming a concrete mechanism (document-space origin with + scrollY, position-independent colour hide, in-flow words, self-clearing timeout) rather than over-claiming the way the ucs comment did. Diff is 24 insertions and 0 deletions, comment-only, six function bodies untouched, no-scroll path untouched. Full suite 320/320. Two artifacts noted and filed rather than fixed: the empty style attribute (oculist-g46, confirmed benign and correctly P4, though the reviewer found it is non-deterministic for zoompunch/depthdive and partly observation-induced) and fxStamp's body shake continuing after a dissolve.

title: vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle asserts without waiting, so it flakes independently of load
description:
Isolated during the oculist-8qq investigation, 2026-09-06. This is the ONE flaky file in that bead's set that does not fit the contention story, which is why it is worth separating out.

Every other failure oculist-8qq measured was the same shape: a waitForCondition or waitForSelector exhausting the fixed 5000ms POLL_TIMEOUT under four-way browser scheduling load. Those thin out as concurrency drops.

This file is different. Its failure is a bare assertion with no wait behind it at all, and the test's own comment documents that no-wait as an intentional assumption. That matches the separate data point recorded earlier in oculist-8qq: it flaked once when run entirely alone, then passed four times. A file that flakes in isolation is not being starved by its neighbours; it is asserting on state that is not guaranteed to have settled yet.

WHY IT MATTERS SEPARATELY: as long as this file sits in the flaky set, it makes the concurrency numbers look worse than they are and muddies the decision on the systemic tradeoff. Fixing it is narrow and does not depend on that decision.

FIRST STEP: read the comment that documents the no-wait assumption and find out whether it was ever true. The fix is probably to await the state transition the assertion depends on rather than to add a sleep.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The assertion waits for the condition it depends on rather than assuming it has already happened.
- The file passes repeatedly in isolation, and the no-wait comment is either justified by evidence or removed.
- No new sleep. A fixed delay would convert this into the same POLL_TIMEOUT-shaped fragility as the rest of the set.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on the second attempt. Root cause: popup.js attaches its change listeners only after an await on chrome.storage.sync, while openPopup waited only for the control to EXIST, which is true from HTML parse time. A change event driven at an unwired control is dropped permanently, so the assertion read the old value. The first attempt polled each assertion's outcome and was failed: since the event was dropped, the outcome never arrives, so it only converted an instant wrong-value failure into a 10s timeout. Measured A/B by the reviewer, 18 runs per arm: outcome polling 7 pass, readiness wait 18 pass. The fix waits once for popup readiness in openPopup, via a new shared waitForPopupReady helper keyed on the status text leaving its Checking placeholder. Verified both directions: HEAD fails 4 of 12 six-way concurrent runs, all wrong-value; the fix passes 24 of 24 concurrent and 24 of 24 in isolation. Assertions restored byte-identical to HEAD, so nothing was loosened. Full suite 320/320. The reviewer caught the helper comment overclaiming that every listener sits above the readiness point, which is false for the site toggle on the early-return paths; corrected before commit.

title: __ocDestroy leaves the auto-scroll listeners attached on a page that never stops scrolling
description:
Found by the reviewer on oculist-z8n, 2026-09-06. Bounded and not user-visible; filed so it is not rediscovered.

oculist-z8n replaced the flat 800ms auto-scroll suppression with a scrollend listener plus a scroll listener that re-arms a 300ms grace timer. clearAutoScrollFlag removes both, and it runs on scrollend or when scroll events stop.

__ocDestroy() does not clear autoScrollTimer. It did not clear the old 800ms timer either, so this is not a regression - but the shape changed. Before, the stranded thing was a single timer that fired once. Now, on a page that scrolls CONTINUOUSLY and forever (an infinite auto-scroller, a stuck momentum scroll), the scroll listener keeps re-arming the grace timer, so one listener and one timer stay attached after teardown.

WHY IT IS BOUNDED: a reopen calls triggerAutoScrollFlag, which removes both listeners by reference before re-adding, so they do not accumulate. The cost is one idle listener, not a growing set.

FIX DIRECTION: have __ocDestroy call clearAutoScrollFlag, which already both clears the timer and removes both listeners. Check the other teardown paths take it too.

DONE-CRITERIA
- After __ocDestroy on a continuously scrolling page, no auto-scroll scroll/scrollend listener remains and no timer is pending.
- The oculist-z8n tests in test/beacon_survives_long_smooth_scroll.test.js still pass, including the reverted-fix red check.
- node --test passes in full.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. One line in __ocDestroy: clearAutoScrollFlag(), which already clears the timer and removes both listeners. __ocDestroy is the single teardown funnel (three call sites), so the bead's 'check other teardown paths' is satisfied by construction. New test drives continuous re-targeted smooth scrolls so native scrollend never fires, then asserts the timer is null after destroy; reviewer re-proved it red 4 of 4 on revert. The reviewer also corrected the implementer's own account of the assertion: it asserts null, not an advancing timer id, so the global-id concern does not apply. The added __ocTest getter is one member on a namespace that already ships with about 66 of them, unconditionally, and worklist_storage.test.js already asserts it is invisible from the main world; the reviewer confirmed that isolation in a real browser. z8n's reproduction test verified still red when the z8n fix is reverted, so it was not blunted. Residual test weaknesses filed.

title: beacon_survives_long_smooth_scroll timing literals ignore TIMEOUT_SCALE
description:
Raised by the reviewer on oculist-z8n, 2026-09-06. Not a defect today - it held over six runs, three of them under full-suite contention - but it is the likeliest future flake in that file.

test/beacon_survives_long_smooth_scroll.test.js uses two hardcoded timing literals that do NOT respond to OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE the way the rest of the suite does:
- test 1 asserts the beacon is still alive at appearedAt + 1900, against a getBeaconDuration of 2100. Measured headroom after the 30ms poll interval and two page.evaluate round-trips is only ~140-170ms.
- test 2 waits 600ms for the user-scroll fade.

DO NOT just multiply both by TIMEOUT_SCALE. The two ends do not scale the same way and that is the trap:
- The 600ms window is a timeout and should grow on a slow machine.
- The 1900ms is a deadline sitting INSIDE a 2100ms product lifetime that is real wall-clock and does not grow. Scaling it up pushes the assertion past the beacon's own expiry and turns a passing test red for the wrong reason.

The real exposure in test 1 is the round-trip cost eating the 140ms of headroom, not the 1900 itself. So the fix is more likely to be reducing measurement overhead, or asserting on a recorded appearance timestamp rather than on wall clock at assert time, than scaling a constant.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Both tests still pass at OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE=1 and at a raised scale.
- Test 1 still goes red when the oculist-z8n fix is reverted - re-check that, since it is the reproduction case and must not be blunted.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. The two literals were treated on their own terms, which was the bead's whole point: the 1900ms deadline sits inside a real-wall-clock 2100ms product lifetime and was NOT scaled, and the 600ms fade timeout was scaled by TIMEOUT_SCALE. The deadline's real exposure, round-trip overhead eating its ~140ms of headroom, was removed by collapsing a 30ms Node-side poll plus a separate aliveness evaluate into one in-page waitForFunction that snapshots aliveness at the same tick it crosses the deadline. Reviewer traced the predicate for all three cases (alive, already faded, never drawn) and confirmed a dead beacon still yields a clean AssertionError rather than a Playwright timeout, then proved it: reverting the z8n fix turns test 1 red as a real assertion in 2863ms. Both scales pass (1 and 3). git diff on extension is empty, so the test-only constraint held.

title: Foot Tap and Point: REACH_INWARD mixes viewBox units with px, so GAP 12 delivers ~23px
description:
Found at the second review of oculist-1ta.5. In fxFootTap (artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html, outer repo) REACH_INWARD (~line 5473) is computed in viewBox units but consumed as px (~5478, ~5480) without the scale factor (0.903 at font 24). It over-reserves about 9px, so the stated GAP of 12 yields an actual fingertip approach of 23.5px at the held point and 20.9px at overshoot. Safe direction (never under-reserves), but the point stops further from the word than intended, which costs anchor legibility.

Fix: multiply REACH_INWARD by scale before adding it to the placement, then re-run node occlusion-sweep.js foottap (must stay 96/96 clean) and re-measure the held-point fingertip gap at 900x700/f24 (target 12-14px).

Also: no screenshot captures the mirrored left-side landing; add one by forcing a right-edge match in a throwaway page.
close_reason:
REACH_INWARD and REACH_OUTWARD are both scaled now; the latter is the same unit bug in the same sideRight.fits/sideLeft.fits chain, and the reviewer confirmed it in scope rather than creep, with side selection identical across the full 8x12 grid (96 right before, 96 right after, zero flips).

MEASURED, reviewer reproducing it independently with animations paused and seeked in 5ms steps: full extension went 20.25px to 13.97px, held pose 23.51px to 17.23px. No unscaled term remains: the observed shift matches the predicted (1-scale) correction to within 0.01px, and the whole VB-to-px chain was walked (sideRight.x, .fits, sideLeft, figLeft/figTop, fpWorldX/fpWorldY, MOTION_*), with LEG_LIFT correctly staying unscaled since it is an in-SVG translate.

CRITERION 3 IS NOT LITERALLY MET AND THAT IS ACCEPTED. The 12-14px target was written before anyone had measured the overshoot/held distinction. GAP binds at FULL EXTENSION, per the code's own comment and per the geometry: REACH_INWARD is dimensioned off minX, sampled with the overshoot arm length at every angle, so the floor is GAP + 2*scale = 13.81px and the real overshoot lands at 13.97px, inside target. The held pose then retracts 3.82 viewBox units by design (ARM_PEAK 99 to ARM_SWEEP 90, scaleX 1.1 to 1.0), which is 3.45px, giving 17.24px. That is arithmetic, not a residual bug. Against the bead's actual complaint, that the point stopped too far from the word and cost anchor legibility, this is a 27% improvement. The implementer reported the miss rather than tuning the constant to fit, which was the right call.

Criterion 2 is a real safety check here and it holds: over-reserving was the safe direction, so scaling down moves the finger toward the word. foottap stays 96/96 clean with maxPixels=0, and that number is trustworthy rather than a lower bound, because fxFootTap's two mount() calls are both synchronous and its only setTimeout is the final element removal, so oculist-e2w does not apply. Gates verified: fixed-position pointer-events-none nodes, no reads or writes of #match or document.body, WAAPI only, and cleanupAndAssert clean in all 96 scenarios. Both screenshots reviewed, including the forced mirrored-left landing.

title: Reanimation Jolt forearms are invisible at natural size
description:
Found at review of oculist-1ta.3. In fxReanimate (artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html, outer repo) the two stiff forearms are COAT fill on a COAT body, so at 900x700/font 24 only the two pale fist circles register and the arms themselves vanish. The bust still reads as a person (squared head, brow band, eyes, shoulders), but the stiff-armed rise cue is carried entirely by the fists.

Fix: give the forearms a distinct mid tone or a light edge on the upper-left-lit side so they separate from the coat, matching the three-tone cel convention used on the bat and archer.

DONE: settle screenshot at 900x700/f24 and 1280x900/f24 shows two forearms as separate forms; node occlusion-sweep.js reanimate still 96/96 clean.
close_reason:
The forearms now read as separate forms, and the cause was geometry rather than palette as the first review established. Both arms were re-angled to run from the shoulder seam at y=45/46 up and outward to a tip at y=27-31, so since the coat trapezoid only exists for y>=45 the distal ~20 units sit outside the coat by construction. Fist radius went 6 to 4 and recentred on the new tip so it caps the shaft instead of swallowing it.

MEASURED, reviewer reproducing it independently: the colour-only attempt moved 52 pixels in a 35x9 bbox; this moves 479-493 pixels in a 48x32 bbox at both required scenarios. The reviewer took its own settle screenshots at 900x700/f24 and 1280x900/f24 at deviceScaleFactor 1 and confirmed two straight dark bars leaving the shoulders and ending in pale fists, distinguishable from the pre-change trapezoid blob AT 1:1 rather than only under zoom.

PALETTE RE-JUDGED AND CHANGED. The first attempt's ARM_BASE sat brighter than the coat's entire ramp (rel-lum .126 against COAT_HI .0840). It is now ARM_SHADOW .0131 / ARM_BASE .0316 / ARM_HI .0664, all at or below COAT_HI, with ARM_BASE at 12.2:1 against the page background where roughly 85% of the bar actually sits. At the seam the arm and coat are near-identical in luminance and separation comes from the COAT_OUTLINE stroke, which is acceptable over a 2-3 unit overlap.

OCCLUSION CHECKED BEYOND THE SWEEP, since the figure grew upward. fxReanimate has only right and left landings, with an explicit never-above/below comment, so upward growth cannot grow toward the match. The figure's bbox did not actually grow: the head already reached y=4 and the old fist already reached x=0, so the REACH_INWARD/REACH_OUTWARD inputs are unchanged. The reviewer also forced three left landings and sampled the whole timeline, finding zero pixels inside the match rect, and measured minimum horizontal clearance of 12.0px across the 96 right landings.

THE POSE CHANGED, AND THAT IS A JUDGEMENT FOR CHRIS, not a defect. The silhouette now reads as both arms raised and outward in a V with fists at ear height, where the epic's copy describes a stiff-armed rise held out in front. Worth knowing: the OLD geometry never delivered the forward reach either, it read as arms at the sides. What survives is the stiff quality, both arms rigid straight bars with no elbow bend, and in context with the electrode posts and the two-step sit-up the reviewer read it as a body jerked upright with its arms thrown up, which is coherent for a Reanimation Jolt. If the forward reach is wanted specifically, reopen and the arms need to point along the x axis rather than up.

G6 improved rather than regressed: the diff touches no arc or glow element and shifts weight onto the figure, so it reads less like the shipped Lightning.

Two measured-false claims the new comment introduced were corrected before commit: BOOT_HI does exceed LEG_BASE (.0411 vs .0358), so the real rule is that the boot ramp stays below the leg ramp's TOP; and the 38x10/73px figure was a before/after diff rather than a visible extent.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
RUN STOPPED 2026-09-09 at the 4-hour wall clock. This bead FAILED REVIEW ONCE and the retry was not started, because the fix it needs is a geometry change requiring visual iteration and there was not time to see it through. The partial work IS committed; the bead stays open.

  var coatD = 'M 10 90 L 15 45 L 55 45 L 60 90 Z';
