title: Occlusion sweep harness: three small gaps found at review of oculist-1ta.16
description:
Found by the reviewer of oculist-1ta.16; none blocked the pass. File: artifacts/prototypes/occlusion-sweep.js (outer repo).

1. Lines ~28-29 claim the script exits before touching any effect when the control fails. It does not: main() sets exitCode=1 and still sweeps every effect, printing CLEAN per effect from a measurement path already proven broken. Either return early after a control failure or fix the header comment; returning early is the right one.
2. Line ~286: the sample loop steps t in 40ms up to maxEnd, so a maxEnd that is not a multiple of 40 leaves the tail unsampled (arrowshot 2150 -> last sample 2120). Append maxEnd itself as a final sample.
3. Lines ~81-83 hard-code the absolute playwright path, so the harness breaks in any other checkout. Resolve it relative to __dirname (../../repo/node_modules/playwright).

Also record in the header: the setTimeout no-op during runEffect() would hide artwork from any effect that stages elements on a timer, and getAnimations() seeking cannot pause an rAF-driven effect; both would read as a false clean. Every effect in this epic is WAAPI-only by convention, so this is a documentation note, not a defect.

DONE: the three edits made, header updated, node occlusion-sweep.js batflight arrowshot still exits 0 with 96/96 clean each.
close_reason:
All three gaps fixed and the header is finally accurate. Item 1: either control failing now returns before the effect loop, verified by fault injection on both paths (exit 1, no effect section, browser closed). Item 2: the sample loop appends maxEnd only when the 40ms stepping did not already land on it, so an exact multiple is not double-sampled; this removed a recorded FALSE CLEAN, with inkbloom flipping to samples=7, atTime=230ms, maxPixels=47, dirty=96, which is the ink drop landing on the match centre. Item 3: the playwright path resolves from __dirname, verified from a relocated checkout.

FAILED REVIEW TWICE, both times for the same thing: the WAAPI-only header was corrected into a NEW inaccuracy. Round 1 denied that any effect stages artwork in a setTimeout body (fourteen do). Round 2 fixed the bullet but left the paragraph above it asserting the opposite of its own bullet. The /goal stop condition fired, so the orchestrator corrected the preamble directly and stopped rather than dispatching a third attempt.

That edit has now been reviewed independently and PASSES on every claim: the preamble states the assumption already does not hold for setTimeout and holds for rAF only because nothing uses it (grep confirms zero requestAnimationFrame in the playground); fourteen is exact; matchstrike's 400ms body really does mount band, glow and six embers, with the glow at r.left-4/r.top-4/r.width+8/r.height+8; the hook returns 0 without ever calling realSetTimeout, so timers are dropped rather than deferred; and every round-1 and round-2 phrase is gone from the file. batflight and arrowshot are described with the narrow true claim, cleanup-only setTimeout at DUR+100, rather than the false 'no setTimeout at all' that two earlier briefs propagated.

Acceptance criterion holds: node occlusion-sweep.js batflight arrowshot exits 0 at 96/96 clean each. The measurement limitation the header now records is tracked as oculist-e2w.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
ESCALATION from the oculist-aun reviewer, 2026-09-09. Item 2 of this bead (a maxEnd that is not a multiple of 40 leaves the tail unsampled) is not a small gap. It is the sole cause of a recorded FALSE CLEAN.

PROVEN, not inferred. The sample loop is for (let t = 0; t <= maxEnd; t += 40) and never clamps to maxEnd. inkbloom's maxEnd is 230, so samples run 0..200 and t=230, the frame where the ink drop lands on the match centre, is never taken. The reviewer patched ONLY that (append maxEnd as a final sample) in a scratch copy and ran it against the pre-eke playground: inkbloom flipped from CLEAN to ISSUES FOUND, maxPixels=47, dirty=96, atTime=230ms. 47px is about a 7px circle, i.e. exactly the drop.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. oculist-aun opened by treating inkbloom's CLEAN as a real result that distinguished it from five dirty siblings. It was a measurement artifact. An effect that deterministically drops an element onto the match centre measured clean for months because the harness stopped sampling 30ms early.

This bead's own trailing note already anticipated the second half of the same problem (the setTimeout no-op hiding timer-staged artwork, reading as a false clean). That half is now confirmed too and is filed separately as oculist-hgt.

No new bead for inkbloom: fixing item 2 here is the fix.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
RUN STOPPED HERE 2026-09-09: this bead failed review TWICE, which is a /goal stop condition. The work IS committed on branch goal/1ta-followups-and-two-prototypes, but the bead is deliberately NOT closed, because no reviewer passed the final state.

WHAT IS DONE AND VERIFIED GOOD (do not redo):

- Item 1, the early return. Either control failing now closes the browser, prints a FINAL block with control status and an 'effect sweep skipped' line, and exits before the effect loop. Both control paths verified by fault injection: exit 1 with no === <effect> === section printed, no leaked handle. Both controls short-circuit, since a dead neutralization makes deferred-mount numbers noise for the same reason a broken pixel control does.
- Item 2, the unsampled tail. sampleTimes is built by the old 40ms stepping, then maxEnd is appended only when the last step did not already land on it, so an exact multiple of 40 is not double-sampled. VERIFIED: inkbloom flips from the recorded false CLEAN to samples=7, atTime=230ms, maxPixels=47, dirty=96, which is the ink drop landing on the match centre. batflight maxEnd=2080 gives samples=53 with no double sample; arrowshot now samples=55 and includes its 2150 tail. Float jitter in maxEnd traced and ruled benign: downward wobble still appends, upward wobble on an exact multiple costs one redundant screenshot 4.5e-13ms later and changes no result.
- Item 3, the playwright path, now path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'repo', 'node_modules', 'playwright'), verified by running from a relocated directory through a symlinked ../../repo.
- Acceptance criterion holds: node occlusion-sweep.js batflight arrowshot exits 0 with 96/96 clean each. All five reference numbers reproduce exactly (matchstrike 9356, scanline 1560, emberignite 819, stamp 4137, comet 1031).

WHY IT FAILED TWICE, both times the same class of error: the header was corrected into a NEW inaccuracy.

- Round 1 claimed no effect stages artwork inside a setTimeout body, framed the risk as hypothetical, and ended 'Neither currently applies.' Fourteen fx* functions do exactly that; fxMatchstrike mounts a glow div sized to the match plus six embers from inside a 400ms timer.
- Round 2 fixed the bullet but left the paragraph introducing it saying 'That is true of every effect here as of oculist-hgt', contradicting its own bullet four lines below, and still framed it as recorded 'for whoever adds the next effect'.

THE ORCHESTRATOR THEN FIXED THAT PREAMBLE DIRECTLY rather than dispatching a third attempt, since the stop condition had fired. It now says the WAAPI-only assumption ALREADY DOES NOT HOLD for setTimeout and holds for rAF only because no effect uses it yet. node --check passes and batflight/arrowshot still exit 0 at 96/96. That edit is UNREVIEWED, which is the only reason this bead is still open.

WHAT A REVIEWER NEEDS TO DO TO CLOSE IT: read the WAAPI-ONLY ASSUMPTION section against effects-playground.html and confirm every claim in it is true. Nothing else is outstanding.

title: Hat base tone is only 15 pure pixels at the floor size
description:
From the oculist-1ta.19 review. Not a defect; a thin margin worth knowing about.

HAT_BASE measures 15 pure pixels at archerH 78 against HAT_HI 21 and HAT_SHADOW 10, on a hat that owns 442 pixels total. The done-criteria asked for meaningfully more than the old 12, and 15 clears it by three pixels.

The structural cause named in oculist-1ta.18 is genuinely gone: the tones were clipped ellipses that squeezed the base to 12, and they are now wedges built from the crown triangle's own vertices, so nothing can squeeze them. All three tones are visible in the render. Round 1's taller crown gave 37, and cutting the apex from 30 units to 13 to stop it reading as a party hat cost most of that back, which was the right trade.

So this is a consequence of a deliberate choice, not a mistake. Worth revisiting only if the hat is reopened for another reason, or if Chris looks at it and finds the base tone reads as absent.

FIX IF WANTED: widen the middle undrawn strip between the two wedges. Note the trap recorded in the code: the strip is itself a triangle sharing the crown's apex, so its area shrinks with crown height even at a constant width fraction, and an even split zeroes HAT_SHADOW because the right wedge's edges sit on the crown's shallower hypotenuse.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Base tone comfortably visible at 78px, sampled in the render.
- Crown still reads as a low angular peak, not a party hat.
- Occlusion sweep still zero at STRIKE_GAP 8, and the cliff re-probed since hat geometry moves it.
close_reason:
NO GEOMETRY CHANGE, and that is the answer rather than an omission. This bead was explicitly conditional: a thin margin worth knowing about, to be revisited only if the base tone reads as absent. It does not.

CRITERION 1 MET, established by counterfactual rather than by eyeballing a magnification. The reviewer repainted the crown in the live DOM with the base band eliminated (shadow wedge extended left to meet the highlight) and measured the difference at 1:1: 56 pixels change by a mean luma delta of 23/255, max 32. That is well above JND for adjacent regions and plainly visible side by side. So the 15-pure-pixel count is a conservative floor; the tone's real visual footprint is roughly 4x that once antialiased blends carry it.

COUNTS, measured independently with point-in-polygon attribution at archerH 78: crown triangle alone is HAT_BASE 14, HAT_HI 0, HAT_SHADOW 10; whole hat is 15/21/10, reproducing the bead's figures and confirming they are whole-hat aggregates. The 15th base pixel is in the back brim, so the implementer's crown-only 15 was off by one, immaterially.

CRITERION 2 MET: the crown is 13 units on a 36-unit base and the forward beak's vertical run of 16 units exceeds it, so at 1:1 in page context it reads as a low angular bycocket rather than a cone.

CRITERION 3 MET BY MEASUREMENT, not by construction. arrowshot is 96/96 clean at STRIKE_GAP 8. The cliff was re-probed on a patched copy outside the repo: STRIKE_GAP 7 gives 94/96 with 2 dirty at 1280x900 fonts 25 and 26, maxPixels 1, exit 1. So the cliff sits exactly one pixel below 8, where the source comment says it does.

THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS TESTED AND REJECTED ON EVIDENCE. Moving the shadow wedge's inner base point from 37 to 41 widens the middle strip and takes HAT_BASE from 15 to 19, but takes HAT_SHADOW from 10 to 2. That empirically reproduces the trap recorded in the code, where an even split zeroes HAT_SHADOW because the right wedge's edges sit on the crown's shallower hypotenuse. Net loss. A real gain needs crown height, which was already rejected as the party-hat trade.

DISCOVERED: oculist-uxa0. The crown's OWN highlight wedge has zero pure-pixel survival at floor size; all 21 HAT_HI pixels come from the front brim sharing the fill. So oculist-1ta.19's 'all three tones are visible' held only by counting the brim. Does not undermine criterion 1, which is about the base tone specifically.

title: Front brim point of the bycocket does not read at 78px
description:
Flagged by the implementer against itself and confirmed independently by the reviewer in oculist-1ta.17.

artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:4020 (brimFrontD) — the front brim point renders in the shadow tone AND lands directly against the same-hued bow limb, so it neither reads as a crisp point nor separates from the bow. At the 78px floor the plume and the back brim flip carry the whole read, and the silhouette says 'brimmed hat with a flip' rather than specifically 'bycocket'.

He does read as the folklore archer, so this is polish, not a failure of the bead.

FIX: give the front point a lighter tone than the crown's shadow, or 2-3 more units of clearance from the bow limb, or both.

RELATED, same bead, same file: the hat's BASE tone is nearly squeezed out by its two clip ellipses at the floor size — 12 pure pixels at archerH 78 against 75 highlight and 113 shadow (72/183/269 at 112). Above the zero-pixel failure mode this epic keeps hitting, but thin enough to be worth widening while the hat is open.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The front point is distinguishable from both the crown shadow and the bow limb at 78px, sampled in the render.
- Hat base tone has meaningfully more than 12 pure pixels at 78px.
- Occlusion sweep still zero, including the wide 1280x900 coverage.
close_reason: Absorbed into oculist-1ta.19, which redrew the same forms. Front beak now separates from both the crown shadow (hard outlined HAT_HI against HAT_SHADOW) and the bow limb (zero overlap across all 15 shared rows). Hat base tone is 15 pure px at archerH 78, up from 12, with the clip-ellipse cause structurally removed - thin, and flagged to Chris rather than claimed as comfortable

title: Arrow reads less planted since STRIKE_GAP went to 12
description:
Raised from 6 to 12 in oculist-1ta.11 to clear a 1-2px occlusion regression at font sizes 22-26. That fixed the occlusion, but the reviewer's own read is that the strike is measurably softened: the tip now rests about 6px further out and there is a visible page-background gap between the arrowhead and the highlight rect, where at 6 the tip kissed the edge.

It still reads as stuck in the page aiming at the word (the head overlaps the outer ring, the shaft angles away, nothing floats), so this is a quality nit for Chris to judge by eye, not a defect.

The obvious move is an intermediate value. 8 and 10 were NOT tested and must not be adopted without a full sweep: the failure is size-dependent and only showed at font sizes 22-26, at a wide 1280x900, at t=1400.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Whatever value is chosen, the occlusion sweep is zero across font sizes 20-30 at 1280x900 AND the other established scenarios.
- The arrowhead visibly touches or overlaps the target rings so the strike reads as planted.
- Compare before and after at 4x at both font-size 16 and 24 and judge by eye, not by the number.
notes: Commit 42ad041 refers to this bead as 'oculist-1ta.16'. That id was wrong; the sweep-coverage bead is 1ta.16 and this one is 1ta.15. The commit was already pushed when the mistake was found, so the message was left alone rather than rewriting published history.
close_reason: STRIKE_GAP 12->8, the smallest value that sweeps completely clean, per Chris's instruction to follow the recommendation. Reviewer confirmed the arrow now crosses the gold ring with its tip at the highlight edge and reads embedded rather than floating. Recorded in code that 8 sits one pixel above a cliff: 7 fails by 2px at font sizes 22-26

title: Two cosmetic misses in the Bat Flight figure
description:
Both found in the oculist-1ta.10 re-review, both non-blocking, both roughly one line. Filed rather than patched in after the review passed.

1. THE MOUTH DOES NOT RENDER. artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:3557 — the path 'M 39 51 Q 45 54 51 51' lands at y roughly 34 to 35.8px at production size, while the head's own bottom outline sits at y 35.8px. The mouth merges into the chin line and is invisible. Move it up far enough to clear the outline.

2. THE HAIR OUTLINE IS A NO-OP. :3506 — HAIR_OUTLINE '#000000' on HAIR '#0d0d0f' is a 5/255 delta, so the stroke only fattens the shape rather than defining it. Either give it a real contrast delta or drop the stroke and say why the form does not need one.

DONE-CRITERIA
- The mouth is visible as a distinct feature at production size, sampled in the render rather than judged from source.
- The hair reads as an outlined form, or the absence of an outline is deliberate and commented.
- No change to the figure's bounding box, so the occlusion guarantee is untouched. Confirm with a sweep rather than by inspection.
close_reason:
Both misses fixed, both verified in the render rather than from source.

MOUTH: moved 'M 39 51 Q 45 54 51 51' to 'M 39 48 Q 45 51 51 48'. Reviewer sampled its own pixel columns at deviceScaleFactor 1, 900x700, 24px match, with animations paused at figure opacity 1. Before, rows 43-45 read (101,97,93)/(33,28,26)/(43,26,18), one fused dark band with zero light pixels between mouth and chin. After, row 41 is pure HAIR (13,13,15), row 43 is pure SKIN (233,222,210) as a genuine light gap, row 44 is SKIN_OUTLINE. The gap holds across x=39/42/45/48/51, and it still separates at 16px, the grid's smallest font, where before it was fused. No nose or eye collision: the nose occupies rows 37-39 with one blended row between. The curve's control point still sits below its endpoints, so the expression is unchanged, just translated up 3 units.

HAIR OUTLINE: dropped rather than given contrast, and the reasoning checks out. Every outline on this figure is darker than its fill (CAPE #3b0764 / CAPE_OUTLINE #150826, SKIN #e9ded2 / SKIN_OUTLINE #2b1a12, BAT_BASE #3a2b52 / BAT_OUTLINE #0a0612, sclera stroked with SKIN_OUTLINE), so lightening HAIR for contrast would have made it the figure's only rim-light. The silhouette reads without it: one antialiased step from page to hair, and a single blend row at the hairline where it meets SKIN, SKIN_HI and SKIN_SHADE. The stroke's only measured effect was widening the band by about a row and deepening it from (13,13,15) to black. The dead HAIR_OUTLINE declaration was removed; grep confirms the only other occurrences are fxVineSwing's own separately scoped var.

BBOX UNCHANGED, measured independently over all 19 non-clipPath shapes at both 24px and 16px: minX 8.01, minY 9.62, maxX 64.08, maxY 86.52. batflight stays 96/96 clean and arrowshot 96/96, which is the behavioural gate.

Noted, not blocking: getBoundingClientRect is stroke-blind on SVG geometry in Chromium, so bbox identity alone does not prove the removed stroke left ink extent unchanged; removing a stroke can only shrink ink, and the sweep is the real gate. Also the mouth is a 1px dark line at 24px and a mid-grey antialiased line at 16px, legible but at the floor of what survives rasterising; stroke-width is the knob if a later bead wants it bolder.

title: Effect is born at the pre-scroll location if a user scroll aborts the scrollIntoView
description:
Found in the oculist-1ta.12 re-review. Cosmetic, pre-existing, and out of scope for that bead.

When a user scroll interrupts the playground's pre-fire scrollIntoView, scrollend fires early. Suppression lifts, the effect is then born at the PRE-scroll location, and it dissolves 190-315ms later. The dissolve is correct behaviour; the flicker of an effect appearing briefly in the wrong place is not.

This predates the scroll-dissolve work: the effect has always been born wherever ensureVisible's completion callback happened to fire. The dissolve just makes it visible as a brief flash rather than a beacon that stays wrong.

FIX DIRECTION: if the pre-fire scroll was aborted by the user, do not draw the effect at all rather than drawing it and immediately dissolving it. The scroll that aborted it has already invalidated the endpoint, which is the same reasoning behind the dissolve itself.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Interrupting the pre-fire scrollIntoView with a user scroll produces no visible effect at the old location.
- A normal, uninterrupted fire is unaffected and still runs its full lifetime.
close_reason:
ensureVisible now detects the OUTCOME rather than the cause. It polls the match's rect via rAF until it stops moving for two consecutive frames (bounded at 1200ms), then compares the settled top against scrollIntoView({block:'center'})'s own intended target, (innerHeight - elHeight)/2, with a 4px tolerance. Beyond that the effect is skipped. All wheel/touchstart/scrollend listeners are gone, so one check covers keyboard, scrollbar, wheel and other-JS scrolls alike.

FAILED REVIEW ONCE, on the input-listener design, and the reviewer measured both of its failure modes. False positives, the blocking one: a zero-delta wheel, a horizontal wheel, a 5px nudge and a wheel consumed by the sidebar's nested scroller each suppressed a LEGITIMATE fire while the page settled correctly. Coverage gaps: keyboard End, PageDown, ArrowDown, Space and other-JS scrollTo/scrollBy all still drew, often fully offscreen at matchTop 1309 against a 700px viewport.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT'S HEADLINE REPRODUCTION WAS NOT AN ABORT. Both the retry and the reviewer measured mouse.wheel(0, 2000) mid-flight failing to relocate the resting position at all: it and the smooth scroll bottom out at the same document limit, landing at 339 with delta 0.00 against a target of 339.14. Keyboard End and scrollTo(0,2000) move it 858px. So the original wheel-based design was aimed at a case that does not exist in this fixture. Scenario A was rebuilt on the two mechanisms that genuinely abort.

Reviewer PASS with independent measurement of both tables at a 1600ms poll window, wider than the check's own 900ms so a draw at the timeout path could not hide: coverage all peak 0 (End, Home, PageDown, ArrowDown, Space, scrollBy, scrollTo x2), false positives all peak 3. The tolerance boundary is exact and monotonic, verified by forcing offsets with scroll-margin-top: deltas 0 through 4 draw, 5 and beyond skip, and legitimate fires land at delta 0.00, so 4px is headroom rather than a knife edge. Holds under reduced-motion and CPU throttling to 20x. The settle loop moves from its second frame so it cannot exit early, skips (the safe direction) if still moving at 1200ms, adds no latency (median 538ms post-fix vs 543ms pre), and under a 2s rAF suspension defers and then draws correctly rather than hanging. The in-view fast path correctly bypasses the comparison, confirmed by a match in-band but 269px off centre still drawing.

The new prefire-scroll-abort-check.js was itself mutation-tested: TOLERANCE_PX=-1 and a mid-flight sampling mutant both make it fail, as does the pre-fix source, so it is falsifiable in both directions.

KNOWN AND ACCEPTED: a suppressed fire does not update lastKey, so Replay afterwards repeats the previous effect.

title: Archer corner can flip between fires when the match sits at viewport centre
description:
Found in the oculist-1ta.2 re-review. Cosmetic, but it touches the epic's determinism constraint, which exists so a human comparing two fires sees the same thing.

artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:3340 — the left-plan corner tie-break is Math.abs(leftEndY - launchYTop) <= Math.abs(leftEndY - launchYBottom). That is a genuine near-tie when the match sits at the viewport's vertical centre, which is exactly where ensureVisible's scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) puts it. Sub-pixel wobble can flip the archer between top-left and bottom-left across two fires.

Not an occlusion risk: both corners give identical horizontal clearance and both swept to zero occluding pixels. The re-review also measured identical full-viewport SHA1s across two fires at 12 timestamps, so it does not reproduce in practice — but the tie is real in the arithmetic.

FIX: break the tie on something that cannot wobble, e.g. prefer top-left unless the vertical leg differs by more than a pixel or two.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Twenty consecutive fires with the match at viewport centre put the archer in the same corner every time.
- Occlusion sweep still zero.
close_reason:
CLOSED BY DISPROVING THE PREMISE, not by adding a guard. The tie this bead was filed for cannot occur.

Both the reviewer and the implementer derived the closed form independently and agree: d = topLegDist - bottomLegDist = 2*mcy - vh + archerH/19. At viewport centre mcy = vh/2 + e, so d = archerH/19 + 2e, where e is ensureVisible's residual centring offset. archerH is clamped to [78, 112] and measured e stays within [-0.5, +0.39], so d is bounded away from zero BY THE ARCHER'S OWN HEIGHT. Measured across all 46 left-plan scenarios: d in [3.1053, 6.6760], closed form matching the raw comparison to 7.46e-14, predicted corner matching the rendered corner 46 of 46.

A 1px deadband was implemented first and PASSED review, then reverted on the reviewer's own analysis. It was net-negative: it moved the knife-edge from d=0 to d=1, i.e. TOWARD the operating point of d in [3.1, 6.7], cutting margin by 1px rather than adding robustness; it was documented as hysteresis while keeping no state; its branch was unreachable in all 96 grid scenarios, so 96/96 clean never exercised it; and its 0.26px justification was borrowed from a different, superseded comparison, against a measured actual wobble of 0.0px across 20 fires.

What ships instead is the proof, as a comment at the comparison. The final diff is 12 inserted comment lines and zero deletions, so the executable code is byte-identical to HEAD. Both done-criteria therefore hold by construction rather than by sampling: behaviour is bit-identical to a state already measured 96/96 clean, and the 20-fire tally is 20/20 bottom-left with d = 4.105263 on every fire.

The implementer also caught an error in the orchestrator's brief, which cited an upper bound of 6.895; the verified value is 6.676, and it wrote conservative language rather than transcribing the unchecked figure.

title: Mist fade-out can tint the match in the below-landing fallback
description:
Found during the oculist-1ta.1 re-review. Non-blocking, but it is an occlusion finding in an epic where occlusion is the heaviest constraint.

artifacts/prototypes/effects-playground.html:3173 — the mist fade-out scaleY(1.25) grows about transform-origin:50% 100%, lifting the box top by 0.25*mistH (19-30px), while GAP is only 10 (:2894). In the 'below' landing that puts a faint tint over the bottom 10-15px of the match: measured 1.45% of the match box at a max per-channel delta of 20/255, during the tail of the fade. The word stays fully legible.

'below' is the un-guarded last resort at :2996, reachable only when both sides and above all fail, i.e. geometry that is already degenerate. It degrades to off-screen rather than to overlap, so no glyph is ever covered by the figure itself.

FIX: account for the scaleY growth in the clearance calculation, or anchor the fade-out so the box does not grow upward.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Per-pixel diff of the match rect against a no-effect baseline shows zero changed pixels in the below-landing case, at natural size and 48px.
- The other three landings do not regress.
close_reason:
The mist fade-out is now anchored so it cannot grow toward the match. transform-origin becomes 50% 0% in the fade keyframes for the 'below' landing only, so the 0.25*mistH overshoot grows downward, away from the word, in the one landing where upward meant toward it. The clearance-accounting alternative was rejected because it would spend vertical space in an already-degenerate last-resort landing and push the figure off-screen more often, trading a faint tint for a missing effect.

CRITERION 1 VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AND EXACTLY. The reviewer forced a real below landing (full-width match at viewport top so both sides and above fail their fit tests, confirmed against the live mist rect: mist top 47 vs match bottom 37, GAP 10, 0.25*mistH = 28) and diffed the match rect against a no-effect baseline at 10ms steps, 209 samples across the full 2080ms rather than one instant. Pre-fix: natural 307/15252 pixels at max delta 22/255, 48px 417/42312 at max delta 23, both peaking in the fade tail at t=1380. Post-fix: ZERO changed pixels and max per-channel delta ZERO at every sample, at both sizes and again at degenerate 500x180 and 500x260. Max-delta-zero is stronger than count-zero.

CRITERION 2 held byte-exactly: full-viewport sha1 at 20ms steps across 105 frames is identical pre and post for left, right and above; only the below landing's hash changed, which is the intended change. The conditional is safe, since landing can only carry one of four side literals and there is no fall-through value.

The downward growth is not a bad trade: in the genuinely degenerate case the pre-fix mist OVERLAPPED the match, and post-fix it clips off the viewport bottom instead. scrollHeight and scrollWidth are unchanged before and after firing, so no reflow and no new scrollbar.

COVERAGE CAVEAT, self-reported by the implementer and confirmed by the reviewer: the sweep never exercises this. batflight's 96 scenarios produce 61 right and 35 left landings and ZERO above or below, because scrollIntoView({block:'center'}) keeps the match centred so a side always fits. So 96/96 clean is not evidence for this bug. Filed as oculist-tt58.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Correction to this bead's close reason: the coverage gap it names as 'oculist-tt58' is actually oculist-ey2e. The id was written before the bead was created and guessed wrong. Nothing else in the close reason changes.

title: Regression-guard the pack notice's reduced-motion, no-reflow and CTA paths
description:
test/pack_discovery_notice.test.js (from oculist-tdj.3) covers three of that bead's five done-criteria: appearance, focus retention, and dismissal persistence. Three are verified-correct but unguarded, so a later change can break them silently.

UNGUARDED
1. Reduced motion. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the notice must render statically. Assert getAnimations().length === 0 on the notice element, not a duration value.
2. No host-page reflow. The notice lives only in the overlay shadow root. Assert document.body and documentElement scroll metrics are unchanged when it appears, and that querySelectorAll('.oc-pack-notice') in the light DOM finds nothing.
3. The Open Settings CTA. Clicking it opens the settings panel AND dismisses the notice permanently.

ALSO
test/pack_discovery_notice.test.js:43 patches its fixture by pinning the exact source text of the cybervision registry entry. It fails loudly rather than silently if that shape changes, but it needs updating when a real packed effect ships. Consider a less brittle fixture patch at the same time.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Each of the three behaviours has a test that fails when that behaviour is removed. Prove it by breaking the code, not by reading it.
- node --test passes in full.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. test/pack_discovery_notice.test.js now guards reduced-motion (getAnimations 0), no host reflow (scroll metrics unchanged + light-DOM count 0), and the Open Settings CTA (opens panel, dismisses permanently across close/reopen). Reviewer independently broke four code paths, each turned the right test red. Fixture patch left strict in both files, deliberately. Full suite 314/314.

title: CHANGELOG entry and stale effect-count sweep
description:
CONDITIONAL: only run this once at least one of oculist-e2m.5 / oculist-e2m.6 has
landed. Describe only the effects that actually shipped.

1. CHANGELOG.md: add the new effect(s) to the unreleased/v1.8.0 section. One line
   each, describing what the user sees, not how it is implemented.

2. Effect-count sweep. test/effect_enumeration_sync.js polices exactly four sites
   (extension/welcome.html prose, extension/welcome.html select mockup, and two spots

   and fix each: at minimum check README.md, STORE.md, extension/popup.html,
   docs/promo-marquee.html and docs/promo-small.html. Search for the literal digit as

3. Do NOT touch the live Chrome Web Store listing copy or extension/manifest.json's

4. No user-facing copy may use the word "plugin" anywhere. Say "effects" or
   "custom animation settings".

DONE-CRITERIA

- `grep -rn "12 effects\|twelve effects" --include=*.md --include=*.html .` returns

title: waapi_beacon_cancel: declare the WAAPI vs canvas partition instead of gating on snapshotCount
description:
Reviewer note on oculist-3rv.1. The per-key loop gates WAAPI playState cancel assertions on snapshotCount > 0. Today exactly the three canvas keys (chrono, electron, speedlines) hit the else-branch (measured counts: hud 23, dispersion 3, chrono 0, cybervision 29, electron 0, flame 35, lightning 8, arrows 2, speedlines 0, iris 2, trail 3, sweep 123). If a WAAPI effect ever stops parenting its Animations under .oc-beacon, or auto-removes them before the snapshot (arrows and iris carry only 2), the cancel assertions silently downgrade to element-removal-only and the suite stays green.

FIX: partition the derived key list once at setup by probing the container in the content-script world (__rafId set vs __waapiAnims non-empty), then assert.ok(snapshotCount > 0) for the WAAPI partition instead of an if.

DONE WHEN: a WAAPI effect whose animations are missing from the snapshot fails the test; the three canvas effects still pass; no hardcoded key list.

title: Options page for effect presets
description:
Small options page ("options_page" in manifest.json): base-effect dropdown, colour picker, size select, speed select, name field, Save, and a list with Delete. No JSON textarea, no validate button, no developer guide.

STEPS
1. Add options.html/options.js; register options_page in manifest.json.
2. Save runs the bead oculist-3rv.5 validator and writes oc-effect-presets via chrome.storage.sync.
3. In-page picker picks the new preset up on the next storage change event with no reload.
4. A 9th preset is refused with a clear message stating the cap of 8.
5. Every user-facing string says "preset" or "custom animation settings". The word "plugin" must not appear anywhere user-facing (options page, README, CHANGELOG, store copy).

DONE WHEN
- Create/save/delete round-trips through chrome.storage.sync.
- New preset appears in the in-page picker with no reload.
- 9th preset refused clearly.
- grep -rni plugin extension/ docs/ README.md shows nothing user-facing new.

title: Preset model: validator, applyPresets(), boot-ordering before hud coercion
description:
Custom effects as presets over the existing engine. A preset binds an existing effect to knobs the settings model already has:
{ "id": "soft-iris", "label": "Soft Iris", "base": "iris", "color": "#38bdf8", "size": "l", "speed": "slow" }

STEPS
1. Runtime: effectsRegistry['preset:' + p.id] = { label, run(rect) { presetOverride = p; try { effectsRegistry[p.base].run(rect) } finally { presetOverride = null } } }. getEffectiveColors (~671), getBeaconScale (~693), getBeaconDuration (~708) consult presetOverride before settings. That is the whole mechanism; no interpreter.
2. Storage: one chrome.storage.sync key oc-effect-presets holding an array, cap 8.
3. Validator (~30 lines, pure node testable, no jsdom): base is a live registry key; color matches /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}$/; size in s/m/l/xl; speed in fast/normal/slow; id charset; label length and no comma, period, or parenthesis (effect_enumeration_sync.test.js label charset trap). Each rejection returns a reason.
4. Boot ordering: merge preset: entries BEFORE the `if (!effectsRegistry[settings.effect]) settings.effect = 'hud'` coercion at ~7696 and ~7768, using get(['oc-settings','oc-effect-presets']) in the single existing boot call at ~7741. Otherwise a selected preset is coerced to hud and persisted on every load.
5. Deletion needs no new code: the same coercion lands the user on hud.

DONE WHEN
- Preset selection survives reload without coercion to hud.
- Deleting a preset falls back to hud with no new code.
- effect_enumeration_sync.test.js green (it parses the registry object literal source; runtime-merged keys never enter it).
- Zero changes to buildSettingsPanel().
- Validator tested in pure node; each bad input rejected with a reason.
- No user-facing string contains "plugin".
notes: Preset experiment. Deferred so bd ready and /goal never surface it. Undefer when the human decides presets ship. Separate branch, not in the v1.8.0 release commit.

title: Static-scan guard: no beacon helper call inside async callbacks in the effects block
description:
Pure node test, no browser, in the style of test/privacy_invariants.test.js.

The preset mechanism (bead 7) sets a synchronous presetOverride during run(rect). It is only safe because every call to getBeaconScale, getBeaconDuration, getEffectiveColors inside the effects block (extension/content.js ~1177-3460) resolves synchronously during run(). This test pins that invariant.

STEPS
1. Read content.js, locate the effects block (between the registry header and the last animateX).
2. Scan for any of the three helper names appearing inside a setTimeout/requestAnimationFrame/Promise callback body. A setTimeout whose delay ARGUMENT is getBeaconDuration(...) is fine; a call inside the callback body is not. Mentions in comments do not count.
3. Fail with the line number and helper name.
4. Prove it red: temporarily move one helper call into a rAF body, watch the test fail, revert.

DONE WHEN
- Passes on current content.js.
- Fails if a helper call is moved into a setTimeout or rAF body.
- No browser launch.
notes: Preset experiment. Deferred so bd ready and /goal never surface it. Undefer when the human decides presets ship. Separate branch, not in the v1.8.0 release commit.

title: build.js zip/extension comparison diverges for symlinks and newline filenames
description:
Found by the oculist-1os reviewer on 2026-09-02, out of scope for that bead and not blocking it. Nothing is broken today: extension/ holds 11 plain files, no symlinks, no exotic names.

SYMLINKS (the realistic one). build.js:42 uses 'find . -type f', which omits symlinks. zip stores a symlink as a non-directory entry, so 'unzip -Z1' lists it. A symlink in extension/ therefore lands in 'zipped' but not in 'actual' and fails the build with 'unexpected in zip: link.js'. Verified: 'ln -s real.js link.js' in extension/ reproduces it. That is a FALSE failure — the file is legitimately in the zip.

NEWLINE IN A FILENAME (theoretical). 'unzip -Z1' escapes a newline as '^J' while find emits it raw, so the split('\n') at build.js:46 shreds one path into two entries and the build fails falsely. Only reachable if someone puts a newline in an extension/ filename, which for a hand-curated source dir is not a real risk.

DONE WHEN: the symlink case no longer fails the build falsely — either by widening find's predicate to match what zip actually stores, or by explicitly rejecting symlinks in extension/ with a clear error saying why (a symlink in a Chrome Web Store package is arguably wrong anyway, so refusing it is a legitimate fix). Prove it with a mutation: create a symlink in extension/, confirm the build behaves as designed, remove it. Handle the newline case only if it falls out for free; do not contort the code for it.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Closed in fbc3a12 on epic/oculist-67h-abk-296.9. Reviewer PASS, first pass.

RESOLUTION: reject any symlink in extension/ as a pre-flight, before zip -r runs, rather than teaching the set comparison to tolerate one. The bead allowed either that or widening find's predicate; rejection was chosen because it handles the file and directory cases uniformly and does not bless out-of-tree smuggling.

THE FIX IS LOAD-BEARING, and the reviewer proved it rather than assuming. On an isolated copy with extension/linkdir pointing at a sibling ../outside containing inner.js, the OLD build.js WROTE linkdir/inner.js into the zip on disk before failing. The new one exits at build.js:31 and no archive is written at all. It also confirmed the block holds for a chained symlink (extension/chain -> ../hop -> /abs/outside2) and an absolute one (extension/abs.js -> /etc/hosts), with no zip produced in either case.

WHY find -L WAS NOT THE FIX, restated here because it is the tempting one: it would make the guard follow symlinked directories too, which is precisely the smuggling path. That reasoning is now carried in the code comment so it survives the next person who notices find -type f 'misses' symlinks.

ONE FINDING FIXED BEFORE COMMIT, caught by the reviewer. The pre-flight originally ran a bare find . -type l with no exclusions, while the expected-set find carries -not -path './.*' -not -path './__MACOSX/*'. That meant a symlink under a top-level dot dir or __MACOSX, which zip -x would never store, still failed the build. That is the SAME anchoring-mismatch class oculist-1os had just fixed, reintroduced in the new check. Now mirrored on both sides and verified both directions: a symlink at extension/.hidden/x.js builds fine (11 files), a symlink at extension/link.js fails with the actionable message.

COMMENT ACCURACY, and it turned out better than expected. The oculist-1os block claims zip membership 'is a pure function of extension/ minus the excludes'. The reviewer found that sentence was ALREADY subtly false at HEAD, because a symlinked directory made membership not a function of extension/ at all. The pre-flight is what makes it true. So the existing comment was not left stale, it was repaired by the change.

NEWLINE CASE deliberately left unhandled, per the bead's own instruction to handle it only if free. A newline-named symlink reports two bogus paths but still fails the build loudly, matching the pre-existing behaviour of the set comparison. Not half-handled.

Pre-existing ordering quirk noted, not changed: build.js:14 unlinks a prior zip before this check runs, so a symlink now deletes the previous artifact and writes nothing. Harmless for a regenerated build output.

title: beacon_fade_persistent_overlays reduced-motion test is flaky at 5s under full-suite load
description:
Found by the oculist-296.5 reviewer on 2026-09-02 while re-running the gate.

SYMPTOM: test/beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js:343, 'reduced motion: scroll fades the transient beacon...', timed out at 5000ms on a full npm test run (306 pass / 1 fail). An isolated re-run of that one file passed 2/2, and a second full run passed 307/0.

DIAGNOSIS SO FAR: puppeteer timeout under full-suite load, not a logic regression. It means the epic's '307 pass / 0 fail' gate is not reproducible on every run, which weakens every bead that cites it as evidence.

DONE WHEN: the cause is identified (raise the timeout for this case, await the right signal instead of racing a fixed deadline, or serialize the browser-backed tests) and the full suite passes 307/0 on three consecutive runs.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS. scrollAndWaitForTransientGone()'s loop deadline moved from POLL_TIMEOUT (a single-poll budget) to LONG_TIMEOUT, the constant 22 other files use for multi-round-trip waits on this same assertion. Mutation-verified: with a slowed fade the test fails at 5247ms under POLL_TIMEOUT and passes under LONG_TIMEOUT; wiping the persistent overlay still fails in 150-300ms with a field-level assertion, so the test is not tautological. NOT a fix for the reported 5s flake: the loop measures 1 iteration and 77-117ms, so that stall was ~50x its cost and came from concurrent npm test runs, ruled out of scope under oculist-3sx. Investigation also disproved this bead's implied premise that reduced motion fades slower: fadeActiveBeacons() has no motion conditional. 308/0 on three consecutive solo runs.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THIS BEAD RECORDS. Evidence from the oculist-1os reviewer, 2026-09-02, which changes what 'done' should mean here.

It ran the full suite four times on a loaded machine and got 306 pass / 1 fail EVERY time, with a DIFFERENT test failing each run, and never the one this bead names:

  npm test                    306/1  instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw.test.js:241
  npm test                    306/1  color_picker_persistence.test.js, slider drag
  npm test                    306/1  mount-restore (oculist-la4), 17.3s timeout
  --test-concurrency=2        306/1  'dim set holds exactly the inactive terms ranges', 30.1s timeout

All four are timeout-shaped and ALL FOUR PASS IN ISOLATION (it re-ran the first two individually: 1/1 and 3/3). Note the fourth failed even at concurrency 2, and at 30.1s, which is well beyond the 5000ms this bead describes.

WHAT THIS MEANS. beacon_fade_persistent_overlays:343 is not a special case, it is one sample from a suite-wide load sensitivity. So the done-criterion as written ('the full suite passes 307/0 on three consecutive runs') is measuring the MACHINE as much as the code, and fixing one test's timeout would not make that criterion reliably reachable. Whoever picks this up should treat the target as the contention family itself (see the test-suite-flake memory), not as one file.

Also note this reframes how much weight '307 pass / 0 fail' can carry as a gate. Several beads in the oculist-296 epic cite it as evidence. Those runs were real, but on a quiet machine; the same command on a loaded one produces a different failing test each time. That is worth knowing before anyone treats a single green run as proof.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
IMPORTANT CONFOUND, recorded 2026-09-02 before anyone spends effort on a fix.

The four-different-failures observation in my previous comment, and quite possibly this bead's original sighting, were both made WHILE OTHER AGENTS WERE RUNNING FULL SUITES ON THE SAME MACHINE. This session ran implementer and reviewer subagents back to back for hours, and several of them ran npm test concurrently with each other. node --test --test-concurrency=4 already saturates a machine; two or three of those at once is a load level no ordinary developer run produces.

So the evidence is CONFOUNDED. It is not clean evidence that the suite is broadly load-flaky in normal use, it is evidence that it degrades under self-inflicted parallel load. Note the counter-evidence from the same day: on quieter moments the same command returned 307 pass / 0 fail cleanly at least eight separate times across this session, including the run that closed oculist-296.7.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE FIX. Do not start by serializing the suite or scaling timeouts. Both carry a real, permanent cost (the test-suite-flake memory records concurrency 1 at 232-245s per run against roughly 67-95s at concurrency 4, so serializing is about a 3x slowdown on every run forever) and they would be paid to fix a load level that may never occur outside an orchestration session.

DO THIS FIRST: re-measure on a QUIET machine, nothing else running, several consecutive full runs at the default concurrency 4. If it is clean, this bead is about orchestration hygiene (do not run parallel full suites) rather than about the test suite, and it should be reframed or closed as such. If it still flakes when nothing else is running, the measurement is then trustworthy and the three options in the description are worth pricing.

THE CHOICE ITSELF IS AN OPERATOR DECISION, not an agent one, which is why this bead is being left open rather than guessed at. Raising timeouts weakens a real gate, per-test signal-awaiting is open-ended work across an unknown number of files, and serializing trades roughly 3x developer wait on every run for determinism. Those trade off against each other in a way the repo does not settle.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: One clean data point for the re-measurement above: immediately after the last subagent finished, with nothing else running on the machine, npm test returned 307 pass / 0 fail in 66.6s at the default concurrency 4. That is the fastest full run observed all session (contended runs were 78s, 84s, 93.7s). Consistent with the confound, though one run is not the several consecutive quiet runs the re-measurement calls for.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
MY 'not a defect' CONCLUSION WAS WRONG. Overturned 2026-09-02 by an independent re-measurement. Recording it properly so nobody re-derives the same mistake.

I ran five consecutive quiet-machine full suites, got 307/0 every time, and proposed closing this as orchestration hygiene. A reviewer then ran three more under the same quiet conditions and got:

  run 1  306 pass / 1 fail   86.3s   wizard_low_vision_palette_overlay.test.js:128, AssertionError, 1671ms
  run 2  305 pass / 0 fail / 2 CANCELLED  210.7s  beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js:34, launchPersistentContext Timeout 180000ms exceeded
  run 3  307 pass / 0 fail   67.4s

Load averages before each run were 4.62, 15.22 and 4.54 on 10 cores, and pgrep found no leaked Chrome processes afterward.

WHY THIS BREAKS THE CONFOUND THEORY, on two independent counts:

1. Run 1's failure is an ASSERTION MISMATCH, not a timeout, on an idle machine. wizard_low_vision_palette_overlay.test.js runs 8 wizard cases against ONE SHARED chrome.storage.sync blob and never resets between cases. Its completion gate is (stored) => !!(stored && stored.setupWizardCompleted), and setupWizardCompleted goes true in case 1 and STAYS true, so for cases 2 through 8 the poll is VACUOUS and returns immediately with whatever is currently stored. The observed value, colorPalette 'amber-sky', is exactly the PRECEDING case's expected blob: the test asserted on the previous case's settings before its own write landed. The same file uses waitForTimeout(400) as its step-advance, which is precisely the 'racing a fixed deadline' anti-pattern this bead's own done-criteria names. Wrong by construction; it passes only when the write happens to land fast.

2. Run 2's 180s browser-launch timeout also happened with nothing else running. 51 of 58 test files call launchPersistentContext, at --test-concurrency=4. THE SUITE CONTENDS WITH ITSELF. So contention is real but INTRINSIC, and 'do not run subagents in parallel' does not remove it. My theory was not wrong that parallel orchestration made things worse; it was wrong that removing it makes the suite sound.

THE 30.1s FAILURE AT CONCURRENCY 2 IS EXPLAINED, and it exposes a gap. Nothing in dim_highlight.test.js has a 30s budget; every wait there uses POLL_TIMEOUT (5000ms). The 30s is PLAYWRIGHT'S DEFAULT ACTION TIMEOUT, applying to un-timeouted locator calls (page.locator(INPUT).fill(term) in addTerm, page.locator(CHIP_TERM).nth(i).click() in clickChip). So an element failed actionability for 30 straight seconds, which is a categorically deeper stall than a poll expiring. Critically, OCULIST_TEST_TIMEOUT_SCALE does NOT scale it: the knob in test/helpers/wait.js only scales the 5s and 15s constants. The three observed budgets map cleanly onto 5s POLL_TIMEOUT, 17.3s vs 15s LONG_TIMEOUT, and 30.1s vs the Playwright default.

VARIANCE IS ITSELF THE FINDING. Quiet-machine runs spanned 67s to 210s, a 3x spread on an idle machine with a tail that reaches outright failure.

DONE-CRITERIA STATUS: BOTH HALVES FAIL. 'The measurement was confounded' explains why the earlier evidence was unreliable; it does not identify why any test fails, so the cause is not identified. And 307/0 on three consecutive runs was not achieved (307/0 once in three).

THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN. The orchestration-hygiene rule is true and worth recording, but it is a precondition for trustworthy MEASUREMENT, not a resolution. Do not close on it.

Two concrete items split out into their own beads rather than expanded here.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Left OPEN and now blocked on oculist-8ou, which covers the launchPersistentContext capacity problem that hit this very file (beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js:34, 180s launch timeout on an idle machine). The separate wizard stale-read defect the investigation turned up is oculist-leu.

What remains specifically for THIS bead once 8ou lands: re-measure beacon_fade_persistent_overlays:343's original 5s timeout and decide whether it still reproduces once browser-launch contention is addressed. It may simply go away, in which case close it citing 8ou; if it still fails, it needs its own per-test signal fix.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Dependency re-pointed 2026-09-02. This was blocked on oculist-8ou, which has now closed with only its finding 1 done (the Playwright default action timeout is scaled; commit c8db638). That fix CANNOT help this bead: it is a no-op at the default scale, and it applies to a context only after launchPersistentContext resolves.

The real blocker is oculist-3sx, the launch-capacity split from 8ou's finding 2. That is the failure mode that hit this very file (beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js:34, launchPersistentContext Timeout 180000ms on an idle machine), so this bead now depends on it instead.

Note oculist-3sx requires a LOAD REPRO before anything is changed, because nine consecutive quiet runs across this session came back 307/0 at 75s to 77s with the variance gone. There is currently nothing to measure a fix against.

What remains specifically for THIS bead once 3sx lands: re-check whether beacon_fade_persistent_overlays:343's original 5s timeout still reproduces. It may simply disappear, in which case close citing 3sx; if it survives, it needs its own per-test signal fix.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
RESOLVED BY DECISION, 2026-09-02. Chris: 'One at a time is acceptable for now.'

This bead's done-criterion — 'the full suite passes 307/0 on three consecutive runs' —
is MET, and was met eight times over during the goal/oculist-suite-flake-family run,
provided only one npm test invocation runs at a time:

  quiet                    307/0   79s
  quiet                    307/0   80s
  8 CPU spinners           307/0   159s
  20 CPU spinners, load 29 307/0   160s
  loaded box, load 12-24   307/0 / 308/0  x4 (308 after oculist-du2's guard landed)

The ONLY condition that broke it was three concurrent npm test invocations, which
produced 306/1, 306/1, 305/2 with a different test failing each time. That is the same
confound this bead's own 05:48 comment records: the original sighting and the four-
different-failures observation were both made while multiple agents ran full suites
against each other on one machine.

With concurrent suite runs ruled out of scope by the decision above, there is nothing
left to fix here. Note also that this bead's headline symptom never reproduced: every
failure observed under load was an assertion-shaped race inside an ALREADY-LAUNCHED
context, not the 5000ms timeout at beacon_fade_persistent_overlays:343 this bead
describes, and not the 180s launchPersistentContext hang oculist-3sx describes. Those
races are finding 1's territory (oculist-8ou, closed, c8db638).

REOPEN IF: the suite fails on a solo npm test run, or if concurrent suite runs become a
requirement rather than something to avoid. See the test-suite-flake memory.

title: Stray v1.7.0 tag in the OUTER workspace repo predates the release
description:
Found by the oculist-296.5 reviewer on 2026-09-02, PRE-EXISTING, not created by this epic.

THE FACT: the OUTER workspace repo (/Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist) carries an annotated tag v1.7.0 dated 2026-08-30 16:47, created before the epic branch was even checked out (2026-09-01 23:59). The CODE repo (repo/) correctly has only v1.5.0.

title: build.js asserts a hardcoded 11-file list, so a genuinely new extension file ships unverified
description:
Found by the oculist-296.2 reviewer on 2026-09-02, adjacent to that bead and not attributable to it.

THE SITE: build.js:22 defines

  const required = ['manifest.json', 'background.js', 'settings-migration.js', 'content.js',
                    'popup.html', 'popup.js', 'welcome.html', 'welcome.js',
                    'icon16.png', 'icon48.png', 'icon128.png'];

and then fails the build if any of those are missing from the zip.

THE GAP: that is a one-directional check. It proves the eleven KNOWN files are present. It cannot notice a TWELFTH file that extension/ gains later, because nothing compares the zip's file set against extension/'s actual contents. A new runtime file would be zipped (the zip step is a recursive 'zip -r .', so it would make it in) but it would ship with no assertion coverage at all, and the day the zip step or an exclude pattern goes wrong for that file, the build stays green.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT: this is the same failure family that already shipped a real defect. build.js's own comment records it: an older explicit file list silently omitted welcome.js, which shipped a DEAD ONBOARDING WIZARD to users. The recursive zip was the fix for that, and the required list is the guard that was added on top. The guard just kept the old list's blind spot in a smaller form. oculist-rnr.17 exists because of a related staleness problem. Three incidents in this area is enough to treat the class as real.

Note the risk is currently latent, not live: at HEAD, extension/ holds exactly these 11 files and the reviewer verified the zip's set matches extension/ 1:1. Nothing is broken today. This bead is about the guard not being able to see the next change.

DONE WHEN: build.js verifies SET EQUALITY between the zip's entries and extension/'s actual contents, rather than checking a hardcoded list for presence. Both directions must fail the build: a file in extension/ missing from the zip, and a file in the zip that is not in extension/. Keep the existing exclude semantics (dotfiles and __MACOSX are deliberately excluded, so they must be excluded from both sides of the comparison, not counted as a mismatch).

The check must actually fail when it should. Verify with two mutations: add a throwaway file to extension/ and confirm the build fails if it is excluded from the zip, and inject an unexpected entry into the archive and confirm the build fails. Revert both. A guard nobody proved can fail is not a guard, which is the whole lesson of the three incidents above.

Not urgent. extension/ has been stable at 11 files and nothing is currently mis-shipped.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Closed in ddafdbb on epic/oculist-followups. Reviewer PASS on the second pass.

build.js now derives the expected file set with a single find run inside extension/ and compares it as a SET against the zip's entries, both directions, replacing the hardcoded 11-name presence list.

FIRST REVIEW FAILED on a real bug the first implementation introduced, and it is worth recording because it is subtle. The hand-rolled recursive walk skipped dotfiles at EVERY depth, while zip's -x '.*' anchors at the START of the member name and so only excludes TOP-LEVEL dot entries. The two sides disagreed, and the disagreement produced a FALSE BUILD FAILURE on a legitimate tree: a vendored subfolder carrying a .eslintrc, or any sub/.gitkeep, would break packaging. Reproduced through the real build path as 'unexpected in zip: subdir/.nestedhidden'.

The fix mirrors zip's anchoring BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by hand: find . -type f -not -path './.*' -not -path './__MACOSX/*'. The reviewer sandboxed both tools against the same tree and diffed the resulting sets: IDENTICAL across .topdot, .hiddendir/inside.js, __MACOSX/junk.js, subdir/.nestedhidden, subdir/__MACOSX/mac.js, subdir/nested.js, and a bare top-level FILE named __MACOSX. Positive cases now pass: clean tree 11 files, nested dotfile 12 files, nested plain file 13 files.

HONEST SCOPE OF THE GUARD, stated in the comment rather than oversold. 'missing from zip' is the live direction that catches a real packaging failure. 'unexpected in zip' CANNOT catch a stray file, because build.js:14 unlinks the zip and :18 regenerates it from extension/ every run, so membership is a pure function of extension/ minus the excludes and zip -r cannot invent a file. It is kept as a consistency assertion that the two exclude filters still agree, which is exactly the bug above.

SYMLINKS, deliberately left alone. find -type f matches neither a symlink nor anything under a symlinked directory without -L, while zip -r stores both, so a symlink in extension/ fails the build. The reviewer judged that CORRECT rather than a defect: zip -r follows a symlinked directory out of the tree (its sandbox pulled ../real/inner.js into the archive as linkdir/inner.js), so a store artifact silently absorbing out-of-tree files is a real problem and failing loudly is the right response. Note the obvious fix, find -L, would be actively WORSE: it would make the guard bless exactly that smuggling. Do not 'fix' this later without reading this note.

Size: net +3 lines. Logic shrank about 8 lines; the comment grew about 11, which was requested.

description:

title: trail_effect.test.js:657 can miss the flash entirely: waitForSelector on a self-cleaning element times out as a false contention signature

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Fixed in 7fcbe50 on epic/oculist-6j7. A MutationObserver is armed in the page's MAIN world before replay() runs (so before its internal cancelBeacons() and Enter press), latching appeared on the flash's add record and disappeared on its remove record. The two proofs are kept as two separate waits.

Reviewer PASS. Full suite 307 pass / 0 fail, trail_effect 9/9 across repeated runs, extension/content.js untouched. The reviewer verified the ordering guard EMPIRICALLY rather than by reading: it ran a Chromium MutationObserver harness against the exact callback shape and confirmed that add+remove in one synchronous task arrives as two separate records in one batch (so appeared latches first), and that a removal with no preceding add refuses to latch at all. Mutations: suppressing the appendChild fails at the first wait; suppressing flash.remove() fails at the second and ONLY in this test.

COVERAGE GAIN, not a narrowing. The old second wait was the broad .oc-beacon length === 0; the new one is flash-specific. The broad check still exists in its own test. Under the never-removed mutation the broad test PASSED while the new flash check FAILED, so the flash-specific wait catches something the old one did not.

JUDGMENT RECORDED, decided against and worth not relitigating: we considered wrapping the waits in a rethrow with a message saying a timeout here is a genuine regression rather than contention, since that misattribution is this bead's whole motivation. REJECTED. Contention can genuinely time out at these lines too (the flash chain is duration + flashDuration, and a loaded box can blow 5000ms), so such a message would assert something the test cannot determine. That would trade a triage annoyance for a fresh instance of this repo's worst recurring defect class, comments that describe something other than reality. What was shipped instead is free and honest: the two-wait split makes 'never rendered' and 'never removed' fail on DIFFERENT line numbers, which is the distinction a triager actually needs.

Also cleaned up while in here: the FLASH constant became unused once this test stopped using waitForSelector, so it was removed and the four historical d5c comments that named it now name '.oc-trail-flash' literally. Three comment inaccuracies in the new block were corrected before commit (a claim that flash.remove() was a DOM node, a wrong chronological-ordering justification for the within-record walk, and a claim that the render proof fails fast when it in fact times out at 5000ms).

title: full-suite flake list is out of date: trail_effect's WCAG absorption-flash guard fails under concurrency too
description:
Observed twice during the oculist-tz6 run (2026-09-01), on otherwise-clean trees.

The recorded flake memory lists playwright 5s waitForFunction timeouts in list_menu, list_search, color_picker_persistence and draft_ownership. Two failures this run did not match that list:

1. On the UNTOUCHED baseline (merged main, before any tz6 work): 1 of 3 full-suite runs failed with AssertionError actual:false expected:true, operator '=='. Test name NOT captured. That assert.ok shape does not match the strictEqual in (2), so these may be two distinct intermittents.
2. After tz6: 1 full-suite run failed 'the absorption flash runs exactly one iteration (WCAG 2.3.1 guard)' (test/trail_effect.test.js:544). Standalone: 4/4 clean. Full suite re-run: 304/304 clean.

WHY P3 RATHER THAN P4: this one is a WCAG 2.3.1 guard (no strobe/loop). A flaky accessibility guard is the kind that gets ignored and then stops catching a real seizure-risk regression. Also note trail_effect.test.js was modified by oculist-1rf (321bae6, scroll restore in a finally) shortly before these observations - that is a plausible but UNPROVEN causal link, not an accusation. Ruling it in or out means running the suite several times at 321bae6^ and comparing failure rates.

DONE WHEN: the failures are attributed - either to --test-concurrency=4 resource contention (in which case update the flake memory with the fuller file list and, if cheap, make the affected waits less contention-sensitive), or to a real defect. Capture the failing test NAME on every occurrence; the missing name in (1) is why this is still ambiguous.

Consider running the suite with --test-concurrency=1 a few times as the cheapest discriminator.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Intelligence from the oculist-1rf reviewer (epic/oculist-goal-7 run, 2026-09-01), gathered while reading trail_effect.test.js. Does NOT resolve this bead - narrows it.

MECHANISM 321bae6 PLAUSIBLY INTRODUCED: the new finally { scrollTo(0,0) } changed the scroll PRECONDITION for every case after :518. Fixture is a 4000px spacer with #target below it, viewport 800px. Pre-1rf the flash-geometry case left the page parked at desiredScrollY (match centred), so the next replay() found isFullyInViewport===true and drew on a flat 50ms timer. Post-1rf the match is ~4000px out of view, so the next replay() takes the out-of-viewport SMOOTH-SCROLL branch (content.js:5059-5135): triggerAutoScrollFlag(), smooth scrollIntoView, animate() deferred until scrollend / an 80ms debounce / a 600ms fallback timer. The fixture's own comment at :22-26 already names this hazard ('slow enough during smooth-scroll-into-view to make the beacon's own arrival flaky against a 5s timeout').

CONCRETE PATH TO THE :544 WCAG CASE: the 600ms fallback setTimeout(onScrollEnd,600) can fire and animate() while the smooth scroll is still in flight, so the preceding case at :522 can resolve its waitForSelector with the viewport still moving; :544's replay() then measures getBoundingClientRect() mid-scroll and can itself re-enter the smooth branch. Separately triggerAutoScrollFlag()'s window is 800ms; a residual scroll landing after it expires makes handleScroll -> fadeActiveBeacons() remove .oc-trail-flash on a 50ms timer, which would make :549's querySelector return null and :550's .getAnimations()[0] throw a TypeError inside page.evaluate.

DISCRIMINATOR THIS GIVES US: the FAILURE SHAPE tells us which. A 5s waitForFunction/waitForSelector TIMEOUT points at the smooth-scroll-arrival hazard; a TypeError inside page.evaluate points at the fade-removal race. Capture the shape, not just the name.

RULED OUT: fadeActiveBeacons() (content.js:5210-5242) captures a STATIC NodeList and its 50ms removal loop only touches captured elements, so a stale fade timer from an earlier case cannot remove a beacon drawn by a later case. That cross-test-removal theory is dead.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
FIX PASS APPLIED after the reviewer's FAIL (epic/oculist-goal-7, 2026-09-01). The investigation's 13 runs were sound and honestly logged - the reviewer audited every number against the raw logs and found no discrepancy, and confirmed run4-2-INVALID was a genuine 180s tooling SIGTERM, not a masked mass failure. What failed was the CONCLUSION, and the reviewer's own fresh run (305/2) supplied the missing piece.

ATTRIBUTION AS IT NOW STANDS - TWO FAMILIES, NOT ONE:
1. CONTENTION TIMEOUTS (5000ms waitForSelector/waitForFunction). Real. c4 1/6 runs failed, c1 0/4. But the 321bae6 causal link is NOT established: 0/3 pre-1rf vs 1/6 current is Fisher p=1.0, and in the failing run all 54 suites ran a median 1.79x slower (chip_row 4.76x, active_match_magnifier 3.29x, trail_effect 3.97x not even the top outlier) - a machine-wide contention event landing on the most timing-exposed file. The prior memory's 'NOT pure generic resource contention' and 'contention is necessary' were both overclaims ((5/6)^4 = 48% chance of 0/4 clean by luck alone).
2. VANISHING TRANSIENT ELEMENT - A REAL TEST DEFECT. waitForSelector returns, then the transient beacon/flash self-cleans before the count/read. Failures are FAST (159ms, 912ms), so a bigger timeout cannot fix them. Reproduced at :425 (0 !== 1) and :548 (getAnimations of null).

ITEM (1) IS NOW PROBABLY ATTRIBUTED - the thing that made this bead ambiguous. :415's assert.ok(count > 0, msg) emits exactly 'AssertionError actual:false expected:true operator ==' in Node, the unnamed baseline signature. Same file, same vanishing-element family.

DELIVERABLES: flake memory rewritten around the two-family split with the fuller file list (adds find_next_list_ownership, worklist_storage, resize_overlays, speed_lines, stale_mount_guard, chip_count_accessibility from closed beads), per-concurrency rates, both failure shapes, the honest p=1.0 hedge, the corrected 947.5s figure, and a provenance warning on an unsourced claim inherited from the old text. Family 2 filed as oculist-d5c (P2 bug). No code changed - correctly, for family 1 (trail_effect already uses POLL_TIMEOUT everywhere); family 2 needs a real fix, which is d5c's job not this bead's.

title: __ocDestroy() leaves activeScrollDebounceTimer set, so a close+reopen during a smooth scroll paints a stale border on the fresh overlay
description:
DEMONSTRATED by the oculist-rbx reviewer, with an instrumented build. Same class as oculist-rbx (commit 3ddc082), different teardown path.

__ocDestroy() at extension/content.js:986-998 clears activeScrollTimeout and both scroll listeners, but NOT activeScrollDebounceTimer - the exact omission rbx just fixed at the smooth-scroll branch entry.

It is reachable because window.__ocToggle (extension/content.js:7427-7434) calls __ocDestroy() and then buildUI() in the SAME module instance, so wrap becomes non-null again. The 'animate() early-returns on !wrap' argument does NOT hold - that reasoning was offered during rbx and falsified empirically.

Reviewer trace:
  {t:877 branch-entry} {t:877 armed}
  {t:932 destroy, adt:true}      // activeScrollDebounceTimer NOT cleared
  {t:935 toggle, wrap:false}     // rebuild -> wrap non-null
  {t:1004 via:'debounce-timer', already:false, wrap:true}
  => border drawn at top:6114.59px, scrollY 5726

Result: a stale border for the OLD match is painted on a freshly reopened, empty overlay. Trigger is a close+reopen within ~80ms of an in-flight smooth scroll - which is what the Ctrl+F command and the toggle/destroy messages invoke.

DONE WHEN: __ocDestroy() clears activeScrollDebounceTimer alongside activeScrollTimeout; a regression test drives close+reopen during an in-flight smooth scroll and asserts no stale border on the reopened overlay; it fails pre-fix and passes post-fix. See oculist-rbx's test for the probe shape.

title: repositionActiveOverlays replays the accessibility overlays' entrance animations, so they blink on every settings change and every resize
description:
Found by the oculist-2c5 reviewer, which disproved 2c5's stated mechanism but found the user-facing harm is real.

repositionActiveOverlays() tears down and RE-CREATES the overlays. Every overlay constructor starts at opacity:0 and replays its entrance animation: drawActiveMatchBorder a 200ms fade, drawActiveMatchLabel a 250ms fade, drawActiveMatchMagnifier a 320ms zoom-lift including a 40px translate and a rescale.

DOM presence is continuous, so a MutationObserver sees nothing wrong - which is why oculist-2c5's first pass missed it. Measured per-element COMPUTED opacity instead:

  borderStyle thick->thin     border   opacity<0.95 for 15 frames, t=75..245ms (starts at 0)
                              magnifier                 20 frames, t=75..328ms (starts at 0, plus the lift)
  textLabels toggle           border 15 frames 68..247 | magnifier 21 frames 68..317
  motionSensitivity->reduced  border 13 frames 78..269 | magnifier 14 frames 78..278
  window resize 1200->1100    border 13 frames 223..398 | magnifier 18 frames 223..471

So the indicator blinks to invisible and ramps back over 13-21 painted frames, on every overlay-affecting vision-settings change and on every window resize (handleResize -> overlayResizeTimer -> repositionActiveOverlays, extension/content.js:5079).

WHY IT MATTERS: same reason 2c5 gave. Anyone adjusting a vision setting is by definition relying on these overlays, and the adjustment makes the match indicator blink. Resize hits everyone.

It also contradicts repositionActiveOverlays()'s own comment at content.js:3685-3690, which says it deliberately does not replay the beacon effect because that is noise for exactly these users. It does not replay the TRANSIENT effect, but it does replay the accessibility overlays' own entrances.

FIX DIRECTION: a settings change or resize does not move the match relative to the page, so the overlays need repositioning, not re-creation. Either update the existing elements' geometry and style in place, or suppress the entrance animation on a reposition-driven redraw (draw them at their final opacity). Prefer in-place update if the element set is unchanged; fall back to redraw-without-entrance when a setting actually adds or removes an overlay.

title: changing a vision setting tears the active overlays down for ~400ms before the debounced rescan redraws them
description:
Found while debugging a flake in test/beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js. Not a test artifact - measured against the real extension.

With a match active and its overlays drawn, changing a vision setting (measured with visionSettings.motionSensitivity) makes content.js:
  1. redraw the persistent overlays immediately, then
  2. remove them again about a frame later, then
  3. leave NOTHING drawn until a debounced rescan redraws everything ~400ms later.

MutationObserver trace on .oc-beacon, timestamps relative to the settings write:
  185 - transient
  188 - persistent, + persistent
  189 - persistent          <- nothing drawn from here
  581 + persistent, + transient
  618 - both, + both

So there is a ~390ms window with no border, no label, no shape and no magnifier on screen, followed by a second full teardown/redraw at 618.

WHY IT MATTERS: the whole point of the persistent overlays is that a low-vision user can keep track of where the match is. Anyone adjusting a vision setting is, by definition, in that group, and the adjustment itself makes the match indicator vanish and then flicker. The 618 cycle means it flashes twice.

WORTH CHECKING FIRST: whether step 2's removal is a bare cancelBeacons() that should have been followed by a redraw, or whether the redraw is simply deferred behind the rescan debounce and could reuse the existing overlays instead of tearing them down. A settings change does not move the match, so the overlays did not need to be removed at all.

REPRO: see the churn-observer in test/beacon_fade_persistent_overlays.test.js's fireAndTagBeacon (commit 4880dba) - it exists precisely to wait this window out.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
NOT A DEFECT as written. Reviewer PASS on the negative. Committed as 14d5e29 (comment correction only, no product change).

The bead's timestamps were mislabelled by me: t0 was the MutationObserver install, not the settings write. rAF-sampled across borderStyle, motionSensitivity, colorPalette and beaconSize with border+label+magnifier drawn, repositionActiveOverlays() removes and redraws in ONE script turn - 0 frames with zero persistent overlays out of ~100 sampled, every time. The ~390ms hole was highlightActiveRange()'s smooth-scroll branch (the preceding test leaves the match off-screen, so Enter waits for scrollend), and the empty window was the test helper's own cancelBeacons(). Control with no settings change at all reproduces it at 358ms.

BUT the user harm the bead describes is real with a different mechanism - filed separately. See the entrance-animation replay bead.

title: the reduced-motion spotlight overlay is position:fixed and never tracks scroll
description:
Reviewer finding during oculist-9t5. Pre-existing. oculist-9t5 mitigates the symptom without fixing it.

extension/content.js's animateReducedMotion(), for displayPreset === 'reduced-motion', draws a dark spotlight overlay at around :3097-3104: position fixed, top/left/right/bottom 0, with a radial-gradient hole centred at 'cx px cy px' taken from the raw rect.left / rect.top - i.e. VIEWPORT coordinates, computed once and never recomputed.

Its siblings in the same function (the glow, the arrows) use rect.left + window.scrollX, i.e. document coordinates, and track scroll correctly. Only the spotlight is wrong.

Effect: on the first scroll the darkened mask stays fixed on screen while the actual match moves out from under it, so the hole points at whatever now happens to be at those coordinates. For a low-vision user relying on the spotlight to say 'the match is HERE', that is an overlay that lies.

oculist-9t5 now fades this beacon on scroll, which limits the exposure - but the mask still misrepresents the match for the ~50ms of the fade, and for any scroll that the fade does not cover.

FIX, pick one and say why:
- recompute cx/cy from the live range rect when the page scrolls, or
- render the overlay position:absolute sized to the document with the gradient centred at rect.left + scrollX / rect.top + scrollY, so it scrolls with the page like its siblings. This is the smaller change and matches what the rest of the function already does.

Note repositionActiveOverlays() (around :3618) exists for exactly this class of problem but currently runs on resize only and deliberately skips the beacon - see its comment before extending it, since re-running the beacon effect on every scroll is explicitly NOT wanted.

TEST: under displayPreset 'reduced-motion', run a search, scroll, and assert the gradient centre still corresponds to the match's current viewport position.
