A listener would be a literal no-op re-inject and a CSS-diff test would have nothing to diff. The done-criteria's literal 'the CSS changes' wording is UNSATISFIABLE for this flip, not unimplemented. The bead's INTENT is satisfied: behaviour does update live, probed at 23 beacon parts on full motion, 0 after the flip, 23 restored, because effectiveMotion() (content.js:2180-2184) reads reducedMotionQuery.matches fresh per render, so there is no staleness window. That is already covered by test/prefers_reduced_motion.test.js:93. VERIFIED: retained MediaQueryList.matches confirmed live in-page; registration cannot stack (module scope, behind the top-of-file re-injection guard at content.js:4) and cannot fire before boot() (a change event cannot interrupt the synchronous IIFE); post-destroy flips throw nothing and leave exactly 1 global style element, and that element is present on every page at HEAD anyway; 15 alternating flips produced no style stacking. Suite 118 pass / 0 fail, no new waitForTimeout so oculist-l6m.32 is not regressed. KNOWN RESIDUE, deliberate: the listeners are not removed in __ocDestroy() (content.js:663), matching the existing chrome.storage.onChanged pattern, so a torn-down instance keeps re-injecting an inert style element on every OS flip for the page's lifetime.

title: Flaky: lite_mode_restore.test.js draft-ownership assertion fails intermittently under full-suite load
description: Found during oculist-l6m.42 review. One uncontrolled full-suite run hit AssertionError: 'the draft must own oculist-match while it is non-empty' at test/lite_mode_restore.test.js:225. Not seen in 10 subsequent controlled runs (5 on the working tree, 5 at detached HEAD), so it is rarer than oculist-nw4's resize flake. Recorded so the suite's flakiness is known to extend beyond the resize test rather than being written off as a single bad test. Same family as oculist-nw4 and oculist-l6m.32: readiness and wall-clock dependence under parallel load. Needs a repeat-run harness to characterise before fixing.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: LEFT OPEN deliberately after the oculist-l6m.32 conversion (commit e97e029). The implementer reported this bead as 'addressed as part of the general lite_mode_restore.test.js conversion', with no repro attempted since it was already rare. The reviewer judged that honest but not evidence: nothing in that diff targets this flake specifically and no test demonstrates it is gone. Closing would be closing on faith. The general conversion did replace lite_mode_restore.test.js's fixed waits with debounce-result polling, so this may well be fixed - it just is not shown. NEXT STEP: run the suite repeatedly on an idle machine (this flake was seen once in ~16 full runs, so it needs a repeat-run harness to characterise) and close only if it does not reappear. Related: oculist-nw4 and oculist-mmm were both closed by that same commit with verified root-cause fixes.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CLOSED on differential evidence, no code change required - this bead was resolved by oculist-l6m.32's sleep-to-poll conversion (commit e97e029). MECHANISM: the assertion moved to test/lite_mode_restore.test.js:358. Before the conversion, typeDraft() was fill() plus a fixed waitForTimeout(400) against a 400ms debounce plus a rescan, i.e. zero margin, then the test read CSS.highlights.get('oculist-match') once and asserted. That is exactly the described flake. Now the assertion is preceded by waitForContentScriptValue polling the SAME expression with the SAME predicate the assertion checks, at 30ms intervals with a 5000ms budget, so the value asserted on is by construction one that satisfies the predicate. The named AssertionError is structurally unreachable; the only reachable failure is a poll timeout, which raises a different, self-describing error. POSITIVE CONTROL, which is what actually closes this: the reviewer restored the pre-conversion file as a temp probe and ran both versions under 12 CPU burners at load average ~45. OLD version, 8 runs: 1 FAIL with the bead's exact symptom, reproduced verbatim on demand. CURRENT version, 14 runs under identical load: 14/14 pass. The load condition demonstrably reproduces the flake on old code and not on new, which is a differential rather than an absence of evidence. Corroboration: 62 total runs of the current code across orchestrator and reviewer, zero reproductions. NOTED STRICTNESS LOSS, not a blocker: the old test asserted ownership was correct at T+400ms; the new one asserts it becomes correct within 5s. A regression that merely DELAYS draft ownership by up to 5s would now pass. That is correct semantics for a debounced pipeline, but the invariant is enforced by the poll's timeout rather than by the assert line, which is a tautology of the poll.

title: Two fixed 300ms sleeps in active_match_magnifier.test.js are unprincipled and under-sized
description: Found during oculist-l6m.42 review. The two tests added for l6m.42 use page.waitForTimeout(300) at test/active_match_magnifier.test.js:566 and :620 to settle a race before toggling settings. The implementer added them to fix a reported false-negative negative control, but the reviewer could not reproduce that false negative: reducing the settle wait to 0ms still produced a clean negative-control failure 3/3. Worse, the scroll path defers up to 600ms (content.js:3269), so 300ms does not even cover the branch these tests take. The waits are 'usually-green' rather than principled. Fix: replace both with a condition-based wait on the actual readiness signal. The underlying production race (a deferred animate() at content.js:3293 reading settings at fire time, so a late animate can draw the card on its own) is benign and not worth its own bead - a setting applying a few ms early is not user-visible. Fold into oculist-l6m.32 if that bead is taken first.

title: Flaky: 'repositions on resize' test in active_match_magnifier.test.js intermittently fails under full-suite load
description: During full 'npm test' runs (not isolated), test/active_match_magnifier.test.js's 'repositions on resize instead of stranding in old document coordinates' test intermittently fails with 'card should start centered on the match, dx=-476...ms' — a large offset suggesting the 100ms resize debounce/reflow hadn't settled within the 5000ms waitForFunction window under full-suite CPU contention. Reproduced on 2 of 4 full-suite runs (2026-08-26); passes reliably in isolation (node --test test/active_match_magnifier.test.js). Unrelated to oculist-l6m.42's fix — observed both before and after that change. Likely needs a more generous timeout or a more robust readiness check than the current dx<6 poll.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: CORRECTION - the diagnosis in this bead's description is wrong and will send an implementer to the wrong line. Established during the oculist-l6m.42 review with 10 controlled full-suite runs (5 on the working tree, 5 on a detached HEAD worktree; the resize test failed 0/5 in BOTH, so the flake did not reproduce under controlled conditions at all). The failing assertion is assert.ok(Math.abs(before.dx) < 6, ...) at test/active_match_magnifier.test.js:415, which runs BEFORE any resize happens - so the cause is not an unsettled 100ms resize debounce. The real cause: the readiness gate searchUntilMagnifierWord() polls only the card's TEXT and never its POSITION, so the test proceeds while the card is still at stale coordinates. Fix direction: make the readiness gate assert on position as well as text. Also NOT the same root cause as oculist-l6m.32 - this test uses waitForFunction throughout rather than fixed sleeps, so l6m.32's '106 fixed sleeps' framing does not cover it, though both are the same family of readiness/wall-clock dependence.

title: loadWorkList mount restore writes workListTerms/activeTermIndex without a rescan, so the .20 invariant does not literally hold
description: Found during oculist-l6m.15 review. content.js:4550 (the loadWorkList mount-restore callback) is a 0-to-N workListTerms transition that does NOT call performListSearch() and does NOT reset termRanges - it calls renderChipRow() directly. It is safe today only by virtue of __ocDestroy (content.js:674) zeroing termRanges, and every reopen routing through it, so termRanges is provably [] at that point. Only a theoretical race could beat it (a chrome.storage.session callback losing to a 150ms input debounce plus a 350ms mutation debounce), which in-memory storage makes unreachable in practice. The issue is that the invariant comment landed by oculist-l6m.20 at content.js:2521 states 'every writer of activeTermIndex must call performListSearch() synchronously after setting it', and this call site does not do that. Either route this site through the rescan, or amend the comment to name the __ocDestroy-zeroing exception explicitly. Leaving it as-is means the documented invariant is subtly false, which is the exact failure mode .20 was closed to avoid.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: STOPPED after two failed reviews, left IN_PROGRESS with work UNCOMMITTED on branch epic/oculist-followups. The production change PASSED both reviews and is correct; the test file is what failed, twice, in the same way. PRODUCTION (good, verified twice, content.js SHA-256 020be66f...dccb06 byte-identical across both reviews): content.js:4670 sets termRanges = [] explicitly in the loadWorkList mount-restore callback, making the site locally correct rather than dependent on __ocDestroy zeroing it. The oculist-l6m.20 invariant comment at content.js:2620-2628 was amended to allow two legal forms, and the reviewer verified it is now literally true of all 9 activeTermIndex write sites: :646 init and :742 __ocDestroy and :4194 loadSavedList and :4666 mount-restore all satisfy form 2 (set termRanges consistently), while :3080 activateChip and :3098/:3100/:3102 removeChipAt and :3187 addChipTerm satisfy form 1 (synchronous performListSearch). No writer satisfies neither. REVIEW 1 FAILURE: the no-scan assertion was decorative - injecting a real buildPageIndex() into the restore path left the suite green, because the getComputedStyle baseline was captured after the restore had already completed. Fixed in the second pass via installRestoreProbe(), which brackets the callback synchronously inside a patched chrome.storage.session.get; the reviewer reproduced that injecting buildPageIndex() now correctly fails with 3 !== 2. That part is genuinely fixed. REVIEW 2 FAILURE, still outstanding: the out-of-range test's NAME and comment claim it pins normalizeWorkList's clamp, and the describe header repeats the claim. It does not. The reviewer deleted the clamp at content.js:108 and the suite stayed 5/5 green, proving the mutation was live with a peek hook showing activeTermIndex = 99 at the callback. The test stays green only because of renderChipRow's tolerance (isActive = i === activeTermIndex never matching), which the comment explicitly disclaims as not being what it tests. Both halves of the comment are backwards, and the previous vaguer name was net better than the new specific-but-wrong one. TO FINISH: either assert the observed index is -1 (a value-level assertion that diverges at 99), or strip the mechanism claim from the test name, its comment, and describe-header claim (3), describing it as what it is - an end-to-end no-throw/no-active-chip render check that does not distinguish sanitizer from renderer. Nit: the comment cites normalizeWorkList at content.js:102-109; it is actually at 103-110. NOTE THE PATTERN worth human attention: on a bead whose entire subject is documentation promising what the code does not enforce, the implementer shipped exactly that defect twice.

title: Toggling a vision setting does not redraw the current match
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.39 review. Pre-existing, shared by magnifier and textLabels.

The chrome.storage.onChanged listener (content.js:5355-5360) does not call
repositionActiveOverlays(), so flipping Match Labels or the new Magnifier toggle does not swap
the overlay in or out on the match currently on screen. The change only appears on the next
navigation or redraw.

A user toggling the setting to see what it does gets no feedback and reasonably concludes it is
broken.

Done: a vision-settings change redraws the active match's overlays in place; a test toggles the
magnifier with a match on screen and asserts the card appears without navigating.

title: Nothing tests the magnifier's font scaling or truncation
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.39 review. The code is correct (the reviewer verified it at
content.js:1975-1979) but no test protects it.

Untested:
- font-size derived from the MATCH's own computed font-size x 2.5, clamped to 16-48px. This was
  called out in the bead as the point most likely to be got wrong, precisely because bead .11
  records the same mistake being made with getBeaconScale() for chip sizing. A regression here
  would be silent.
- the ~24-character truncation with ellipsis for long matches.

Also minor, same file: test/active_match_magnifier.test.js shares one browser page across the
whole file, so one failure cascades into later tests. Harmless while green, noisier when red.

Done: tests pin the x2.5 derivation, both clamp bounds, and the truncation; the suite isolates
its page per test or resets state between them.

title: Chip accessible-name tests assert the raw attribute and skip two states
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.16 review. The behaviour is correct (the reviewer verified it live via
the CDP accessibility tree), but the committed tests are weaker than the verification was.

1. test/chip_count_accessibility.test.js:145 and :156 assert getAttribute('aria-label'), the raw
   attribute, rather than the computed accessible name. Those differ whenever name computation
   changes precedence, which is exactly the kind of regression this test exists to catch.
2. No test covers the two subtle states: a cap-starved chip (skipped because the total match cap
   was hit, lands in the sparse-array undefined bucket and must announce no count) and a Lite Mode
   chip (announces the real count from countMatchesOnly). Both were verified by hand only, so a
   regression in either would go unnoticed.

Done: the assertions read the computed accessible name, and both the cap-starved and Lite Mode
states have coverage.

title: restoreActiveChip claims 'no match' for an unscanned chip via the input debounce
description:
Found during the oculist-l6m.19 re-review. Same false-claim class as the regression .19 fixed,
reached through a different entry point, so .19's guard does not cover it.

restoreActiveChip (content.js:2499-2501) writes i18n.noMatch for an unscanned chip when
reached via the INPUT DEBOUNCE rather than via findNext. Repro: against a restored but
unscanned working list, type a draft then clear the input. The debounce fires,
restoreActiveChip runs, and the count reads "no match" for a chip whose term may well have
matches on the page, because it has never been scanned.

Count and nav still agree (nav disabled, nothing highlighted), so this is cosmetic, but it is
the extension stating something false about the page.

The distinction .19 established is the fix: termRanges[i] === undefined means never scanned
(show blank), an empty array means scanned with genuinely zero matches (show "no match").
Apply the same test here.

Done: an unscanned chip restored via the debounce path shows a blank count, not "no match";
a test covers type-then-clear against a restored unscanned list.

title: welcome.js localStorage fallback contradicts the privacy policy
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.10 review. Low severity, pre-existing.

extension/welcome.js:665,672 read and write localStorage['oc-settings'], which contradicts
PRIVACY.md's statement that Oculist writes to no storage area other than the ones listed.

It is a dead fallback branch: chrome.storage.sync is always defined on an extension page, so
no user data actually lands in localStorage. But the policy sentence is absolute and the code
is not.

Done: delete the dead branch, or soften the policy sentence to match. Deleting is preferable,
since an absolute privacy claim is worth more than an unreachable fallback.

title: loadSavedList does not clear the pending search debounce
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.9 review.

loadSavedList (content.js:3615) does not clearTimeout(debounceTimer). Typing a draft and then
loading a list inside the 150ms debounce window lets the debounce fire afterwards with
input.value === '', reaching restoreActiveChip() -> performSearch('') with
activeTermIndex === -1.

Benign today (it clears to the empty state) but it is an unintended scan-adjacent call on a
path whose whole contract is "loading runs no scan".

Done: loadSavedList clears the pending debounce; a test loads a list mid-debounce.

title: Theme hover colour reads settings.theme instead of the resolved theme
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.9 review. Three sites, same mistake, fix together.

content.js:4888 (new, from .9), :4303 and :4741 (both pre-existing) use
settings.theme === 'dark' rather than the already-in-scope resolved activeTheme (:4176).
Under theme 'system' with a dark OS, the hover tint renders the light-mode value.

Done: all three use the resolved theme; a test covers system-theme + dark OS.

title: Saved-list storage rough edges
description:
Three minor findings from the oculist-l6m.8 review.

1. deleteList (content.js:378) reuses the SAVE failure message on a delete failure, so a
   failed delete tells the user "delete a saved list and try again". Needs its own string.
2. readListIndex (content.js:272-277) counts junk keys toward the 50-list cap, while
   listSavedLists hides them. A corrupted oc-list-* key could block saving while the user
   sees fewer than 50 lists and cannot work out why.
3. Note only, not fixable with the chrome.storage API: an inherent TOCTOU between the cap
   read (content.js:304) and the write (content.js:314) means two devices sitting at 49
   lists can both pass the check.

Done: 1 and 2 fixed, 3 recorded as a comment where the race lives.

title: Saved-list storage: three untested branches
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.8 review. The behaviour is correct (the reviewer verified all three
by hand via a CDP probe) but the suite does not cover them, so a regression would ship silently.

1. generateListId's collision loop (content.js:217-226) has ZERO coverage. The existing
   assertion notStrictEqual(second.list.id, first.list.id) passes even if the function
   ignored existingIds entirely.
2. The 10-term and 100-char caps in sanitizeListTerms are untested, despite being a stated
   done-criterion of .8. Verified by hand: 16 terms in -> 10 out, 150-char term -> exactly 100.
3. The 50-list cap test catches a permissive off-by-one (> vs >=) but not an over-strict one,
   because no test saves the 50th list successfully.

Done: each of the three has a test that fails against the corresponding wrong implementation.

title: Consolidate the six window.__oc* test-only hooks
description:
Do this AFTER oculist-l6m.9, so the UI tests exist and can make some hooks redundant.

There are now six test-reachability hooks on the isolated-world window: __ocLoadWorkList and
__ocSaveWorkList from .2, plus __ocSaveList, __ocListSavedLists, __ocRenameList, and
__ocDeleteList from .8. Plus the pre-existing __ocToggle and __ocDestroy, which are a real
call path and stay.

Two reviews have now confirmed empirically that these land in the extension's isolated world
and are undefined in the host page, so this is not a security issue. It is accumulating
production surface that exists only for tests, and .2's review already warned against growing it.

The hooks were genuinely necessary: they are IIFE closures, CDP Runtime.evaluate only reaches
globals, and testing through chrome.storage directly would test Chrome's API rather than this
code.

Done: the six test-only hooks are collapsed into a single window.__ocTest namespace, or
deleted where .9's UI tests reach the same behaviour through the interface.

title: Match-cap feedback is misleading in two ways
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.7 review. Both are user-facing copy/affordance problems, not logic
errors.

1. The notice reads "Showing the first 2000 matches. Remove a term for a complete count."
   but the cap is checked BEFORE materialising each term, so the real total can reach 2997.
   The new cap test documents this. The number in the message is simply not true. This
   string came from the v1.7.0 design doc, so the spec is the source of the error.
   Fix direction: say "Showing about the first 2000 matches" or check the cap after
   materialising and report the real figure.

2. A starved chip (skipped because the cap was hit) renders a BLANK count, which is visually
   identical to "not scanned yet" (content.js:2591). The cap notice mitigates this globally
   but the two per-chip states are indistinguishable, so the user cannot tell which terms
   were actually skipped.
   Fix direction: render a distinct marker on starved chips.

Done: the notice states a number that matches reality, and a starved chip is visually
distinct from an unscanned one.

title: traverse() duplicates a narrower check instead of using isOculistNode()
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.4 review.

The self-match fix added an identity check `child !== wrap` to traverse(). It is sufficient
today, because traverse() starts at document.body and every beacon, marker, and label is
mounted on document.documentElement, while oc-global-highlight-styles is a <style> already
covered by SKIP_TAGS.

But it is a partial duplicate of the existing isOculistNode() helper and will silently miss
any future Oculist-owned node mounted under body. The next person to add one gets phantom
matches with no failing test.

Done: traverse() routes through isOculistNode(), or the identity check carries a comment
explaining why it deliberately does not.

title: Chip sizing keys off getBeaconScale(), the beacon knob
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.3 review.

Chip text size is derived from getBeaconScale() (the vision-profile beacon size s/m/l/xl).
At xl (2.25) chip text renders at 27px. That is the only scale hook in content.js, but it
is the BEACON knob, not a UI-text knob, so chip sizing is riding on an unrelated setting.

Needs a design decision: either introduce a separate UI-text scale, or clamp the chip
scale, or accept the coupling deliberately and comment it.

Done: chips render at a sensible size across all four beacon sizes, and whichever way it
is resolved is recorded in a comment.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: RESOLUTION: clamped, not a separate UI-text scale. getChipScale() (content.js:487-494) clamps getBeaconScale() to [1, 1.5] for chip use; the 10 real beacon call sites keep the full 0.7-2.25 range. Chip text is therefore 12px at s/m and 18px at l/xl, down from 8.4px/27px at the extremes. Rejected a separate UI-text scale as a new setting + UI + persistence + migration for a cosmetic issue. Pinned by a test in test/chip_row.test.js asserting computed font-size across all four beacon sizes; mutation-verified to fail at both ends.

title: Release chores for v1.7.0
description:
Steps:
1. Bump repo/extension/manifest.json version to 1.7.0.
2. Add a 1.7.0 entry to repo/CHANGELOG.md describing multi-term lists, saved lists, and the
   carry-over behaviour.
3. Confirm no new manifest permissions were added. 'storage' was already granted, so there
   is no new Chrome Web Store permission justification to write. If a permission did creep
   in, stop and report rather than shipping it.
4. Run `npm test` and `npm run build`, and confirm the zip builds.

Done: version bumped, changelog entry present, permissions unchanged, tests and build pass.
notes:
BLOCKING ADDITION from the .9 review — PRIVACY.md is now factually wrong and this is a Chrome Web Store disclosure issue, not a docs nit.

PRIVACY.md currently states, all three of which are false as of v1.7.0:
- 'Everything Oculist stores lives in chrome.storage.sync under a single key, oc-settings'
  -> saved lists now live under their own oc-list-<id> keys
- 'writes to no other storage area'
  -> the working term list lives in chrome.storage.session
- 'keeps no history of what you searched for'
  -> saved lists ARE a persisted, cross-device-synced record of search terms

Update PRIVACY.md to describe all three storage areas accurately and to state plainly that
saved lists persist search terms and sync across the user's devices. Check docs/privacy.html
for the same claims and keep the two consistent.

NOTE: PRIVACY.md, docs/index.html and docs/privacy.html have uncommitted edits that predate
this epic and are unrelated to it. Do not sweep them into your commit. Report what you find
there rather than reverting or committing someone else's in-progress work.

title: Fix clipped box-shadow glow on Impact Burst effect
description: In repo/extension/content.js, animateImpactBurst()'s burst-shape element has both clip-path (for the star polygon) and box-shadow (for glow) — clip-path clips box-shadow, so the glow never renders. Move the glow to a separate unclipped element behind the star, or drop the box-shadow. Cosmetic only, found during review of oculist-y9h.1.
close_reason: Obsolete — the Impact Burst effect (oculist-y9h.1) was reverted in 2554612, so animateImpactBurst() and its clipped box-shadow no longer exist in extension/content.js. Re-file if the effect is ever reintroduced.

title: playground resize dissolve is swallowed inside the pre-fire scroll suppression window
description:
Noted by the oculist-1ta.27 reviewer, 2026-09-12, from a code read rather than a failure.

trigger() checks suppressScrollDissolve for BOTH event types, but that flag exists only to stop the effect's own ensureVisible() scrollIntoView from dissolving the effect it just fired. Nothing in these effects triggers a resize, so the flag has no business gating resize.

CONSEQUENCE. A real user resize landing inside the pre-fire suppression window (at most SCROLL_QUIET_MS after the last scroll event) is swallowed. The handler returns without setting settled, so no listener leaks and a later resize still fires normally. It is a missed FIRST resize inside a sub-second window, not a lifecycle defect, which is why this is P4.

FIX DIRECTION. Gate the suppression check on the event type, so scroll consults suppressScrollDissolve and resize does not. Confirm the pre-fire suppression still works for scroll afterwards, because that is the severe case: if it breaks, effects dissolve themselves the instant they fire.

DONE-CRITERIA
- A resize inside the suppression window dissolves the effect.
- Firing via the sidebar button with #match out of view still does NOT self-dissolve, at both scroll extremes.

title: occlusion-sweep NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT comment: stale t=230 sampling claim and un-re-measured counts
description:
occlusion-sweep.js's NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT comment block has a stale claim about sampling, and per-effect counts that have not been re-measured since the sampler changed.

Found by the final oculist-ey2e reviewer, 2026-09-10. It is outside ey2e's text: the block is oculist-hgt's.

1. STALE: lines ~396-398 say the sample loop "never takes a t=230 sample ... that is bead oculist-1ta.21". sampleEffect now always adds maxEnd as a final sample (~lines 719-725), so the sentence no longer describes the code.
2. UNVERIFIED: the per-effect pixel counts on ~lines 393-394 (9356, 4137, 1560, 1031, 819) were measured before ey2e extracted sampleEffect and before 1ta.21 changed sampling. They may still be right, since ey2e's grid output was byte-identical for batflight and arrowshot, but the exempt keys were not re-swept.

DONE-CRITERIA
- Re-sweep the six exempt keys and either confirm each quoted count or update it, recording the date.
- Correct or delete the t=230 sentence so it matches sampleEffect.
- Comment-only change; the batflight and arrowshot grid output is unchanged.

title: prefire-scroll-abort-check cannot tell the target comparison from the loose inView band
description:
Found by mutation, by the oculist-1ta.13 reviewer, 2026-09-09. A coverage gap in the check, not a defect in the code.

WHAT THE MUTATION SHOWED. Replacing ensureVisible's intended-target comparison with the loose inView band comparison, which is the design the code comment explicitly says was rejected, STILL PASSES prefire-scroll-abort-check.js. The settle gate alone catches every abort the fixture produces, so the check never exercises the difference between the two comparisons.

THE REAL CODE DOES DISCRIMINATE, which is why this is a check gap rather than a bug: an in-band-but-off-centre match at resting deltas of -259, -189, -89, +111 and +221 draws nothing under the real implementation, while the band mutant draws 3 on all of them.

WHY IT MATTERS. The comment in ensureVisible records that the band was considered and rejected as too generous. If a future edit quietly reverted to it, this check would stay green. That is the same shape as the harness gaps already tracked in oculist-e2w and oculist-ey2e: the test passes for a reason other than the one it claims.

FIX: add a single in-band-off-centre row, e.g. scroll so the match sits inside the band but well off centre, and assert the effect is suppressed. That one row makes the band mutant fail.

DONE-CRITERIA

- Substituting the inView band for the target comparison makes prefire-scroll-abort-check.js fail.
- The existing scenario A and B rows are unchanged and still pass.
- The check still fails against the pre-oculist-1ta.13 source.

title: fxBatFlight's mist fade now animates transform-origin on every landing, which may have dropped it off the compositor
description:
Noted by the oculist-1ta.8 reviewer, 2026-09-09. LOW CONFIDENCE AND UNVERIFIED, recorded so it is not lost rather than because it is known to bite.

WHAT CHANGED. oculist-1ta.8 made transform-origin a keyframe property of the mist's fade-out so the below landing could anchor at the top. The value is unchanged for the other three landings (50% 100%), and full-viewport hashes across 105 frames are byte-identical, so nothing renders differently. But the property is now PRESENT in the keyframes for all four landings where before it was absent.

THE CONCERN. Chromium cannot composite transform-origin. Animating it may have moved the fade from the compositor to the main thread, which cuts directly against the mist's own comment claiming that only its opacity and transform animate so there is no forced main-thread re-raster. If that comment is now false, it is the same class of stale-comment problem this file has repeatedly produced.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN 1ta.8. Setting transform-origin outside the keyframes is not trivially available there: the fade is delay-scheduled, and the base value must stay 50% 100% for the grow-in phase, so a static assignment would break the entrance.

FIRST STEP: measure rather than reason. Check in DevTools or via a compositing probe whether the fade still runs on the compositor with the property in its keyframes. If it does, delete this bead and correct nothing. If it does not, either restore compositing (perhaps by splitting grow-in and fade-out into separate animations with different static origins) or correct the mist's comment so it stops claiming a property it no longer has.

DONE-CRITERIA

- It is established by measurement whether the fade still composites.
- If it does not, either compositing is restored or the comment stops claiming it.
- The oculist-1ta.8 result still holds: zero changed pixels in the match rect on the below landing.

title: fxFootTap comment cites a VERIFY section that does not exist, and a left landing that does not happen
description:
Found by the oculist-1ta.23 reviewer, 2026-09-09. Pre-existing and unrelated to that fix; both halves of one sentence are wrong.

THE COMMENT, effects-playground.html around line 5663: 'Verified empirically below (VERIFY section) at both a right-landing (900x700) and a mirrored left-landing (320x900).'

WRONG TWICE:
1. There is no VERIFY section anywhere in the file. The reference points at nothing.
2. 320x900 lands RIGHT at every font size, verified across the grid both before and after the oculist-1ta.23 diff. It is not a left-landing case, so the comment names a mirrored landing that the cited viewport does not produce.

WHY IT MATTERS. Someone checking the mirrored path would use 320x900 on this comment's authority, see a right landing, and conclude the mirroring is broken when it is not. oculist-1ta.23 had to force a left landing with a throwaway in-page hack precisely because no ordinary viewport in the grid produces one.

WORTH ESTABLISHING while fixing: whether ANY viewport in the 8x12 sweep grid produces a left landing. If none does, the mirrored path is untested by the sweep entirely, which is a bigger finding than the comment and should be recorded as such.

DONE-CRITERIA

- The comment cites something that exists, or the citation goes.
- The viewport named for the mirrored landing actually produces one, or the comment says no grid viewport does.
- If no grid viewport exercises the mirrored path, that is stated in the file rather than left implicit.
close_reason: Folded into oculist-g1d2. The fxFootTap comment no longer cites a nonexistent VERIFY section and states that no grid viewport lands foottap left (0 of 96, tallied). It names forced-left-1/2/3 as the rows that exercise the mirrored path. Both g1d2 reviews passed all three criteria.

title: fxFootTap's motion-line fan now sits at 11.68px, just inside the nominal GAP floor
description:
Measured by the oculist-1ta.23 reviewer, 2026-09-09, across the full 8x12 grid. Worst case 11.68px at 1280x900 font 22, down from 17.96px before that bead scaled the reach reserves. Not an occlusion: the pixel sweep is still 0 dirty of 96.

WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING. The comment at effects-playground.html:5906 budgets the motion fan's 1.71px inward creep against the +2 sampling margin. Two things have drifted from that:
- The fan stroke's own 1px half-width is not in the budget.
- The margin is no longer 2px. It is 2*scale, about 1.81px at font 24, because oculist-1ta.23 correctly scaled it.

So the fan is now inside the nominal GAP of 12 by a small amount, and the comment that explains why it is safe no longer adds up. The pixels say it is fine; the reasoning no longer shows why.

FIX DIRECTIONS: either widen the budget to include the stroke half-width and use the scaled margin, or state plainly that the fan is permitted inside GAP and that the pixel sweep is what guards it. The second is honest and cheaper.

DONE-CRITERIA

- The comment's arithmetic matches the code, including the stroke half-width and the scaled margin.
- node occlusion-sweep.js foottap stays 96/96 clean.
- If the fan is deliberately allowed inside GAP, the file says so rather than implying it clears.

title: Four prototype harnesses still hard-code the absolute playwright path
description:
Reported by the oculist-1ta.21 implementer and confirmed by its reviewer, 2026-09-09. That bead fixed the path in occlusion-sweep.js only, which was its stated scope; these four were deliberately left.

STILL HARD-CODED, all in artifacts/prototypes/ in the outer repo:
- deferred-mount-scroll-dissolve-check.js
- overlapping-run-scroll-dissolve-check.js
- raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js
- style-attr-byte-exact-check.js

WHY IT MATTERS. The absolute path breaks every one of these in any other checkout, which makes the whole prototype harness suite non-portable. occlusion-sweep.js now resolves it as path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'repo', 'node_modules', 'playwright'), verified by the reviewer running it from a relocated directory through a symlinked ../../repo. Copy that shape.

NOTE the cross-repo dependency this encodes: these harnesses live in the OUTER repo and reach into the INNER repo's node_modules. The relative path makes that dependency explicit rather than hiding it behind an absolute path, which is an improvement, but it does mean the harnesses only run when both repos sit in their usual layout. Worth a comment saying so.

DONE-CRITERIA

- All four resolve playwright relative to __dirname.
- Each still exits 0 when run normally.
- At least one is verified to run from a relocated copy, as occlusion-sweep.js was.

title: style-attr-byte-exact-check's double-fire sample point is hand-derived from the 6-char fixture and can drift into a vacuous pass
description:
Noted by the oculist-6wo reviewer, 2026-09-09, while confirming that bead's new double-fire cases genuinely race. Not a defect today; the check works and was proven to discriminate by reverting the guard.

WHAT IS FRAGILE. measureDoubleFire's timing constants are hand-derived from the current fixture text, <mark id='match'>aurora</mark>, six characters. The reviewer verified the arithmetic against it: letterwave's stale restore lands at t=905, run 2 fires at t=300 and its own restore at t=1205, and the sample at t=955 sits inside that 250ms window. scramble's stale restore is at 1470, sample 1520, run 2's at 1770.

THE HAZARD. Both effects' durations scale with the number of characters in the match text. If the fixture's text ever changes length, the sample point drifts out of the overlap window and the check PASSES VACUOUSLY, reporting green while measuring nothing. That is the same silent-false-pass shape as oculist-l2d's fixed sample instant and oculist-l92's empty sweep, which is why it is worth closing rather than tolerating.

The file comment already says the constants are fixture-derived, so this is a known ceiling rather than a hidden one.

FIX DIRECTIONS. Either derive the sample point from the fixture's actual text length at runtime instead of hardcoding it, or assert that the sample landed inside the intended window (the way oculist-l92 made an empty sweep fail loudly) so drift fails rather than passes. The second is cheaper and matches how the sibling harnesses were hardened.

DONE-CRITERIA

- Changing the fixture's match text length does not silently turn the double-fire cases green.
- Reverting the oculist-6wo guard still fails both double-fire cases.
- The existing byte-exact cases are unaffected.

title: occlusion-sweep: fxScramble is nondeterministic and not exempt, so 'node occlusion-sweep.js scramble' always exits 1
description:
Found by the oculist-hgt reviewer, 2026-09-09, while confirming determinism was restored. PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to that fix: scramble is nondeterministic between runs both with the fix and at HEAD before it.

WHAT HAPPENS. node occlusion-sweep.js scramble exits 1. fxScramble picks glyphs with a random pick(GLYPHS) SYNCHRONOUSLY at fire time, so the rendered pixels differ run to run. The timer neutralization cannot help, because the randomness is not deferred, it happens in the synchronous body the sweep exists to measure.

WHY IT IS NOT COVERED TODAY. scramble is absent from NOT_MATCH_CLEARANCE_CONTRACT, the exemption set oculist-aun added, so its dirty count still sets the exit code. That set was built from the six deferred-mount effects the oculist-ucs reviewer measured; scramble was never in that group and was never considered.

THE FORK, and it should be decided rather than defaulted. Either scramble belongs in the exemption set on the same footing as the others (it mutates the mark's own glyphs by design, so a match-clearance contract arguably never applied to it), OR the sweep should seed the randomness so scramble becomes measurable, which is strictly more valuable but needs a seam in the playground rather than the harness. The first is a labelling change; the second buys a real measurement.

NOTE the interaction with oculist-kny: fxScramble now routes its colour restore through captureStyleAttr/restoreStyleAttr, so the style-attribute side is already deterministic. It is only the glyph choice that is not.

DONE-CRITERIA

- node occlusion-sweep.js scramble either exits 0 for a stated reason, or produces identical per-scenario output across two consecutive runs.
- Whichever branch is taken, the reason is recorded in the file next to the other per-effect evidence rather than only in this bead.
- The exempted six and batflight/arrowshot are unaffected.

title: occlusion-sweep neutralization covers only setTimeout, and its control asserts counting rather than dropping
description:
Two residual risks noted by the oculist-hgt reviewer, 2026-09-09, neither exploitable today, both in artifacts/prototypes/occlusion-sweep.js.

1. THE CONTROL PROVES THE COUNTER MOVED, NOT THAT THE CALLBACK DIED. runNeutralizationControl asserts suppressedCount incremented. Counting and dropping live in the same four-line wrapper inside installTimerNeutralizationHook, so today one implies the other, but an edit that increments and then still schedules would pass the control. Cheap hardening: have the control also assert that no deferred .fx element appears after a wait, which is the property actually wanted.

2. setInterval AND requestAnimationFrame ARE NOT INTERCEPTED. requestAnimationFrame has zero occurrences in the playground, so no exposure. setInterval has one, fxScramble's 40ms ticker, and its clearInterval sits inside a setTimeout that the hook now suppresses, so the ticker survives the run and is only stopped when the harness drains restorers via clearFx. Harmless today because scramble measures samples=1 and maxEnd=0, but an effect combining an interval with synchronous animations would reintroduce exactly the non-determinism oculist-hgt fixed, and the canary cannot see a new deferral route.

WHY P4 NOT HIGHER. Both are latent. The measured behaviour is correct now, verified by 4 byte-identical runs each of inkbloom and comet including under CPU contention, and by full per-scenario equivalence with the pre-eke tree.

DONE-CRITERIA

- The neutralization control asserts the absence of deferred work, not only that a counter moved.
- setInterval is either intercepted the same way or a comment states why it deliberately is not, in the way oculist-q9r did for the playground's own shadow.
- The four historical failure shapes still exit 1: hook missing, hook installed after goto, canary pointed at a timer-free effect, and whatever new shape the interval decision creates.

title: instant_scroll stale-draw test: __ocRedrawAt is dead, its doc comment is stale, and solo-run timeout headroom shrank
description:
Three leftovers noted by the oculist-4z3 reviewer, 2026-09-09, none blocking. All in test/instant_scroll_close_reopen_no_stale_draw.test.js unless stated.

1. TIMEOUT HEADROOM ON UNSCALED SOLO RUNS. The old wait budgeted (deadline - now) + POLL_TIMEOUT, roughly 5s of slack. The sibling-timer wait budgets POLL_TIMEOUT alone, 5000ms, against a wait of about 3.6s, so roughly 1.4s of slack. Under npm test the scale factor makes it about 6.4s, which is fine. This is now the one place in the file where a number still matters, which is worth noting given oculist-4z3 existed to remove exactly that.

2. DEAD WRITE AND A STALE DOC COMMENT. window.__ocRedrawAt is written and never read. armRedrawCounter's doc comment (around line 156-158) still claims callers use it to wait for quiet, which describes the mechanism oculist-4z3 replaced. Pre-existing since oculist-3wq for the write; the comment is now actively misleading.

3. ASYMMETRIC ARM. The sibling is armed as a bare orig(fn, stretched), so this is undefined, while the orphan uses orig.apply(window, args). Works in Chrome, verified empirically, and the two are otherwise identical. Cosmetic asymmetry only, but it invites the reader to wonder whether the difference is load-bearing.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING. The FIFO evidence cited in the code comment (0 violations in 200 trials at 50ms and 15 at the real 4000ms delay) was produced by a scratch script that was deleted. The claim is not independently checkable from the tree. If that property is meant to be load-bearing long-term, the trial script belongs in artifacts/prototypes/ where the other checks live.

DONE-CRITERIA

- __ocRedrawAt is either read or removed, and armRedrawCounter's doc comment describes the mechanism actually in use.
- The solo-run timeout budget is either widened or a comment states the measured margin.
- The mutation check still fails 2 !== 1 with clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer removed.
close_reason:
All three items done. __ocRedrawAt's dead write removed after confirming the three sibling stale-draw tests each write AND read their own private copy, so nothing depended on this file's write and no sibling now reads undefined. armRedrawCounter's doc comment rewritten to describe the sibling-flag mechanism actually in use. Solo-run headroom widened rather than merely documented: STRETCH_DELAY_MS = 4000 now backs both the injected patch and the wait budget (POLL_TIMEOUT + STRETCH_DELAY_MS = 9000 unscaled against an observed ~3.5s wait), and it deduplicates a hardcoded 4000 so the two cannot drift apart. The sibling arm is now orig.apply(window, [fn, stretched]), symmetric with the orphan.

FAILED REVIEW ONCE, on exactly the thing the bead exists to prevent: the rewritten doc comment ended 'the count itself is only read afterward, for the final assertion', which was false. __ocRedrawCount is also read before the stretch as a positive-edge gate proving m1's own draw landed. Corrected to state both reads and that neither watches for quiescence; an independent re-check confirmed exactly four occurrences (init, observer increment, the pre-stretch positive-edge wait, and the read feeding the final assertion), so 'read twice' is now accurate.

The FIFO comment was also tightened rather than left soft. It had been reduced to an appeal to convention after the trial script was deleted; same-delay ordering is in fact spec-mandated, and the re-check corrected the wording to registration order within one global (same ordering identifier) rather than the by-handle/per-agent framing I first wrote, with a pointer to oculist-4z3 for the empirical trials.

Criterion 3 verified independently: commenting out clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer gives a real AssertionError 2 !== 1 at 4474ms, not a timeout, with content.js restored to sha256 831f7fe8. Full suite 321 pass / 0 fail / 72 suites.

title: raw-state harness: an empty sweep would read as -Infinity and pass the scrolled arm
description:
Found by the oculist-l2d reviewer, 2026-09-09, while confirming that bead's rAF sweep. Latent, not exploitable as written, but it sits in exactly the place l2d exists to protect.

WHAT. sweepBodyAnimCount's result is reduced with maxCount = Math.max(...counts). On an EMPTY counts array that yields -Infinity, and the scrolled arm's assertion is maxCount < threshold, so an empty sweep reads as a clean PASS.

WHY IT DOES NOT BITE TODAY. counts cannot be empty: the sweep's first tick samples before the loop condition is checked. And an empty sweep would fail the CONTROL arm loudly, since that arm requires maxCount >= threshold, so both arms could not silently pass together.

WHY IT IS WORTH CLOSING ANYWAY. The whole point of oculist-l2d was removing a check that could degrade into a silent false PASS on the falsifiability arm. This is the same failure shape one refactor away: anything that makes the sweep return early, throw and get swallowed, or start after the window has closed would restore it.

FIX: assert samples > 0 (or counts.length > 0) before reducing, and fail loudly if the sweep recorded nothing.

ALSO IN THE SAME FILE, cosmetic: the header comment narrates depthdive's window as 550-950 while animSweep uses [520,1020] and the measured span is 581-981. Same phenomenon, three different number pairs. Make them agree.

DONE-CRITERIA

- An empty or missing sweep fails loudly on both arms rather than passing the scrolled one.
- The depthdive window numbers agree between the comment and the code.
- The existing two-sided falsifiability still holds: deleting either guard fails the scrolled arm, stopping either animation fails the control arm.
close_reason: The -Infinity hole is closed. sweepBodyAnimCount's result now carries empty (counts.length === 0), maxCount is null rather than -Infinity when empty, and main forces animSweepOk false on BOTH arms before any threshold comparison, with a message that names the empty sweep and says the comparison is meaningless rather than reporting a bare count mismatch. Reviewer PASS having proven the guard generally rather than against the one tested shape: empty counts with 0 samples, empty counts with 37 samples, an undefined return and a missing counts field all fail loudly (the last two as FATAL TypeErrors with a stack at measureOne), while counts=[1] with samples=0 correctly does NOT trip the guard and runs the real comparison. maxCount=null traced to both its consumers, both downstream of the short-circuit, never string-formatted and never compared, so there is no null < threshold path recreating the bug in a new costume. All four falsifiability arms re-established independently against mutant playground copies rather than inherited, each failing exactly one row via animSweepOk. Depthdive's three number pairs are now labelled by what they mean rather than flattened: 550-950 nominal (setTimeout 550 plus duration 400), about 581-981 measured, [520,1020] the padded sweep window; the header's wrong claim that the sweep covered 550-950 is corrected. One factual error in the new comment was fixed before commit: a swallowed throw does not hang, Playwright 1.61 rejects it at the 30s default timeout and the harness exits 1 with a FATAL, which is louder than the comment claimed.

title: fxLetterwave/fxScramble: a stale restorer from a previous run un-hides the mark mid-flight of the next
description:
Found by the oculist-kny reviewer, 2026-09-09, while confirming that bead's fix. PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by kny: the same behaviour is present on the old direct-property code, so this is not a regression from routing through captureStyleAttr/restoreStyleAttr.

WHAT HAPPENS. Firing fxLetterwave or fxScramble twice inside roughly 2 seconds lets the FIRST run's restorer fire in the middle of the SECOND run. The mark is un-hidden early, so the colour comes back while the second run still expects it hidden.

WHY. Each run adds a restorer and each run's terminal setTimeout calls it, but neither effect participates in the run-identity machinery: they do not call armScrollDissolve, and the restorer closure is not tied to the run that created it. So run 1's timeout lands during run 2 and restores run 2's element.

WHY P4. The playground fires one effect at a time in normal use, so this needs deliberate rapid re-firing to see. It is visual only: the final state is still correct, because run 2's own restorer fires afterwards and restores the same captured string. Nothing is stranded.

RELATED. oculist-eke gave mount() real run identity via the setTimeout shadow, and oculist-9j4/oculist-cst guard deferred callbacks with it. This is the same class of problem in the two effects that were never brought into that scheme. Whoever picks this up should check whether the existing run-identity guard applies here rather than inventing a second mechanism.

FIRST STEP: establish whether the effects can simply adopt the mount()-style run-identity check in their restorer, or whether their restorer runs on a path where that identity is not in scope.

DONE-CRITERIA

- Re-firing either effect within 2s does not let the earlier run's restorer touch the later run's mark.
- The single-run path is unchanged, byte-exact restore included (the oculist-kny result still holds).
- A runnable check fails if it regresses; style-attr-byte-exact-check.js is the natural home.
close_reason:
Both effects' terminal setTimeout callbacks now carry an identity guard, so a superseded run's restorer no longer un-hides the next run's mark. Reproduced before fixing: midColor came back rgb(10, 20, 30) mid-flight of run 2 for both effects.

THE GUARD DELIBERATELY DIFFERS from the mount()/fxStamp/fxDepthdive shape: it uses only owner !== currentRunEls and omits owner.dissolved. The reviewer proved that omission CORRECT AND NECESSARY rather than merely different, by applying the established shape and running the raw-state harness: exit 1, with letterwave and scramble both stranded at match style attr='color: transparent;'. armScrollDissolve's onScroll sets els.dissolved and fades fx nodes but never touches restorers, which are drained in exactly one place, clearFx. So a merely-dissolved run still needs its own terminal timeout to restore, and the dissolved clause would strand the mark hidden forever.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE: the description said these two effects do not call armScrollDissolve. That is stale post-uc1, which made rect() arm it centrally for every run. They do dissolve, which is exactly why the dissolved clause would have been live and harmful rather than inert.

Stranding ruled out for the identity half by construction and by grep: rect() is invoked at one site, two lines after clearFx, and nothing between them adds a restorer, so currentRunEls cannot be reassigned without a prior full drain. Whenever the guard skips, the restore has already fired. Guard fails open as the established shape does. The divergence is protected: the raw-state harness fails loudly if someone 'corrects' it back.

Criterion 2 intact, byte-exact restore still holds with and without an author color. New double-fire cases in style-attr-byte-exact-check.js verified to genuinely race (letterwave stale restore at 905ms sampled at 955ms against run 2's own at 1205ms). Regression sweep and occlusion-sweep --control all exit 0.

title: fxLetterwave/fxScramble cannot byte-restore a pre-existing author inline style (trailing-semicolon re-serialization)
description:
Found by the oculist-g46 reviewer, 2026-09-08, while confirming that bead's guard is safe. PRE-EXISTING, not caused by g46: verified identical against a HEAD copy.

WHAT HAPPENS. If the match element already carries an author inline style before the effect fires, fxLetterwave and fxScramble restore it as a RE-SERIALIZATION rather than the original string. Measured: style='font-weight: 900' comes back as 'font-weight: 900;', with a trailing semicolon.

WHY. Those two restorers set and clear the property through the .style CSSOM interface (mark.style.color = ''), so what lands back in the attribute is whatever Chromium serializes from the property bag, not the author's original text. The other effects avoid this because they go through captureStyleAttr/restoreStyleAttr, which snapshots and restores the attribute STRING.

WHY IT IS P4. Purely cosmetic in the DOM: computed styles are identical, nothing renders differently, and a trailing semicolon is valid CSS. It only shows up in a byte-exact attribute comparison, which is how the reviewer found it. It also only bites when the page already had an inline style on the match element, which the playground fixture does not.

FIX DIRECTION. Route fxLetterwave and fxScramble through captureStyleAttr/restoreStyleAttr like the others, instead of setting and clearing the property directly. That also folds them into the same empty-attribute guard g46 added, rather than each carrying its own copy.

DONE-CRITERIA

- With an author inline style present on the match element, both effects restore the attribute byte-exactly.
- With no author inline style, no style attribute is left behind, i.e. the oculist-g46 result still holds.
- The colour is still hidden during the effect and restored after, scrolled and unscrolled.
close_reason: fxLetterwave and fxScramble now capture/restore the style attribute STRING via captureStyleAttr/restoreStyleAttr instead of writing mark.style.color directly; their local empty-attribute guards are gone, since restoreStyleAttr carries the oculist-g46 guard. New harness artifacts/prototypes/style-attr-byte-exact-check.js seeds an author inline style (with and without color) and asserts byte-exact restore. Reviewer PASS, running both harnesses and the falsifiability proof independently: new check exit 0 with the fix and exit 1 on all 4 cases without it, raw-state harness exit 0 with matchStyleAttr=null on both arms, colour still hidden mid-flight (asserted at t=50ms). SEVERITY WAS UNDERSTATED: the pre-existing bug dropped the author's color declaration outright, not merely re-serialized it with a trailing semicolon.

title: raw-state harness: fixed 220ms sample point, off-by-one line refs, and an incomplete explanation of what suppresses the stamp shake
description:
Three cosmetic items from the oculist-9j4 reviewer, 2026-09-08, none blocking, all in the same file pair.

1. THE SAMPLE POINT IS A FIXED 220ms. raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js asserts on document.body.getAnimations().length at one instant, midSampleMs 220, to prove the stamp shake does not start on a scrolled run and does on the control. Measured window: animations are live from about 173-180ms to about 295-302ms. The sample actually lands at 222-224ms on the control and 230-246ms on the scrolled arm, the extra being page.mouse.wheel overhead. Headroom is about 45ms early and 76ms late on the control, about 54ms late on the scrolled arm. The scrolled arm is both the tighter one AND the falsifiability arm, so a large overshoot there degrades silently into a false PASS rather than a noisy failure. Under 8-way CPU saturation the landings were unchanged at 223-237ms, and timer slip moves the 170ms start alongside the sample, so drift is partly self-correcting. About 2x the worst observed overshoot: real, but not generous.

FIX: sweep with requestAnimationFrame across 170-300ms and assert on whether any sample saw an animation, instead of one fixed point.

2. OFF-BY-ONE LINE REFERENCES. raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js:91 and :202 cite effects-playground.html:1337-1338 for the guard; it is actually at :1338-1339.

3. AN INCOMPLETE EXPLANATION. raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js:35-36 says the shake 'only starts if mountRunEls === currentRunEls'. True as a necessary condition, but incomplete as an explanation of the case it then asserts on: a scroll-dissolve leaves currentRunEls pointing at the SAME array (armScrollDissolve sets only els.dissolved, around :442), so on the scrolled run it is the owner.dissolved clause, not the identity clause, that does the suppressing. Name both.

DONE-CRITERIA

- The stamp assertion no longer depends on a single fixed sample instant.
- Line references match the code.
- The comment names both clauses and which one fires on a scrolled run.
- Deleting the guard still fails the harness on the scrolled arm, and stopping the shake entirely still fails it on the control arm.
close_reason: The fixed-instant sample is gone: sweepBodyAnimCount runs a requestAnimationFrame loop inside a single page.evaluate, so timing rides the browser clock rather than Playwright IPC. Both effects are swept, not just stamp, since oculist-cst had just added a second fixed sample. Windows: stamp [150,320] threshold 1, depthdive [520,1020] threshold 2. Reviewer PASS having re-run all four falsifiability mutations independently plus a fifth of their own, narrowing fxStamp's guard to the identity clause alone, which fails the scrolled arm and empirically confirms the corrected comment's claim that owner.dissolved is what suppresses there. Observed cadence 10-14 samples for stamp and 33-35 for depthdive, so it is a real sweep. Threshold soundness measured in both directions: depthdive's baseline stays at exactly 1 across the window and 2 is unreachable without the deferred animation. One stale playground citation renumbered to :1352-1353, the duplicate removed.

title: fxDepthdive starts a second body animation from a later setTimeout that survives a scroll-dissolve
description:
Measured by the oculist-9j4 reviewer, 2026-09-08, while confirming that bead's fix. Same artifact oculist-9j4 fixed for fxStamp, in the one effect that genuinely shares its shape.

MEASURED. Fire fxDepthdive, scroll at 60ms. maxBodyAnims reaches 2, with live document.body animations still running 250 to 900ms AFTER the run has been scroll-dissolved. The overlay is gone; the body is still moving.

WHY THIS ONE AND NOT THE OTHER FOUR. The oculist-9j4 review checked all six raw-state effects from oculist-ak5. fxZoompunch, fxLetterwave, fxScramble and fxShockwave all mutate raw state SYNCHRONOUSLY at fire time, when nothing is dissolved yet, so a dissolve check there would be meaningless and their restorer is already the right mechanism. fxStamp was fixable precisely because its raw mutation is deferred. fxDepthdive is the only other effect that starts a body animation from a LATER setTimeout, so it is the only real sibling.

THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN. oculist-9j4 guards fxStamp's deferred callback by reusing the run identity oculist-eke's setTimeout shadow already captures. Apply the same one-line check to fxDepthdive's deferred body animation. Use the null-safe shape mount() uses, so a future routing through the native setTimeout leaves the effect working rather than silently dead.

NOT URGENT. Like fxStamp's, this is visual only: nothing is stranded, the restorer fires unconditionally and the body transform returns to none either way (established under oculist-ak5).

DONE-CRITERIA

- After a mid-flight scroll-dissolve, fxDepthdive starts no new body animation.
- The body transform still reverts to none, scrolled or not, with no non-empty style attribute left behind.
- fxDepthdive is unchanged on the no-scroll path.
- A runnable check fails if it regresses. raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js is the right home; oculist-9j4 added the equivalent getAnimations assertions there for stamp.
close_reason: fxDepthdive's deferred 550ms body animation now carries the same run-identity guard oculist-9j4 gave fxStamp, character-identical to mount()'s null-safe shape, so it fails open if the run identity is ever unavailable. raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js gained a depthdive branch sampling body.getAnimations() at t=700ms: 2 on control, 1 on the scrolled arm. Reviewer PASS with independent measurement: animation window is 581-981ms and the harness sample lands at 716-728ms, so roughly 140ms headroom before and 250ms after. Falsifiability re-proven independently, removing the guard gives exit 1 on the scrolled arm alone while the control still passes at 2. Synchronous fire-time animation and the unconditional restorer untouched; the other four raw-state effects unmodified.

title: Playground setTimeout shadow drops trailing args, and the overlapping-run harness mislabels which guard it mutates
description:
Two cheap cleanups in the oculist-eke work, both confirmed inert today by that bead's reviewer, 2026-09-08. Neither is a defect now; both are traps for the next person editing these files.

1. THE SHADOW'S SIGNATURE. oculist-eke gives mount() run identity by shadowing the global setTimeout inside the IIFE with function setTimeout(fn, delay), so all 45 fx* functions pick it up without being edited. It takes only two named params, so it DROPS trailing arguments: setTimeout(fn, 10, 'X', 'Y') delivers [undefined, undefined]. Its this-binding also differs from the spec (it calls fn() rather than binding the global thisArg).

Inert today, measured: 82 setTimeout call sites in the file, ZERO with more than 2 args, and no code in the IIFE uses this. But a future setTimeout(fn, delay, arg) in a 6100-line file would break silently, which is the worst failure shape.

Related, same mechanism, also inert: setInterval (around :1859, fxScramble) is NOT shadowed, so an interval-scheduled mount would bypass the run-identity guard entirely; that callback does not mount today. And var mountRunEls = null is declared AFTER the shadow, so any future top-level IIFE statement between them that calls setTimeout would capture undefined and get every mount refused. Verified: no setTimeout call currently executes before nativeSetTimeout is assigned.

FIX: accept and forward rest args, and either shadow setInterval the same way or comment that it deliberately is not.

2. THE HARNESS DOCSTRING MISLABELS ITS MUTATION. overlapping-run-scroll-dissolve-check.js:53-54 names the guard it falsifies as 'owner !== currentRunEls'. Removing ONLY that sub-clause still passes: with the shadow in place, owner.dissolved already reads the SCHEDULING run's array and catches this scenario on its own. So that clause is unfalsified belt-and-braces in this harness. It is not dead, it covers supersede WITHOUT a scroll, which the harness does not exercise.

FIX: either name the whole guard line as the mutation, or add a supersede-without-scroll case so the clause is falsified on its own. The exit-code contract at :31-40 is accurate and needs no change.

DONE-CRITERIA

- setTimeout shadow forwards trailing args, or a comment says why it does not need to.
- The harness docstring names a mutation that actually falsifies what it claims, or a case exists that falsifies owner !== currentRunEls alone.
- The oculist-eke three-way proof still holds: neutered mount FAILS, guard removed FAILS, unmutated PASSES.
close_reason: The setTimeout shadow now forwards trailing args via slice(arguments, 2) and fn.apply(void 0, extraArgs); this stays undefined, which is behaviourally identical to the previous bare fn() call, and the comment states the spec divergence rather than papering over it. setInterval left unshadowed with a comment, justified because fxScramble's ticker only writes textContent on pre-mounted spans and never calls mount(); mountRunEls declaration order left with a comment rather than a risky 250-line relocation. Item 2 achieved option (b), the harder one: the harness now runs a supersede-WITHOUT-scroll scenario, so owner !== currentRunEls is falsified on its own. Reviewer PASS with independent runs: removing that sub-clause alone leaves scenario 1 passing at 2 nodes and fails scenario 2 at 10 nodes with matchstrike leaked in. The oculist-eke three-way proof re-established: unmutated exit 0, mount() neutered fails both, whole guard removed fails both. Reviewer also probed the real in-page shadow rather than trusting the extracted copy, confirming setTimeout(fn, 10, 'A', 'B') delivers both args, and verified the check's hardcoded pre-fix literal is byte-identical to HEAD. The reported raw-state flake did not reproduce in 4 runs.

title: instant_scroll deadline still carries a 500ms guessed constant (FIRE_JITTER_MS)
description:
Noted by the oculist-3wq reviewer, 2026-09-08, who passed the bead anyway. Optional cleanup, only worth doing if 'no guessed constants' is meant to be an absolute bar.

WHERE IT STANDS. oculist-3wq replaced a 600ms margin against CDP round-trip overhead with a 500ms FIRE_JITTER_MS, and the reviewer ruled that legitimate rather than a re-smuggled sleep: the 600ms had to absorb four CDP round trips plus a waitForSelector and an inputValue read, all process-external and load-sensitive, whereas the 500ms absorbs one in-page setTimeout dispatch and one MutationObserver microtask hop. Measured consumption of that budget was 2.0 to 4.7ms under concurrency 4, under 1 percent. Same shape of constant, about 100x smaller thing to cover.

BUT IT IS STILL A NUMBER RATHER THAN A GUARANTEE.

THE STRUCTURAL ALTERNATIVE the reviewer identified: inside the setTimeout patch, arm a SIBLING timer at the same instant with the same stretched delay, and wait for its marker instead of for a numeric deadline. Same-delay timers fire FIFO, so the sibling firing proves the orphan's slot has passed, with no slack constant at all.

DONE-CRITERIA

- FIRE_JITTER_MS is gone, or a comment explains why the sibling-timer approach was rejected.
- The mutation check still fails 2 !== 1 with clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer() removed.
- Clean-path wall clock does not increase.
close_reason: FIRE_JITTER_MS, STRETCH_MS, armedAt and the whole deadline arithmetic are gone, replaced by a sibling timer armed synchronously right after the orphan with the same stretched delay, so FIFO ordering proves the orphan's slot has passed rather than a number covering it. The sibling signals through window.__ocSiblingFired, an isolated-world global, not a DOM mutation, which is what makes it also resolve oculist-jz0. Reviewer PASS with independent verification: falsifiability re-proven 2/2 as a real AssertionError 2 !== 1 rather than a timeout, content.js restored byte-identical, full suite 321 pass 0 fail. FIFO checked from the code (no await, no recompute, only an if between the two arms) and empirically, exactly one delay===50 intercept per run and it is always the orphan. Criterion 3 exceeded: per-test duration dropped from ~4850ms to ~4370ms, roughly 480ms faster, matching the analytic prediction. The sibling is not cancelled by clearActiveImmediateDrawTimer, so it is a clock anchored to the slot rather than an outcome signal, which is why the clean path cannot pass spuriously.

title: fxStamp's body shake keeps playing after its run has been scroll-dissolved
description:
Measured by the oculist-ak5 reviewer, 2026-09-06. A visible artifact, not a correctness bug: nothing is stranded and no geometry goes stale.

WHAT HAPPENS. Scroll mid-flight through fxStamp. The overlay dissolves as oculist-ucs intends, but the document.body shake still plays at t=170ms, after the overlay is already gone. The outer setTimeout that starts the shake is not cancelled by the dissolve.

WHY IT IS NOT THE ak5 BUG. ak5 asked whether these effects strand raw page state or anchor it to a stale position. This does neither: the shake is a pure translate() with no position-dependent origin, and its restorer fires unconditionally on the effect's own 130ms timer, so body transform always returns to none. It is purely that the effect keeps going after the user has been told, visually, that it stopped.

WHY IT IS P4. One brief shake on an effect the user already scrolled away from. Worth fixing only if 'dissolve means everything stops' is a property someone wants to hold literally.

FIX DIRECTION. If it is worth fixing, the dissolve would need to cancel the effect's own pending timers, not just its mounted nodes. That is a bigger change than it sounds and overlaps oculist-eke's territory (run identity for deferred work), so consider doing both together rather than separately.

DONE-CRITERIA

- Either the shake no longer starts once the run is dissolved, or a comment at fxStamp records that it deliberately does and why.
- The body transform still always reverts to none, scrolled or not.
- No change to fxStamp on the no-scroll path.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on the second review. Decision was to STOP the shake rather than document it, because oculist-eke had just made that a one-line reuse rather than a new mechanism. Re-measured first, as the bead's ground had shifted: post-eke the shake still started after a mid-flight dissolve (animCount 1, shaking t=183-296ms) even though the badge had already gone, because it is a raw document.body.animate() that never passes through mount(). The puffs WERE correctly refused, which confirmed eke's machinery works for mount()-gated nodes and that the gap was exactly the raw mutation. FIX: fxStamp's deferred callback now reads the owning run the same way mount() does, via the identity eke's setTimeout shadow already captures, and returns early if that run has been superseded or dissolved. Null-safe in the same shape as mount() at :227, so a future routing through the native setTimeout leaves the effect working rather than silently dead. VERIFIED: HEAD gives maxBodyAnims 1 with the body shaking t=105-220ms, the fix gives 0 with no non-none transform sample; the body transform still reverts to none with a null style attribute across 9 scenarios including three sidebar paths; the no-scroll path is identical to HEAD; and a re-fire 50ms apart correctly leaves exactly ONE shake, run 2's, where HEAD had two. Null-safety was instrumented rather than argued: mountRunEls was non-null at all 9 executions, and the fail-safe direction is suppression rather than a TypeError. FAILED THE FIRST REVIEW for shipping a behaviour change with ZERO regression coverage: deleting the guard left all three harnesses passing, the same defect shape that failed oculist-eke's first review on this file. Now covered by a mid-window assertion in the existing raw-state harness, and proven live on BOTH arms: deleting the guard fails the scrolled arm (midBodyAnimCount 1 at t=220ms), and making the shake never start at all fails the control arm. Two comments the fix had made false were corrected. THE SCOPE QUESTION the brief raised, whether guarding only fxStamp makes 'dissolved' mean two different things, was answered by the reviewer checking all six raw-state effects: fxZoompunch, fxLetterwave, fxScramble and fxShockwave mutate raw state SYNCHRONOUSLY at fire time, when nothing is dissolved yet, so a check there would be meaningless. fxDepthdive is the one genuine sibling, with a second body animation from a later setTimeout still live 250-900ms after a dissolve; filed as oculist-cst rather than scope-creeping this P4. Full suite 321/321. Cosmetic residue filed as oculist-p3e: the 220ms sample is a fixed instant with about 54ms of headroom on the tighter arm, two line references are off by one, and one comment names only the identity clause when it is the dissolved clause that fires on a scrolled run.

title: fxZoompunch/fxDepthdive/fxLetterwave/fxScramble leave a stray empty style="" attribute after restore (benign, not scroll-related)
description:
Measured while verifying oculist-ak5's six raw-state-mutating effects: after
restore() runs, fxZoompunch and fxDepthdive leave document.body with a
present-but-empty style="" attribute (via restoreStyleAttr's
removeAttribute('style') after document.body.animate()+cancel()), and
fxLetterwave/fxScramble leave #match with the same empty style="" (via
mark.style.color = '').

Identical whether the run is scrolled mid-flight or left alone -- not caused
by, or related to, oculist-uc1/ucs's scroll-dissolve mechanism. This is
standard CSSOM behavior: clearing the last inline style property does not
remove the attribute node, you need an explicit removeAttribute() call, and
these effects' cancel()/property-clear paths don't do that last step. It has
zero visual or functional effect (an empty style attribute applies nothing).

Reproduced deterministically with
artifacts/prototypes/raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js (see its bodyStyleAttr/
matchStyleAttr fields in the PASS rows).

Low priority: cosmetic DOM-diff only, no behavior change. If picked up, the
fix is likely to explicitly removeAttribute('style') in these four restore
paths when the attribute is now empty.
notes:
Reviewer findings from oculist-ak5, 2026-09-06, worth folding in before this is worked:

1. IT IS NOT ALWAYS PRESENT. For fxZoompunch and fxDepthdive the empty style attribute is NON-DETERMINISTIC, not a constant. An independent probe read bodyStyleAttr=null, a fully exact revert, where the shipped harness read empty string. The difference was whether getComputedStyle(document.body) had been called first. So the observer is partly causing what it reports; any fix here needs to establish what it is actually measuring before changing anything. For fxLetterwave and fxScramble it IS plain CSSOM (clearing the last property does not remove the attribute node), on code dating to 8acee250, well before uc1/ucs.

2. A PRE-EXISTING INACCURATE COMMENT BELONGS WITH THIS. effects-playground.html:1193-1198 claims that clearing the property 'avoids that quirk entirely'. That is contradicted by the measured matchStyleAttr of empty string. Correct it as part of this bead.

Confirmed benign and correctly P4: an empty style attribute applies nothing, and the behaviour is identical scrolled or not.
RUN STOPPED HERE 2026-09-08: this bead failed review TWICE, which is a /goal stop condition. The work IS committed on branch goal/playground-runidentity-followups but the bead is deliberately NOT closed, because the reviewer did not pass it.

WHAT IS DONE AND VERIFIED GOOD (do not redo):
- The code fix is correct and safe. restoreStyleAttr does a guarded second removeAttribute('style') when the attribute is confirmed present-and-empty, and fxLetterwave/fxScramble carry the same guard. An author's pre-existing inline style survives all four effects, scrolled and control; the guard is strictly narrower than the unconditional removeAttribute it follows. Restores are byte-equal across 4 effects x scrolled/control.
- MECHANISM ESTABLISHED, and it is TWO mechanisms, not one. Body path (zoompunch/depthdive): Chromium serializes .style writes into the attribute LAZILY, so removeAttribute on a not-yet-synchronized attribute detaches it and the pending sync then writes back style=''. Reading getAttribute('style') first forces synchronization, which is why the guard is deterministic and why probes perturb the measurement. Mark path (letterwave/scramble): plain CSSOM, mark.style.color = '' leaves the attribute present-but-empty, with no removeAttribute involved at all. Measured in an isolated page: clearProp gives '' with or without getComputedStyle; removeAttribute-after-.style-write gives '' then null on a second call; read-then-remove gives null directly.
- The bead's own NOTES hypothesis (a getComputedStyle ORDER effect) is WRONG. The earlier reviewer's null reading came from their probe reading the attribute first. Disregard that part of the NOTES.
- Round 1 failed for zero persisted coverage; that is fixed. attrOk in raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js is now attr === null, and it falsifies: reverting the playground fix makes the harness exit 1 naming the empty attribute on all four effects; restoring it exits 0 with every row null/null. Verified independently.

THE ONE OUTSTANDING DEFECT, which is why it is not closed:
raw-state-scroll-dissolve-check.js:51-61 attributes ALL FOUR effects' leftover to lazy attribute synchronization and explicitly denies the CSSOM cause, saying 'The cause is not a CSSOM-setter quirk' and that each guard is 'a SECOND removeAttribute call'. That is wrong for fxLetterwave/fxScramble: their leftover IS plain CSSOM, there is no prior removeAttribute, and their guard call is the FIRST one. It also contradicts the same change's own playground comment at effects-playground.html:1265-1270, which is correct.

THE FIX: split that NOTE paragraph into the two mechanisms actually measured. No code change, and no need to re-run the falsifiability proof.

ALSO WORTH A BEAD, from the same review: attrOk is fixture-coupled. measureOne snapshots before.bodyTransform/matchColor/articleHTML but NOT the before style attributes, so the assertion is hard-coded to null rather than compared to before. Adding an author inline style to the fixture's body would make zoompunch/depthdive fail spuriously despite byte-restoring correctly. Capture bodyStyleAttr/matchStyleAttr in before and assert equality.
close_reason: Final outstanding defect fixed: the raw-state harness NOTE now splits the empty-style-attribute cause into the two mechanisms actually measured (lazy attribute serialization on the body path, plain CSSOM on the mark path) instead of attributing all four effects to one. Reviewer PASS: comment-only diff, both mechanisms correctly attributed, no contradiction with effects-playground.html, retained null-assertion claim verified against attrOk. 321 tests pass.

title: Two untriaged loose ends from the suite-flake measurement
description:
